sentence: El lunes le pedí a mi hermana Ana que viniera a mi casa el martes para cenar; hoy es miércoles y ayer cenamos aquí.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb
grammar: Viniera expresses the visit requested on Monday for Tuesday. The imperfect subjunctive can refer to an action later than a past request; it does not itself establish whether that action happened.
register: Neutral family conversation.
note: Le pedí a mi hermana que = I asked my sister to; viniera = she come within that request. Wednesday's update explicitly confirms Tuesday's dinner.

sentence: El lunes le recomendé a Luis que estuviera en la sala el martes a las nueve para preparar la reunión de las diez; hoy es miércoles y él estuvo ahí ayer de ocho y media a once.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive locative verb
grammar: Estuviera locates Luis in the state recommended Monday for Tuesday morning. His actual presence is established by the separate estuvo clause.
register: Neutral meeting preparation.
note: Le recomendé que = I recommended that he; sala = room; de ocho y media a once = from eight thirty to eleven.

sentence: El lunes visité la biblioteca del barrio; era pública y cualquier vecino podía usarla. Me alegró que fuera un servicio para todos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive copular verb
grammar: Me alegró que selects subjunctive for an emotional evaluation of an established classification. The library's public character is explicitly accepted, rather than doubted.
register: Neutral account of a neighborhood visit.
note: Barrio = neighborhood; pública = public; cualquier vecino = any neighbor; me alegró que = I was glad that; servicio = service.

sentence: Ayer no creía que Ana tuviera una bicicleta; después me mostró la suya y la vi salir en ella.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive possession verb
grammar: No creía que introduces a possession the speaker did not previously believe Ana had. The later observation corrects that earlier stance.
register: Neutral personal conversation.
note: Me mostró la suya = she showed me hers, referring to her bicycle; la vi salir en ella = I saw her leave on it.

sentence: El viernes yo quería que mi papá pudiera abrir el frasco, pero la tapa estaba atorada; al final la aflojó con un trapo y lo abrió.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive modal verb
grammar: Quería que pudiera expresses a past wish for the father's practical ability. The stuck lid supplies the obstacle; the final opening establishes the outcome separately.
register: Everyday family narrative.
note: Frasco = jar; tapa = lid; atorada = stuck; aflojó = loosened; trapo = cloth. La refers to the lid and lo to the jar.

sentence: Ayer mi abuela me explicó el origen del nombre del barrio; me sorprendió que supiera ese dato, porque yo no lo sabía.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive factual-knowledge verb
grammar: Me sorprendió que evaluates knowledge demonstrated by the grandmother's explanation. Supiera does not deny her knowledge; no lo sabía separately describes the speaker's lack of it.
register: Neutral family conversation.
note: Origen = origin; barrio = neighborhood; dato = fact or piece of information; me sorprendió que = it surprised me that.

sentence: Ayer Marta, la encargada del teatro, le prohibió a Luis que hiciera ruido durante el ensayo de la tarde; él respetó la indicación y guardó silencio todo el ensayo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in a prohibition clause
grammar: Prohibió que places the prohibited action under a completed past prohibition. Luis is the potential noise-maker; Marta issues the prohibition. His compliance is explicitly reported.
register: Neutral theater-work narrative.
note: Encargada = woman in charge; hacer ruido = make noise; indicación = instruction here; guardó silencio = remained silent.

sentence: Antes de la fiesta del sábado, yo tenía miedo de que Ana le dijera a Luis que el regalo para Luis estaba en mi casa; Ana no le contó nada y Luis vio el regalo por primera vez durante la fiesta.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive disclosure verb
grammar: Tenía miedo de que presents Ana's possible disclosure as feared, rather than asserted. Luis is the intended recipient inside that feared event; the ending explicitly excludes the disclosure.
register: Neutral social narrative.
note: El regalo para Luis explicitly identifies the gift's intended recipient; no le contó nada = Ana told Luis nothing; por primera vez = for the first time.

sentence: El lunes yo quería que mi mamá me diera permiso para usar su carro el martes; ella aceptó esa noche y el martes lo usé para llevar a mi abuela al mercado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in dar permiso
grammar: Diera supplies the granting verb in dar permiso para. The mother owns the car and grants permission to the speaker; the speaker's later use is reported separately.
register: Everyday family coordination.
note: Me diera permiso = she grant me permission; aceptó = agreed; lo usé = I used it, referring to the mother's car.

sentence: El viernes Ana me sugirió que pusiera las sillas en círculo para la charla del sábado; el sábado las acomodé así y todos pudimos vernos de frente.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect subjunctive placement verb
grammar: Sugirió que introduces Ana's past suggestion about the speaker's later arrangement. Pusiera has the speaker as subject; the Saturday clause establishes that the arrangement was made.
register: Neutral preparation for a group conversation.
note: En círculo = in a circle; charla = talk or discussion; acomodé = arranged; de frente = facing one another here.

sentence: El jueves Ana propuso que ella y yo fuéramos al museo el sábado; acepté la invitación, pero el museo cerró ese día y no hicimos la visita.
part_of_speech: first-person plural imperfect subjunctive movement verb
grammar: Fuéramos refers to Ana and the speaker in the outing proposed Thursday for Saturday. Its written accent is required. The ending shows that accepting the invitation did not produce the visit.
register: Neutral social planning.
note: Propuso = proposed; museo = museum; acepté = I accepted. Fuéramos is ir here because al museo supplies a destination.

sentence: El lunes Marta propuso que Ana y yo pidiéramos prestado el salón del club para nuestra lectura del viernes; Ana y yo hicimos la solicitud el martes y el club nos autorizó a usarlo.
part_of_speech: first-person plural imperfect subjunctive requesting verb
grammar: Marta proposes the action; Ana and the speaker form the requesting group. Pidiéramos retains i in the stem and requires the written accent on é.
register: Neutral community reading-event preparation.
note: Pedir prestado = ask to borrow; salón = event room; solicitud = request here; autorizó = authorized; usarlo refers to using the room.

sentence: Ayer Elena leyó mi cuento completo y después me comentó el final; agradecí que lo leyera con tanta atención.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive reading verb
grammar: Agradecí que evaluates reading already established as completed. Leyera can express that earlier event within the appreciative evaluation; it does not make the reading hypothetical.
register: Neutral personal literary exchange.
note: Cuento = short story; comentó el final = commented on the ending; agradecí que = I appreciated that; con tanta atención = so attentively.

sentence: Ana y Luis, el lunes les pedí a ustedes que trajeran sus sillas a mi casa para la cena del martes; hoy es miércoles y las sillas siguen aquí desde que llegaron con ellas ayer.
part_of_speech: third-person plural imperfect subjunctive verb referring to ustedes
grammar: Trajeran refers to the explicitly addressed ustedes, Ana and Luis. They transport their chairs toward the speaker's home; the later arrival with the chairs confirms completion.
register: Familiar plural Mexican address.
note: Les and a ustedes identify Ana and Luis as the people asked; sus sillas means your chairs in this direct address. Desde que llegaron con ellas = since you arrived with the chairs. Ellas refers to the chairs.

sentence: En la carta del lunes le pedí a mi hermano que viniese a mi casa el viernes; él aceptó y cenamos juntos ese día.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in the -se form
grammar: Viniese is the -se imperfect-subjunctive variant in an ordinary induced past request. Both -ra and -se forms are valid in written American Spanish; neither belongs exclusively to one region.
register: A written family request recounted in neutral Spanish.
note: Carta = letter; ese día refers to Friday. The brother's acceptance and shared dinner establish the outcome separately from the written request.

sentence: En su mensaje del lunes, Marta nos pidió a Ana y a mí que dijésemos «gracias por prestarnos el salón» a los vecinos al iniciar la reunión del viernes; ese día les dimos las gracias con esas palabras.
part_of_speech: first-person plural imperfect subjunctive verb in the -se form
grammar: Dijésemos is the first-person plural -se form of decir and requires the accent on é. Marta requests wording to be delivered by Ana and the speaker to the neighbors.
register: Written community-event coordination.
note: Prestarnos el salón = lending us the room; al iniciar = at the start of. The quoted thanks acknowledge the neighbors' loan.

sentence: No tengo dinero para comprar los materiales del taller; ojalá tuviera cien pesos ahora para empezar hoy.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect subjunctive possession verb
grammar: Ojalá tuviera expresses a current wish for money the speaker explicitly lacks now. The imperfect-subjunctive form does not place this wish in past time.
register: Everyday expression of a practical wish.
note: Ojalá = I wish or if only here; materiales del taller = workshop materials; ahora and hoy anchor the wish in the present.

sentence: Sé que el ensayo empieza hoy a las seis, pero no sé en qué salón; ojalá supiera dónde es para ir directamente.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect subjunctive factual-knowledge verb
grammar: Ojalá supiera expresses a present wish for missing location information. The speaker knows today's time but does not know the room; neither the wish nor its missing knowledge is located in the past.
register: Neutral preparation for a rehearsal.
note: Ensayo = rehearsal; salón = room; dónde es asks where the event takes place; directamente = directly.

sentence: —Buenas tardes, soy la encargada de la taquilla del teatro. —Quisiera comprar dos boletos para la función de esta noche, por favor.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect subjunctive modal verb expressing a courteous present request
grammar: Quisiera softens the customer's present request and takes comprar directly. This conditional-like modal use does not describe a past desire or license automatic replacement by quisiese.
register: Courteous service request.
note: Taquilla = box office; encargada = woman in charge; función = theater performance. The employee identifies her service role before the customer requests tickets.

sentence: La masa del pan no crece; pudiera ser que la cocina esté demasiado fría, pero aún no he medido la temperatura.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive modal verb in a tentative explanation
grammar: Pudiera ser que tentatively proposes a current explanation and introduces esté. Pudiera expresses possibility here, not permission or a past ability; the corresponding -se form is not an automatic substitute in this modal use.
register: Tentative household explanation.
note: Masa = dough; no crece = is not rising here; demasiado fría = too cold; aún no he medido = I have not measured yet.

sentence: Ayer a las cinco, mientras Ana seguía en el camión, acordamos empezar la cena cuando ella llegara a mi casa; llegó a las seis y cenamos después.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in a prospective temporal clause
grammar: Cuando llegara supplies the still-pending arrival viewed from yesterday's five-o'clock agreement. The separate llegó clause confirms that the arrival later occurred at six.
register: Neutral meal coordination.
note: Acordamos empezar = we agreed to start; seguía en el camión = was still on the bus. Llegara is prospective from the earlier agreement.

sentence: Ayer decidí no salir de casa hasta que mi hijo terminara su tarea; acabó a las cinco y salimos juntos a las cinco y diez.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in a prospective endpoint clause
grammar: Decidí no salir presents the child's completion as still pending when the speaker made the decision. Hasta que terminara supplies that prospective endpoint. Acabó separately confirms actual completion; the subjunctive does not deny that it happened.
register: Neutral family narrative.
note: Decidí no salir = I decided not to leave; acabó = he finished his homework; salimos juntos = we left together. The five-ten departure follows the stated five-o'clock completion.

sentence: Ayer le di a Ana su suéter a las siete y media, antes de que ella saliera de casa; se fue a las ocho.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in a temporal clause
grammar: Antes de que selects subjunctive saliera in this past sequence. The speaker hands over the sweater at seven thirty; Ana's actual departure is established at eight.
register: Everyday personal narrative.
note: Suéter = sweater; se fue = she left, referring to Ana. The handover and departure have different actors.

sentence: Ayer Ana y yo llevamos las cajas al cuarto sin que Luis entrara; él se quedó afuera durante toda la mudanza.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb after sin que
grammar: Sin que entrara excludes Luis's entry from the completed moving activity. Ana and the speaker carry the boxes; Luis remains outside and does not enter.
register: Neutral household narrative.
note: Cuarto = room; afuera = outside; durante toda la mudanza = throughout the move. Él refers to Luis.

sentence: Ayer moví la lámpara para que mi abuela viera las letras del libro; aun con más luz, ella no pudo distinguirlas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive visual-perception verb in a purpose clause
grammar: Para que viera states the intended result of the speaker's action. The grandmother is the intended perceiver; her later inability explicitly shows that the purpose was not achieved.
register: Everyday family account.
note: Moví la lámpara = I moved the lamp; letras = letters; aun con más luz = even with more light; distinguirlas = make them out, referring to the letters.

sentence: El mes pasado buscaba a alguien que trabajara por las tardes en mi panadería; no encontré ayuda y todavía no sé si había alguna persona disponible.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in a search-criterion relative clause
grammar: Que trabajara describes the afternoon work sought from an unidentified person. The failed search does not establish that no suitable person existed.
register: Neutral small-business account.
note: Panadería = bakery; alguien = someone; alguna persona disponible = a person available to help. The speaker explicitly leaves past availability unresolved.

sentence: El lunes buscábamos dos salas que estuvieran cerca una de otra para los talleres del sábado; el martes encontramos dos contiguas y las reservamos.
part_of_speech: third-person plural imperfect subjunctive locative verb in a search-criterion relative clause
grammar: Estuvieran agrees with dos salas and specifies their desired relative location during Monday's search. Tuesday's successful discovery does not invalidate the earlier criterion-framing subjunctive.
register: Neutral workshop planning.
note: Cerca una de otra = near one another; contiguas = adjacent; las reservamos = we reserved them, referring to the two rooms.

sentence: El lunes Elena todavía tenía miedo de hablar frente al grupo; yo esperaba que se atreviera a pedir una explicación durante la clase del martes, y ese día levantó la mano y preguntó.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb with visible lexical-pronominal se
grammar: Esperaba que introduces the speaker's past hope about Elena's later action. Visible se belongs to atreverse, whose action complement is introduced by a: atreverse a pedir.
register: Neutral classroom narrative.
note: Atreverse a hacer algo = dare to do something; frente al grupo = in front of the group; levantó la mano = raised her hand.

sentence: Hoy la autora aclaró que el libro es ficción; ¡no pensaba que fuera una historia inventada, pero ahora sé que lo es!
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive copular verb under a surprised negative expectation
grammar: No pensaba que fuera expresses the expectation now being corrected. The author's clarification and ahora sé que lo es establish the classification; the subjunctive does not preserve permanent uncertainty.
register: Surprised contemporary literary conversation.
note: Autora = female author; ficción = fiction; historia inventada = invented story; lo es = it is, with lo replacing the classification.

sentence: Yo sabía que el departamento tenía poco espacio; aunque tuviera esa limitación, lo renté el mes pasado porque quedaba cerca de mi trabajo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in a factual concessive clause
grammar: Aunque tuviera backgrounds a drawback explicitly acknowledged by sabía que. The subjunctive does not make the limited space unreal; renting proceeds despite it.
register: Neutral explanation of a housing decision.
note: Departamento = apartment; limitación = limitation; lo renté = I rented it; quedaba cerca = was located nearby.

sentence: El jueves acordamos comer juntos el sábado aunque lloviera: con lluvia usaríamos la sala y, con tiempo seco, el patio; no sabíamos qué tiempo haría.
part_of_speech: impersonal singular imperfect subjunctive weather verb in a hypothetical concessive clause
grammar: Aunque lloviera makes possible Saturday rain irrelevant to Thursday's meal commitment. The alternatives specify arrangements for either weather outcome; the sentence does not report actual rain.
register: Neutral social planning.
note: Con lluvia = in rainy weather; con tiempo seco = in dry weather; usaríamos = we would use; qué tiempo haría = what the weather would be like.

sentence: La semana pasada mi hijo viajaba solo; yo tenía miedo de que le pasara algo y le escribía cada noche para saber cómo estaba. El domingo volvió y me dijo: «Todo salió bien».
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive occurrence verb
grammar: Tenía miedo de que le pasara algo presents a feared possible incident. Le identifies the son as affected person; the nightly contact is a precaution, and the favorable outcome is attributed to his later report.
register: Neutral family narrative.
note: Viajaba solo = was traveling alone; le escribía = I wrote to him; volvió = returned; todo salió bien = everything went well.

sentence: Ayer, antes de conocer al nuevo vecino, decidí ayudarlo con sus cajas, fuera quien fuera; lo ayudé sin preguntarle su nombre.
part_of_speech: singular personal relative pronoun in an indefinite concessive construction
grammar: Quien is unaccented in fuera quien fuera. The two visible fuera forms frame the neighbor's identity as irrelevant to the speaker's prior decision to help.
register: Neutral personal narrative.
note: Fuera quien fuera = whoever he was. The repeated fuera forms belong to the concessive pattern; the blank retrieves its person-relative component.

sentence: Ayer dudaba que hubiera sillas para los quince invitados; al llegar conté veinte, así que había suficientes.
part_of_speech: impersonal singular imperfect subjunctive existential verb
grammar: Existential hubiera stays singular before plural sillas. It introduces the availability doubted earlier; no participle follows, so it is not an auxiliary forming a compound tense.
register: Neutral social-event preparation.
note: Dudaba que = I doubted that; invitados = guests; conté veinte = I counted twenty; suficientes = enough, referring to chairs.

sentence: Ayer, durante la función, temí que el niño sentado delante de mí fuera a caerse de la silla porque se inclinaba mucho; su mamá lo sostuvo y no cayó.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive prospective auxiliary followed by a
grammar: Fuera a combines prospective ir with a before caerse. It presents the fall as later than the speaker's past fear; it is not ser classifying the child. The ending explicitly excludes a fall.
register: Neutral account of a theater visit.
note: Temí = I feared; delante de mí = in front of me; caerse = fall; se inclinaba = was leaning; lo sostuvo = held him.

sentence: El lunes le ofrecí ayuda a Ana para su mudanza del martes en caso de que necesitara otra persona para cargar las cajas; al final trabajó con su hermano y no me llamó.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in a contingency clause
grammar: En caso de que necesitara makes Ana's need for another helper the trigger for Monday's offer concerning Tuesday. The offer does not itself assert that she needed the speaker's help.
register: Neutral friendly offer.
note: Le ofrecí ayuda a Ana = I offered Ana help; en caso de que = in case; cargar las cajas = carry the boxes. Ana later works with her brother.

sentence: El lunes Ana y yo buscábamos una hora que nos conviniera para ensayar: ella podía a las seis o a las siete, yo solo a las siete, y elegimos las siete.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive suitability verb with an experiencer dative
grammar: Una hora is the subject represented by que; nos identifies Ana and the speaker as the people whose schedules must be served. Conviniera specifies the mutually suitable time being sought.
register: Neutral rehearsal scheduling.
note: Convenirle una hora a alguien = a time suit someone; ensayar = rehearse; elegimos = we chose. Their stated availability makes seven the shared option.

sentence: Don Raúl, usted dice que a diario busca las llaves por toda la casa; quizá debiera guardarlas siempre en el mismo cajón, si le parece buena idea.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive modal verb giving tentative present advice to usted
grammar: Debiera offers current advice about a recurring problem rather than describing a past obligation. Quizá and si le parece buena idea leave room for the addressee's judgment. This conditional-like modal use does not establish general -se interchangeability.
register: Respectful, tentative advice.
note: A diario = daily; guardarlas = put the keys away here; cajón = drawer; si le parece buena idea = if that seems a good idea to you.

sentence: —Buenos días, soy el recepcionista del taller. —Tengo cita hoy a las cuatro; quisiera que usted me confirmara la hora, por favor.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb referring to usted in a courteous present request
grammar: Current courteous quisiera que introduces confirmara. The person holding the appointment makes the request; usted identifies the receptionist as the person asked to confirm today's appointment time. The imperfect subjunctive does not make the request past.
register: Courteous service inquiry with usted.
note: Recepcionista = receptionist; taller = workshop; confirmar la hora = verify the appointment time. The appointment already exists for today.

sentence: Ana, me gustaría que tu mamá viniera a comer a mi casa el próximo domingo para conocerla; todavía no la he invitado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb after a present conditional wish
grammar: Me gustaría que expresses a present wish about the mother's future visit. Viniera refers to Ana's mother, not Ana; the unissued invitation leaves fulfillment open.
register: Courteous, familiar social planning.
note: El próximo domingo = next Sunday; conocerla = meet her, referring to Ana's mother; no la he invitado = I have not invited her.

sentence: Ahora no tengo dinero para comprar una bicicleta; si tuviera mil pesos, compraría una usada para ir al trabajo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect subjunctive possession verb in a counterfactual condition
grammar: Si tuviera imagines a resource absent now. Compraría expresses the consequence of that imagined possession; neither clause reports an actual purchase.
register: Neutral personal planning.
note: Usada = used; compraría = I would buy. The condition concerns present resources, despite the imperfect-subjunctive form.

sentence: Mi turno casi seguro terminará tarde el domingo, aunque el horario no es definitivo; si pudiera salir a las seis, iría al concierto contigo, Ana.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect subjunctive modal verb in a potential future condition
grammar: Si pudiera presents an unlikely future opportunity. The unfinished schedule leaves that opportunity open; the sentence does not declare early departure impossible.
register: Familiar social planning.
note: Turno = work shift; horario definitivo = final schedule; iría = I would go; concierto = concert. Contigo addresses Ana.

sentence: Luis, tú necesitas descansar después de esta semana de trabajo; si yo fuera tú, pediría un día libre.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect subjunctive copular verb in a perspective-taking advice construction
grammar: Si yo fuera tú places the adviser imaginatively in Luis's position. Pediría recommends an action for Luis, whose need for rest is explicit.
register: Familiar advice to Luis.
note: Pediría un día libre = I would ask for a day off. Yo is the adviser; tú refers to Luis.

sentence: Ana, yo estoy en Puebla y tú estás cargando cajas en tu casa de Toluca; si estuviera ahí contigo, te ayudaría ahora.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect subjunctive locative verb in a present counterfactual condition
grammar: Estuviera imagines the speaker at Ana's location now. The actual separation blocks the simultaneous help expressed by te ayudaría ahora.
register: Familiar household coordination.
note: Ahí contigo = there with you, at Ana's home in Toluca; te ayudaría = I would help you; cargando cajas = carrying boxes.

sentence: No sé el número de teléfono de Rosa; si lo supiera, la llamaría ahora para confirmar la cena.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect subjunctive factual-knowledge verb in a counterfactual condition
grammar: Si lo supiera imagines possessing the telephone number missing now. That knowledge would enable the immediate call; lo represents the number and la represents Rosa.
register: Neutral social coordination.
note: Llamaría = I would call; confirmar la cena = confirm the dinner arrangement. The missing information is Rosa's telephone number.

sentence: Ana, el viaje desde tu ciudad es largo y casi seguro no vendrás el domingo; si vinieras a mi casa ese día, te prepararía la comida.
part_of_speech: second-person singular imperfect subjunctive motion verb in a potential future condition
grammar: Si vinieras addresses Ana as tú and entertains an unlikely Sunday visit. The meal offer depends on that visit; attendance is not asserted.
register: Familiar invitation addressed to Ana.
note: Vendrás = you will come; casi seguro no = almost certainly not, leaving a possibility open; te prepararía la comida = I would prepare the main meal for you.

sentence: Ahora no puedo elegir mi turno; si pudiera hacerlo, cambiaría mi horario para recoger yo a mi hija a las cinco.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative transitive verb expressing a hypothetical result
grammar: Cambiaría gives the speaker's practical action under the unreal present condition si pudiera hacerlo. It is a consequence of imagined choice, rather than a bare recommendation.
register: Neutral explanation of family and work needs.
note: Elegir mi turno = choose my work shift; hacerlo refers to choosing it; recoger a mi hija = pick up my daughter. Yo emphasizes who would perform the pickup.

sentence: Estudio en casa cada tarde porque la biblioteca está cerrada; si la biblioteca siguiera así el próximo mes, yo seguiría estudiando aquí durante las reparaciones.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative continuation auxiliary governing a gerund
grammar: Seguiría estudiando projects continuation of an established activity under a hypothetical condition next month. It does not present studying as a completed result.
register: Neutral study planning.
note: Siguiera así = remained that way, referring to the library's closure; aquí refers to the speaker's home; reparaciones = repairs.

sentence: Hoy llueve y el patio no tiene techo; si estuviera cubierto, comer ahí sería más agradable que comer en la sala ruidosa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular conditional indicative copular verb in a counterfactual comparison
grammar: Sería evaluates eating in the patio under the unreal premise that it is covered. Eating in the noisy indoor room is the explicit comparison benchmark.
register: Neutral discussion of where to eat.
note: Techo = roof; cubierto = covered; agradable = pleasant; sala ruidosa = noisy indoor room. Ahí refers to the patio.

sentence: Solo aceptaría coordinar la exposición si el museo cubriera el transporte de mis cuadros; ese pago es una condición indispensable y todavía no lo han ofrecido.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative verb governing an infinitive in a conditional commitment
grammar: Solo aceptaría binds the speaker's undertaking to the museum's required concession. Aceptar governs coordinar; the sentence makes no unconditional promise.
register: Neutral negotiation of a cultural responsibility.
note: Coordinar la exposición = coordinate the exhibition; cuadros = paintings; cubriera el transporte = paid the transport costs; indispensable = essential.

sentence: Ayer no leí el aviso y llegué cuando la biblioteca ya estaba cerrada; si lo hubiera leído por la mañana, habría ido antes.
part_of_speech: first-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary before a visible participle
grammar: Hubiera leído forms the past counterfactual condition: the speaker did not read the notice. Habría ido antes gives the different unreal past result. Hubiera is auxiliary here, rather than existential.
register: Neutral account of a missed library visit.
note: Lo refers to el aviso; leído = read; habría ido antes = I would have gone earlier. The reading would have preceded the visit.

sentence: Ana y yo no reservamos mesa ayer y nos quedamos sin lugar; si hubiéramos reservado por la mañana, habríamos cenado en ese restaurante anoche.
part_of_speech: first-person plural conditional-perfect auxiliary before a visible participle
grammar: Habríamos cenado expresses the unreal joint past result for Ana and the speaker. The unmade reservation is the prior condition; the actual failure to obtain a place is explicit.
register: Neutral social narrative.
note: Hubiéramos reservado = we had reserved in the counterfactual condition; cenado = had dinner; nos quedamos sin lugar = we were left without a place.

sentence: Ayer empujé la mesa y rompí el florero; si no hubiera empujado la mesa, el florero habría seguido intacto.
part_of_speech: negation followed by a first-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary
grammar: No hubiera negates the auxiliary construction before empujado. The condition imagines preventing an actual positive action and thereby avoiding the vase's breakage.
register: Neutral acknowledgment of a household mishap.
note: Empujar = push; florero = vase; intacto = intact; habría seguido intacto = would have remained intact. The speaker actually pushed the table.

sentence: Cuando llegué ayer a casa de mis primos, las tazas todavía estaban tibias; ellos habrían tomado café poco antes, supongo, pero nadie me lo confirmó.
part_of_speech: third-person plural conditional-perfect auxiliary expressing conjecture about an anterior past event
grammar: Habrían tomado conjectures about coffee drinking before yesterday's arrival. Warm cups provide indirect evidence; supongo and the absent confirmation preserve uncertainty. There is no counterfactual condition.
register: Neutral personal inference.
note: Primos = cousins; tazas tibias = warm cups; poco antes = shortly before; supongo = I suppose; lo refers to the inferred coffee drinking.

sentence: En una carta expliqué: «Recibí el domingo la invitación para la cena del sábado y no fui; si la hubiese recibido antes del viernes, habría asistido».
part_of_speech: first-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in the -se form
grammar: Hubiese recibido uses the accepted -se auxiliary in a written counterfactual condition. The imagined receipt before Friday precedes the missed Saturday dinner; actual receipt occurs Sunday.
register: Neutral written personal explanation.
note: La refers to the invitation; hubiese recibido = I had received in the unreal condition; habría asistido = I would have attended. The -se form is not exclusive to one region.

sentence: Ana, ayer llegaste a comer sin avisarme y solo tenía arroz; si me hubieses avisado por la mañana, yo hubiera preparado tu sopa favorita.
part_of_speech: first-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary expressing an independent unreal past result
grammar: Hubiera preparado is the result clause, rather than the condition selected by si. It can alternate here with habría preparado. The condition uses hubieses avisado and assigns the advance notice to Ana.
register: Familiar explanation to a guest.
note: Hubieses avisado = you had let me know in the unreal condition; preparado = prepared; tu sopa favorita = your favorite soup. Ana would have benefited from the preparation.

sentence: Gasté mis ahorros en el viaje del mes pasado y ahora no me alcanza para la renta; si no los hubiera gastado, tendría dinero para pagar hoy.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative possession verb expressing a present result of an unreal past condition
grammar: Tendría dinero concerns resources today. The condition reverses last month's actual spending, linking an unreal past action to its continuing present consequence.
register: Neutral explanation of personal finances.
note: Ahorros = savings; no me alcanza = I do not have enough here; renta = rent; los refers to the savings.

sentence: No sé coser y ayer tampoco sabía; si supiera coser, habría remendado mi camisa ayer en vez de pagar el arreglo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional-perfect auxiliary expressing a past result of an unreal persistent skill condition
grammar: Habría remendado locates the imagined repair yesterday. Si supiera describes a skill the speaker lacks both now and yesterday, so its scope includes the time needed for the unreal past result.
register: Neutral household explanation.
note: Coser = sew; remendado = mended; arreglo = clothing repair here; en vez de = instead of. The missing skill explicitly persists across both reference times.

sentence: No me inscribí en la carrera de ayer; si hubiera participado, podría haber ganado una medalla, aunque no era seguro.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional modal followed by the perfect-infinitive auxiliary
grammar: Podría haber ganado expresses an unreal past possibility. The speaker did not enter the race, and no era seguro prevents interpreting the imagined medal as a guaranteed achievement.
register: Neutral reflection on a recreational event.
note: Inscribirse en = enter or register for; carrera = race; medalla = medal. Haber plus visible ganado forms the perfect infinitive governed by podría.

sentence: Ayer Ana me ofreció el salón para ensayar, pero no acepté y no ensayé; si hubiera aceptado, habría podido practicar ahí, sin obligación de hacerlo.
meaning: I would have been able to
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional-perfect modal verb governing a visible infinitive
grammar: Habría podido practicar describes an opportunity that acceptance would have provided, without guaranteeing that the speaker would use it. No ensayé explicitly establishes actual nonperformance; sin obligación de hacerlo separately denies an obligation.
register: Neutral discussion of a rehearsal opportunity.
note: Salón = room; ensayar = rehearse; practicar = practice; ahí refers to the room Ana offered; hacerlo refers to practicing.

sentence: En mi explicación escribí: «De haber revisado yo las medidas antes de comprar la mesa, habría elegido una más pequeña; no las revisé y la que compré no pasó por la puerta».
part_of_speech: conditional preposition followed by a perfect-infinitive auxiliary
grammar: De haber revisado supplies a formal past counterfactual condition. Explicit yo identifies the person who would have checked the measurements and chosen the table. No las revisé establishes the actual omitted check separately from the table's failure to fit.
register: Careful written explanation.
note: Medidas = measurements; revisado = checked; habría elegido = I would have chosen; no pasó por la puerta = did not fit through the doorway.

sentence: Todavía no conocemos las medidas del patio; de ser un espacio adecuado para veinte personas, propondríamos hacer ahí la lectura de poesía.
part_of_speech: conditional preposition followed by an infinitival copular verb
grammar: De ser introduces a hypothetical classification of the patio as suitable space. Its nominal predicate remains visible. This conditional use does not make every de plus infinitive construction conditional.
register: Careful cultural-event proposal.
note: Medidas = measurements; espacio adecuado = suitable space; propondríamos = we would propose; lectura de poesía = poetry reading; ahí refers to the patio.

sentence: Mi hermana me prestó su carro y así pude llevar las cajas; sin ese préstamo, me habría sido imposible hacer la mudanza ayer.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing a counterfactual condition of absent means
grammar: Sin ese préstamo imagines removal of an actual enabling resource. The main clause explicitly makes yesterday's move impossible under that alternate condition.
register: Neutral acknowledgment of family assistance.
note: Préstamo = loan, here temporary use of the car; me habría sido imposible = it would have been impossible for me; mudanza = household move.

sentence: La cena la organizamos mis hermanos y yo; si por mí fuera, invitaríamos también a nuestros primos, pero necesito el acuerdo de mis hermanos.
part_of_speech: preposition followed by a tonic first-person singular pronoun in a hypothetical decision-authority frame
grammar: Si por mí fuera imagines the speaker holding sole decision authority. The preference to invite the cousins remains visible, and the required sibling agreement establishes the actual constraint.
register: Neutral family planning.
note: Si por mí fuera = if it were up to me; invitaríamos = we would invite; primos = cousins. Mí takes an accent as a tonic personal pronoun.

sentence: Mañana no cancelaremos el paseo a no ser que cierre el parque; esa es la única excepción que hemos acordado.
part_of_speech: exceptive conditional subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: A no ser que introduces the only agreed exception to not cancelling. Present subjunctive cierre names the possible park closure; the expression does not assert that it will occur.
register: Neutral shared outing plan.
note: Cancelaremos = we will cancel; paseo = outing or walk; cierre el parque = the park closes; única excepción = only exception.

sentence: Ayer a las ocho encontré vacío el salón del ensayo de las siete; supuse que lo habían cancelado, salvo que el grupo hubiera terminado antes de las ocho, cosa que no pude confirmar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in a possible earlier exception
grammar: Hubiera terminado presents an unconfirmed completion before the eight o'clock observation as an exception to the cancellation inference. The target is the anterior compound auxiliary, rather than the already familiar salvo que.
register: Neutral reconstruction of an uncertain event.
note: Vacío = empty; supuse = I assumed; lo refers to the rehearsal; habían cancelado = they had cancelled; cosa que no pude confirmar refers to the possible early finish.

sentence: Ayer le di permiso a mi hijo para ensayar en mi sala siempre que respetara el límite de las diez de la noche; terminó de ensayar a las nueve y media y apagó la música.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive transitive verb in a past permission proviso
grammar: Respetara states the boundary imposed when the parent granted permission. The son's explicitly reported completion before ten establishes compliance separately; siempre que is conditional here, rather than habitual whenever.
register: Neutral household permission.
note: Límite de las diez = ten o'clock cutoff; terminó de ensayar = finished rehearsing; apagó la música = switched off the music; nueve y media = nine thirty.

sentence: El lunes acepté preparar toda la cena del martes con tal de que mi hermana cediera en lo del postre: ella quería pastel y yo, flan; el martes comimos flan y yo hice la cena.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb with a figurative concession meaning
grammar: Cediera names the sister's required concession within Monday's agreement about Tuesday. The speaker undertakes all the cooking in exchange; Tuesday's outcome confirms both sides separately.
register: Familiar family negotiation.
note: Ceder en lo del postre = give in on the dessert issue; pastel = cake; flan = caramel custard. The sister's original preference was cake.

sentence: Mi vecina Ana está cuidando a mi hijo esta tarde; si no fuera por su ayuda, yo no podría pintar ahora.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive copular verb followed by a preposition in a dependency construction
grammar: Si no fuera por su ayuda removes Ana's actual childcare from the imagined situation. The speaker's present ability to paint depends on that assistance.
register: Neutral acknowledgment of a neighbor's help.
note: Si no fuera por = if it were not for; cuidar a mi hijo = look after my son; pintar = paint. Ana supplies help; the speaker benefits.

sentence: Ayer Clara me ayudó a trasladar las cajas y terminé en una tarde; de no haber recibido yo su ayuda, habría necesitado dos días.
part_of_speech: conditional preposition followed by negation and a perfect-infinitive auxiliary
grammar: De no haber recibido negates the perfect-infinitive condition. Explicit yo identifies the receiver of Clara's actual prior help and the person who would otherwise have needed two days.
register: Formal explanatory account.
note: Trasladar las cajas = move the boxes to another place; recibido = received; habría necesitado = I would have needed. Actual completion takes one afternoon.

sentence: El lunes Ana y yo acordamos que llamaríamos a Luis en caso de que la mudanza del martes se complicara; todavía no sabíamos si haría falta su ayuda.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb with visible pronominal se
grammar: Complicara presents a possible worsening of Tuesday's move from Monday's planning viewpoint. Visible se belongs to complicarse; the contingency is not asserted as an actual problem.
register: Neutral contingency planning.
note: Complicarse = become more difficult or complicated; llamaríamos = we would call; haría falta su ayuda = his help would be needed.

sentence: La apertura del taller de cerámica está supeditada a reunir diez participantes; la encargada solo tiene ocho inscritos y no abrirá el grupo hasta llegar a diez.
part_of_speech: feminine singular participle in a predicate with a governed a complement
grammar: Supeditada agrees with feminine apertura and retains a before reunir. Opening the class is made conditional on the explicit ten-person prerequisite, which is not yet met.
register: Careful explanation of a cultural workshop.
note: Estar supeditado a = be conditional on; apertura = opening; cerámica = pottery; encargada = woman in charge; inscritos = registered participants.

sentence: Ana, yo prepararé la comida del domingo para los ocho invitados siempre y cuando tú traigas las tortillas; esa es mi única condición y no te pediré nada más.
part_of_speech: emphatic conditional subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: Siempre y cuando emphatically limits the speaker's meal commitment. Tú names Ana as the actor of present-subjunctive traigas; the sentence explicitly makes that contribution the sole condition.
register: Familiar, explicit social agreement.
note: Prepararé = I will prepare; invitados = guests; traigas = you bring; única condición = only condition. The promise remains conditional on Ana's contribution.

sentence: Si hubiera que cambiar de camión el sábado, Ana y yo saldríamos media hora antes; todavía no sabemos si el servicio será directo.
part_of_speech: impersonal singular imperfect subjunctive obligation auxiliary followed by que
grammar: Hubiera que introduces possible necessity before the visible infinitive cambiar. It remains impersonal singular even though Ana and the speaker would perform the journey and leave earlier.
register: Neutral travel contingency.
note: Cambiar de camión = change buses; saldríamos = we would leave; media hora antes = half an hour earlier; servicio directo = service requiring no vehicle change.

sentence: El taller cuesta mil pesos y yo solo tengo quinientos; si requiriera una inversión de quinientos pesos, me inscribiría sin pedir dinero prestado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive transitive verb
grammar: Requiriera names the resource prerequisite through its noun object una inversión de quinientos pesos. The imagined lower requirement contrasts with the actual thousand-peso cost and the speaker's five-hundred-peso limit.
register: Neutral personal learning decision.
note: Requerir = require or need as a prerequisite; inversión = financial outlay here; quinientos = five hundred; me inscribiría = I would register.

sentence: Esta tarde no tengo un solo minuto libre; si tuviera siquiera cinco, llamaría a mi abuela para saludarla.
part_of_speech: focus adverb marking a minimal desired amount
grammar: Siquiera presents five minutes as a modest sufficient opening within an unreal condition. The actual lack of even one free minute establishes that this minimum is unmet.
register: Neutral personal wish expressed as a condition.
note: Cinco replaces cinco minutos; llamaría = I would call; saludarla = greet her, referring to the grandmother. Siquiera's interpretation follows this minimal-condition context.

sentence: Ahora solo tenemos media hora para ensayar; si tuviéramos dos horas, podríamos preparar cuando menos tres escenas, quizá cuatro, pero no prometería terminar la obra.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution expressing a lower quantitative bound
grammar: Cuando menos sets three scenes as the proposed lower bound under an unreal two-hour allocation. Quizá cuatro allows a higher number, while the final clause withholds a promise to finish the whole play.
register: Neutral rehearsal planning.
note: Tuviéramos = we had in the unreal condition; escenas = scenes; obra = play here; prometería = I would promise. The quantity is a conditional planning estimate.

sentence: Ayer pude asistir a la función porque mi hermana me prestó los cien pesos que me faltaban para la entrada; de otro modo, me habría quedado afuera.
part_of_speech: adverbial connective introducing a counterfactual consequence
grammar: De otro modo recovers the alternative without the sister's actual loan. Me habría quedado afuera expresses the unreal consequence of that missing enabling condition.
register: Neutral acknowledgment of family help.
note: Función = theater performance; entrada = admission ticket; me faltaban = I was short of; me habría quedado afuera = I would have remained outside.

sentence: Ya decidí no atribuir ese poema a Elena; reconsideraría mi decisión si encontráramos un manuscrito del poema firmado por ella, pero hasta ahora no tenemos ninguno.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative transitive verb
grammar: Reconsideraría means revisiting a decision already made, rather than considering the issue for the first time. The conditional makes that reassessment depend on new evidence that is currently absent.
register: Careful literary discussion.
note: Atribuir un poema a alguien = credit someone with a poem; manuscrito = manuscript; firmado por ella = signed by Elena; encontráramos = we found in the hypothetical condition.

sentence: Aun si el teatro bajara el precio para la función de mañana, yo no asistiría porque esa noche debo cuidar a mi hijo; pagar menos no cambiaría mi decisión.
part_of_speech: concessive conditional conjunctive sequence
grammar: Aun si introduces a hypothetical price reduction that would not reverse the refusal. It does not make cheaper admission a sufficient or necessary condition for attendance. Aun is unaccented in this concessive use.
register: Neutral response to a possible social alternative.
note: Bajara el precio = lowered the price; asistiría = I would attend; cuidar a mi hijo = look after my son. The childcare obligation, rather than the ticket price, supports the decision.

sentence: No es que no quiera acompañarte al concierto, Ana; sí quiero ir contigo, pero hoy debo cuidar a mi hijo y no tengo quién lo cuide.
part_of_speech: discourse construction introducing a rejected explanation
grammar: No es que rejects unwillingness as the explanation and introduces subjunctive quiera. The actual reason is the speaker's childcare responsibility; this construction does not universally establish that every embedded proposition is false.
register: Familiar explanation addressed to Ana.
note: Acompañarte = accompany you; concierto = concert; contigo = with you, referring to Ana; no tengo quién lo cuide = I have nobody to look after my son.

sentence: Luis acaba de contar delante de todos un secreto que Ana le confió; desapruebo que revele información privada sin pedirle permiso a ella.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative evaluative verb
grammar: Desapruebo que introduces a negative evaluation of Luis's established conduct and selects subjunctive revele. The speaker condemns the disclosure rather than denying that it occurred.
register: Neutral criticism of a breach of confidence.
note: Desaprobar = disapprove of; delante de todos = in front of everyone; revele = he discloses within the evaluation; pedirle permiso a ella = ask Ana's permission.

sentence: Concedo que tu propuesta reduce el costo del viaje, Ana; ya revisamos las cuentas, pero el horario sigue sin servirnos porque llegamos después de que empieza la función.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative verb acknowledging a point
grammar: Concedo que acknowledges the cost reduction as a point the speaker accepts, using indicative reduce. The concession does not remove the separate scheduling objection.
register: Reasoned disagreement with a familiar person.
note: Conceder que = concede or acknowledge that; cuentas = calculations; sigue sin servirnos = still does not meet our needs; función = theater performance.

sentence: Ana entregó su cuento y ya recibió una confirmación de entrega; eso no implica que el jurado lo haya elegido, porque la selección todavía no se anuncia.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb expressing a logical consequence
grammar: No implica que denies an entailment from confirmed submission to selection. The submission is established; the finite subjunctive clause presents a consequence that the speaker does not endorse.
register: Careful explanation of a cultural selection process.
note: Implicar = entail or necessarily mean here; cuento = short story; jurado = judging panel; lo haya elegido = has selected it within the nonendorsed consequence; selección = selection.

sentence: El dueño del salón se opone a que los músicos ensayen después de las diez de la noche; los vecinos duermen a esa hora.
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a finite-clause complementizer
grammar: Oponerse a que retains the selected preposition a before a finite subjunctive clause. The owner opposes the action; the musicians would perform it.
register: Neutral explanation of a shared-space disagreement.
note: Oponerse a = oppose; dueño = owner; salón = hall here; músicos = musicians; ensayen = they rehearse within the opposed action.

sentence: La práctica diaria contribuyó a que Ana aprendiera a leer las partituras; sus clases también fueron importantes y ahora puede seguir una pieza completa sin ayuda.
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a finite-clause complementizer
grammar: Contribuir a que introduces the result to which something contributes. Aprendiera is subjunctive despite the explicitly realized learning; practice is one cause alongside Ana's classes.
register: Neutral account of musical learning.
note: Contribuir a = contribute to; práctica diaria = daily practice; partituras = musical scores; aprendiera = she learned within the result clause; pieza = musical piece.

sentence: La directora podía presentar ella misma la obra o dejarle esa tarea a Ana; optó por que Ana la presentara y la directora se quedó entre el público.
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a finite-clause complementizer
grammar: Optar por que retains governed por before a finite clause with its own actor. The director makes the choice and Ana is the selected presenter; causal porque would express a different relation. The choice alone does not establish that Ana completed the presentation.
register: Neutral account of a cultural event.
note: Optar por que = choose for someone to perform an action; presentara = she present within the chosen action; obra = play here; público = audience.

sentence: Ana, para entrar mañana a mi taller de dibujo basta con que digas tu nombre en la puerta; no necesitas llevar documentos ni pagar.
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a finite-clause complementizer
grammar: Impersonal basta con que introduces the action sufficient for Ana's admission. The con-clause is a complement of bastar rather than a subject clause without con; no additional payment or documents are required.
register: Familiar explanation from a workshop organizer.
note: Bastar con que = be enough for someone to do something; taller de dibujo = drawing workshop; digas = you say within the sufficing clause; documentos = documents.

sentence: Quiero que mis hijos cenen conmigo todos los días, pero sé que salen tarde del trabajo; me conformo con que vengan los domingos y no les pediré más visitas.
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a finite-clause complementizer
grammar: Conformarse con que introduces the limited outcome the speaker willingly accepts. Sunday visits are below the explicitly preferred daily meals, and vengan is present subjunctive.
register: Neutral family expectation.
note: Conformarse con = be satisfied with or settle for; cenen conmigo = have dinner with me; me conformo con que vengan = I am satisfied if they come.

sentence: Me gustaría tener a mi hermana cerca, pero el lunes se mudará a Mérida por dos años; me resigno a que viva lejos de mí durante ese tiempo.
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a finite-clause complementizer
grammar: Resignarse a que introduces an unwanted outcome the speaker accepts. The announced Monday move establishes the forecast, while the speaker's preference remains different.
register: Neutral acknowledgment of an unwelcome family change.
note: Resignarse a = accept something reluctantly; me gustaría tener a mi hermana cerca = I would like to have my sister nearby; se mudará = she will move home; Mérida is a city.

sentence: Cuando compartía casa con Luis, él ponía música a las dos de la mañana todos los viernes; yo no soportaba que me despertara así.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect indicative verb under negation
grammar: No soportaba que expresses emotional inability to bear an established repeated event. Despertara is imperfect subjunctive. The emotional clause presents the repeated waking as factual; the preceding music routine establishes its setting but does not independently verify the waking.
register: Neutral recollection of difficult shared living.
note: Soportar = bear or put up with; compartía casa = shared a home; ponía música = played music; me despertara = he woke me within the emotional evaluation.

sentence: Si la directora tolerara que los alumnos ensayaran en el patio sin permiso, estaría enterada y no intervendría, pero eso no sería darles su autorización.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb in a hypothetical condition
grammar: Tolerara describes imagined knowing noninterference by the director. Its finite complement names the pupils' rehearsing, and the sentence explicitly distinguishes toleration from affirmative authorization.
register: Careful discussion of an imagined authority's response.
note: Tolerar = knowingly allow something to continue without intervening here; ensayaran = they rehearsed in the hypothetical case; estaría enterada = she would know about it; intervendría = she would intervene; autorización = authorization.

sentence: Luis, ayer revisaste mi cuaderno sin pedirme permiso; sé que lo hiciste, pero no admito que vuelvas a leer mis notas privadas sin preguntarme.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative permission verb under negation
grammar: No admito que withholds present normative permission for a repetition. It does not deny yesterday's acknowledged incident; vuelvas a leer identifies the action the speaker refuses to allow.
register: Firm personal boundary addressed to a familiar person.
note: Admitir = allow or accept as permissible here; cuaderno = notebook; notas privadas = private notes; vuelvas a leer = read again within the refused action.

sentence: La directora le dio a Ana permiso expreso para ensayar en el salón; me sorprendió que consintiera que Ana lo usara gratis el sábado. Ana ensayó ahí ese día.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect subjunctive verb governing a finite action clause
grammar: Consintiera identifies the director's affirmative grant of consent, already established by permiso expreso. Ana's actual Saturday rehearsal is reported separately from the consent and the speaker's surprise.
register: Neutral account of authorized cultural activity.
note: Consentir que = give consent for an action; consintiera has the stem consint-; permiso expreso = explicit permission; lo refers to the hall; gratis = without payment.

sentence: La organizadora quería hornear diez charolas de pan al mismo tiempo; la cocinera objetó que el horno solo tenía espacio para dos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reporting verb
grammar: Objetó que reports the cook's asserted reason for objecting, using indicative tenía. The content is a capacity assertion attributed to her rather than a directive telling someone what to do.
register: Neutral report of a practical objection.
note: Objetar = raise an objection; hornear = bake; charolas = trays; cocinera = female cook; horno = oven; dos replaces dos charolas.

sentence: Elena afirmó que el poema era de su abuelo; Raúl cuestionó que esa atribución fuera correcta porque el manuscrito no tenía firma. Ninguno pudo comprobar quién lo escribió.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb challenging validity
grammar: Cuestionó que challenges the validity of the attribution and introduces subjunctive fuera. The missing signature gives a reason for the challenge, while the final sentence leaves authorship unresolved.
register: Careful literary discussion.
note: Cuestionar = challenge or call into question; atribución = attribution of authorship; manuscrito = manuscript; firma = signature; lo refers to the poem.

sentence: Un mensaje del club anunció que la biblioteca estaría cerrada todo el sábado; la encargada desmintió que estuviera cerrada ese día: me dejó entrar el sábado por la mañana y me prestó un libro.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reporting verb
grammar: Desmintió que rejects the club message's false closure report and introduces subjunctive estuviera. The speaker's actual entry and loan on Saturday provide explicit evidence against the announced all-day closure.
register: Neutral correction of an incorrect service announcement.
note: Desmentir = deny or refute a report as false; desmintió has the stem desmint-; encargada = woman in charge; estaría cerrada = would be closed in the earlier announcement.

sentence: Luis es invitado en mi casa, pero cambia de lugar mis muebles y decide quién entra como si fuera el dueño; yo no le he dado esa autoridad.
part_of_speech: comparative subordinating conjunctive sequence
grammar: Como si introduces an imagined comparison with imperfect subjunctive fuera. Luis's observable conduct resembles an owner's, but the sentence establishes that he is a guest without that authority; this is not an ordinary if condition.
register: Conversational complaint about a guest's behavior.
note: Invitado = guest here; cambiar de lugar los muebles = move furniture around; dueño = owner; autoridad = authority; fuera is ser in this comparison.

sentence: Ana mira al piso y evita hablarme como si hubiera recibido una mala noticia antes de llegar; no sé si alguien le comunicó algo ni qué le pasa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in a comparison
grammar: Hubiera recibido places the supposed receipt of news before Ana's current conduct. Como si frames a comparison, and the speaker explicitly leaves the actual receipt of news unknown rather than declaring it contrary to fact.
register: Neutral observation about Ana's behavior.
note: Mirar al piso = look down at the floor; evita hablarme = avoids speaking to me; hubiera recibido = had received in the comparison; comunicar algo a alguien = tell someone something.

sentence: Ana y yo fuimos al museo como visitantes; ahí el guía nos pidió consejos para organizar la colección como si fuéramos especialistas, aunque ninguno de los dos trabaja en ese campo.
part_of_speech: first-person plural imperfect subjunctive copular verb
grammar: Visible fuimos al museo expresses movement with ir; hidden fuéramos especialistas expresses an imagined classification with ser. The noun predicate especialistas identifies the copular reading of a form that can also belong to ir. Como si frames the comparison, and fuéramos requires its written accent.
register: Neutral account of an unexpected museum interaction.
note: Visitantes = visitors; guía = guide; consejos = advice; colección = collection; especialistas = specialists; ese campo = that field of work or expertise.

sentence: Mi hermana ya me devolvió el libro y lo tengo aquí; me alegra que haya cumplido su promesa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present perfect subjunctive auxiliary
grammar: Haya combines with visible cumplido to evaluate a completed event from the present. The actual return and the book's presence independently establish fulfillment; the emotional subjunctive does not express doubt.
register: Neutral appreciation of a kept promise.
note: Haya cumplido = has fulfilled within the emotional evaluation; cumplir una promesa = keep a promise; me alegra que = I am glad that; lo refers to the returned book.

sentence: Ana y yo todavía estamos limpiando la casa; espero que para mañana a las diez hayamos terminado, porque a esa hora llegan mis padres.
part_of_speech: first-person plural present perfect subjunctive auxiliary
grammar: Hayamos terminado places hoped-for completion before tomorrow's ten o'clock arrival. Ana and the speaker are still cleaning now, so perfect morphology has a future completion reference here.
register: Neutral household preparation.
note: Hayamos terminado = we have finished by the stated future time; espero que = I hope that; a esa hora refers to tomorrow at ten; mis padres are the speaker's parents.

sentence: Ayer a las seis llegué a la biblioteca y vi agua bajo la puerta; temí que la lluvia hubiera dañado los libros antes de mi llegada. A las siete los revisé: estaban intactos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in a past fear clause
grammar: Hubiera dañado places the feared damage before the six o'clock arrival and fear. The seven o'clock inspection is later verification, showing that the books were intact; this is anterior fear rather than fear of a later action.
register: Neutral account of concern about library books.
note: Temí que = I feared that; lluvia = rain; dañar = damage; antes de mi llegada = before my arrival; intactos = undamaged; los refers to the books.

sentence: En mi crónica del sábado escribí: «Las dos actrices terminaron de ensayar a las seis; a las siete me alegró que hubiesen repasado todas sus escenas antes de terminar».
part_of_speech: third-person plural pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in the -se variant
grammar: Hubiesen repasado presents plural completion before the seven o'clock evaluation. The written account establishes that the actresses completed their rehearsal at six; the -se compound is an accepted variant without an exclusive regional label.
register: Written account of a theater rehearsal.
note: Crónica = written account; actrices = actresses; repasar las escenas = go through the scenes again; hubiesen repasado = they had reviewed within the past appreciation.

sentence: Ana recibió mi carta ayer y aún no responde; no creo que haya leído el mensaje, pero no lo he podido comprobar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present perfect subjunctive auxiliary under negated belief
grammar: No creo que haya leído withholds endorsement of completed reading before now. Ana's silence supplies a reason for the belief but does not prove that she has not read the letter.
register: Neutral uncertainty about personal correspondence.
note: Aún no responde = she still has not replied; haya leído = has read within the nonendorsed proposition; mensaje refers to the letter's message; no lo he podido comprobar = I have not been able to verify it.

sentence: El lunes Luis negó que Ana y Diego hubieran usado su horno el domingo; mostró la puerta cerrada como prueba. El martes ellos confirmaron, con fotos del domingo, que sí hornearon pan ahí.
part_of_speech: third-person plural pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in an attributed past denial
grammar: Hubieran usado places the denied use on Sunday before Luis's Monday denial. The closed door is his offered evidence; Tuesday's confirmation and photographs separately establish the actual use rather than converting his denial into narrator fact.
register: Neutral reconstruction of a disputed household event.
note: Negó que = denied that; prueba = evidence here; hubieran usado = they had used within the denial; hornearon = baked; ahí refers to Luis's oven.

sentence: Mañana a las diez pasaré por el taller; en caso de que la costurera ya haya terminado mi falda para entonces, me la llevaré.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present perfect subjunctive auxiliary in a future contingency
grammar: Haya terminado makes completion before tomorrow's ten o'clock visit the contingency for taking the skirt away. Para entonces refers to that future checkpoint; the perfect does not locate the condition before the present.
register: Neutral clothing-service arrangement.
note: Costurera = seamstress; pasaré por = I will stop by; haya terminado = has finished by the future checkpoint; me la llevaré = I will take it away with me, referring to the skirt.

sentence: Mañana mi papá preparará el pan para la comida familiar; cuando haya terminado de hornearlo, yo lo llevaré a casa de mi abuela. Antes de eso no saldré.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present perfect subjunctive auxiliary in a future temporal clause
grammar: Cuando haya terminado requires completion of the father's baking before the speaker takes the bread away tomorrow. The final sentence confirms that departure will wait for completion rather than occur during baking.
register: Neutral family meal coordination.
note: Preparará = will prepare; hornearlo = bake it, referring to the bread; lo llevaré = I will take it; antes de eso = before that completion.

sentence: El lunes decidí no entregar el cuento hasta que Ana lo hubiera leído completo; Ana acabó de leerlo el miércoles a las ocho y yo lo entregué a las nueve.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in a prospective past endpoint clause
grammar: The Monday decision makes Ana's completed reading a prerequisite for submission. Hubiera leído is prospective from that earlier decision but anterior to the planned handover; Wednesday's reading and submission establish fulfillment separately.
register: Neutral account of a literary submission.
note: Cuento = short story; hubiera leído completo = had read all of it; acabó de leerlo = finished reading it here; lo refers to the story throughout.

sentence: El lunes Ana y yo gastamos en el paseo el dinero reservado para la comida; el miércoles lamentamos haber usado ese dinero, porque ya no podíamos comprar lo necesario.
part_of_speech: infinitive auxiliary forming a perfect infinitive in a factual-regret complement
grammar: Haber combines with visible usado to place the acknowledged Monday action before Wednesday's regret. Ana and the speaker are both the people regretting and the understood subject of haber usado. The infinitival clause functions as the direct object of lamentamos, without de.
register: Neutral self-critical account of shared spending.
note: Lamentamos haber usado = we regretted having used; lamentamos has past reference in this Wednesday account. Gastar = spend money; paseo = outing here; dinero reservado para la comida = money set aside for the meal; lo necesario = what was needed.

sentence: Mi abuela salió de viaje ayer y yo no la llamé antes de su salida; ojalá la hubiera llamado para despedirme, porque estará una semana sin teléfono.
part_of_speech: first-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in an unfulfilled past wish
grammar: Current ojalá la hubiera llamado expresses a wish contrary to the explicitly stated omission before yesterday's departure. The missed action is a past call, not a currently absent resource.
register: Neutral personal regret.
note: Ojalá la hubiera llamado = I wish I had called her; despedirme = say goodbye; salida = departure here; estará una semana sin teléfono = she will be without a phone for a week.

sentence: El camión de mi hermana Ana tenía previsto llegar a Oaxaca hoy a las seis; ya son las diez y ella no me escribe. Ojalá haya llegado bien, pero aún no lo sé.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present perfect subjunctive auxiliary in an unverified past hope
grammar: Ojalá haya llegado expresses current hope about arrival before now. The scheduled six o'clock arrival precedes the current ten o'clock reference, but the outcome remains unverified; this is not a known unfulfilled wish.
register: Neutral family concern during travel.
note: Tenía previsto llegar = was scheduled to arrive; Oaxaca is the destination; haya llegado bien = has arrived safely within the hope; aún no lo sé = I still do not know whether she arrived safely.

sentence: Ana, desde ayer sabías que hoy no vendrías, pero no me avisaste y ya cociné para las dos; ¡me hubieras avisado ayer!
part_of_speech: second-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in an independent reproach
grammar: Me hubieras avisado reproaches Ana for an omitted earlier notification. It is an independent retrospective reproach, not an assertion that she notified the speaker or an ordinary conditional result.
register: Familiar, reproachful speech between two women.
note: Hubieras avisado = you should have told me in this reproach; sabías = you knew; vendrías = you would come in the earlier knowledge; para las dos = for both women; me identifies the speaker who should have been notified.

sentence: Ana y yo elegimos comprar los boletos sin revisar la fecha y perdimos el dinero porque eran para el día anterior; mejor hubiéramos comprobado la fecha antes de pagar.
part_of_speech: first-person plural pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in a self-critical missed-opportunity comment
grammar: Mejor hubiéramos comprobado evaluates the group's own omitted check as the better past choice. The actual decision, missing check, and lost money are explicit; the comment expresses shared self-criticism rather than blaming an outside addressee.
register: Conversational self-criticism after a shared mistake.
note: Elegimos = we chose; día anterior = the day before the purchase; mejor hubiéramos comprobado = we should have checked instead; antes de pagar = before paying.

sentence: Luis me ofreció llevarme a casa gratis anoche, pero rechacé su oferta y pagué ciento veinte pesos de taxi; me hubiera ahorrado ese gasto.
part_of_speech: first-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary expressing an independent unreal result
grammar: Me hubiera ahorrado gives the unreal result of accepting Luis's explicitly rejected free ride. The condition is recovered from the preceding text rather than an overt si clause; habría is also valid for this result.
register: Conversational reflection on a rejected offer.
note: Oferta = offer; me hubiera ahorrado ese gasto = I would have saved myself that expense; ese gasto is the actual hundred-and-twenty-peso taxi payment. The implied premise is accepting Luis's free ride home.

sentence: El lunes le pedí a Ana que para el miércoles a las nueve ya hubiera leído el cuento completo, porque a esa hora ella y yo discutiríamos el final; terminó de leerlo el martes por la noche.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary expressing completion before a future-in-the-past deadline
grammar: Hubiera leído requires completed reading by Wednesday at nine, a time future from Monday's request. Tuesday night's completion separately verifies fulfillment; the pluperfect is not limited to events before the request itself.
register: Neutral coordination of a literary discussion.
note: Para el miércoles a las nueve = by Wednesday at nine; cuento = short story; discutiríamos el final = we would discuss the ending; terminó de leerlo = Ana finished reading it.

sentence: El centro cultural abrió ayer una sala gratuita para los vecinos. Celebro que haya creado un lugar donde podamos reunirnos sin pagar.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative evaluative verb
grammar: Celebro que expresses current approval of an established completed result through perfect subjunctive haya creado. Here celebrar evaluates the result positively rather than describing the organization of a festive event.
register: Neutral public appreciation of a community resource.
note: Celebrar que = welcome or express approval that; centro cultural = cultural center; gratuita = free of charge; haya creado = has created within the approval; podamos reunirnos = we can meet.

sentence: Ana me confirmó que trabaja de noche todos los días y duerme solo cuatro horas; me inquieta que duerma tan poco, porque la veo agotada.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative psychological verb with a clausal subject
grammar: The subject of inquieta is the finite clause que duerma tan poco; me identifies the concerned speaker. Ana's report establishes the sleep pattern, and concern does not imply uncertainty about it; clitic spelling alone does not determine grammatical case.
register: Neutral concern about Ana's sleep.
note: Inquietar = cause concern or unease; duerma = she sleeps within the concern clause; tan poco = so little; agotada = exhausted; la refers to Ana.

sentence: El autor de la reseña afirma que esa novela fue la primera publicada en el pueblo; es cuestionable que sea la primera, porque solo consultó un archivo y quedan otros dos sin revisar.
part_of_speech: singular evaluative adjective
grammar: Cuestionable evaluates the reported claim's defensibility through a finite subjunctive clause. The limited archival search gives a concrete reason to question it without establishing that another novel was published earlier.
register: Careful critical discussion of a literary review.
note: Cuestionable = open to question or challenge; reseña = review; novela = novel; publicada = published; archivo = archive; otros dos refers to two further archives.

sentence: La carta describe la casa donde creció mi abuelo; es verosímil que él la haya escrito, pero la carta no tiene firma y aún no sabemos quién fue el autor.
part_of_speech: singular evaluative adjective
grammar: Verosímil evaluates the grandfather's authorship as plausible from the letter's description of his childhood home. The chosen subjunctive clause preserves the possible attribution, while the missing signature and unknown author keep it unconfirmed; this does not impose one construction on every use of the adjective.
register: Careful discussion of family correspondence.
note: Verosímil = plausible or believable; creció = grew up; firma = signature; él refers to the grandfather; la haya escrito = he has written the letter within the plausible attribution.

sentence: La mesa compartida en el patio propició que los vecinos conversaran después de comer; ese domingo se quedaron ahí platicando una hora.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative causal verb
grammar: Propiciar que presents a circumstance that favors another actor's action. Conversaran is factual subjunctive here: the following clause independently establishes the conversation.
register: Neutral account of neighborhood interaction.
note: Mesa compartida = shared table; propiciar que = create favorable conditions for; conversaran = the neighbors talked within the causal clause; platicando = chatting. The verb itself does not guarantee completion in every context.

sentence: En el taller de música, comparar dos interpretaciones favoreció que Ana reconociera distintas maneras de tocar la misma pieza; al final pudo explicar las diferencias sin ayuda.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative causal verb
grammar: Favorecer que links a learning activity to a useful development. Reconociera is factual subjunctive, with Ana's subsequent explanation establishing the achieved learning.
register: Neutral discussion of musical learning.
note: Interpretaciones = performances or interpretations of a musical work; reconocer distintas maneras = identify different ways; pieza = musical piece. Favorecer concerns the development here, rather than preferential treatment of Ana.

sentence: Las bicicletas en el pasillo obstaculizaron que Rosa pasara con sus bolsas; después de mover las bicicletas contra la pared, ella sí llegó a su departamento.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative causal verb
grammar: Obstaculizar que describes difficulty imposed on an action without entailing its prevention. Pasara is factual subjunctive; Rosa's eventual arrival is explicitly established.
register: Neutral shared-building narrative.
