note: Pasillo = hallway; contra la pared = against the wall; departamento = apartment. The bicycles made passage difficult, but Rosa ultimately got through with her bags.

sentence: El nuevo acceso sin escalones posibilita que mi abuelo entre a la sala de lectura con su silla de ruedas; el acceso está abierto, pero él todavía no ha ido.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative enabling verb
grammar: Posibilitar que identifies an available enabling condition. Entre is subjunctive for the enabled action, whose actual performance is explicitly still pending.
register: Neutral discussion of access to a reading room.
note: Acceso = entrance or access route; escalones = steps; sala de lectura = reading room; silla de ruedas = wheelchair. The grandfather can enter through the available access, but has not yet visited.

sentence: El martes mi hermana me desaconsejó que llevara el sillón a mi nuevo departamento el miércoles: el elevador estaba descompuesto; seguí su consejo y lo dejé en mi casa anterior.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative advisory verb
grammar: Desaconsejar que advises against an action rather than forbidding it. Llevara concerns Wednesday's proposed move, later than Tuesday's advice; the speaker's subsequent choice is stated separately.
register: Practical advice between siblings.
note: Sillón = armchair; elevador = elevator; descompuesto = out of order; seguí su consejo = I followed her advice; lo refers to the armchair.

sentence: En la reunión del barrio, la organizadora Elena exhortó a los vecinos a que donaran libros infantiles durante esa semana para abrir una biblioteca; al terminar la reunión, aún no había recibido ninguno.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative directive verb
grammar: Exhortar a alguien a que retains the governed a before the finite clause. Los vecinos is the personal direct object; donaran is the requested action, rather than an assertion of donations.
register: Formal appeal in a neighborhood meeting.
note: Exhortar = formally urge; donar = donate; libros infantiles = children's books; biblioteca = library. Ninguno refers to donated books; none had been received by the meeting's end.

sentence: El lunes, al ver que entraba agua al salón vecinal, Marta, coordinadora del grupo, instó a los voluntarios a que sacaran los libros esa misma tarde; ellos los trasladaron a un cuarto seco antes de las seis.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative directive verb
grammar: Instar a alguien a que expresses pressing an identified actor to act, retaining a before que. The volunteers are the personal direct object; their later removal of the books independently confirms compliance.
register: Urgent community coordination.
note: Salón vecinal = neighborhood meeting room; voluntarios = volunteers; sacaran = they took out within the request; trasladaron = moved to another place; los refers to the books.

sentence: Mi primo Luis pensaba vender su guitarra para pagar una reparación; le mostré que sus ahorros alcanzaban y lo disuadí de que la vendiera. Luis retiró el anuncio y decidió conservarla.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative persuasion verb
grammar: Disuadir a alguien de que retains de before the finite clause. Luis is the person persuaded, represented by direct-object lo; selling the guitar is the purpose he abandons, not the verb's personal object.
register: Reasoned persuasion between cousins.
note: Sus ahorros alcanzaban = his savings were enough; disuadir de que = persuade someone not to carry out a purpose; retiró el anuncio = removed the advertisement; la and conservarla refer to Luis's guitar.

sentence: Ayer Ana intentó persuadir a su hermano Luis para que cantara con ella en la reunión familiar de esa noche; le ofreció ensayar juntos antes, pero Luis rechazó la propuesta y no cantó.
part_of_speech: infinitive persuasion verb with a personal object and finite para que complement
grammar: Persuadir a alguien para que is an admitted finite action frame. Intentó places the persuasion inside an attempt; cantara concerns the later proposed singing, which Luis explicitly declined.
register: Family persuasion without achieved compliance.
note: Persuadir = influence someone through persuasion; cantara = Luis sang within the intended action; con ella refers to Ana; ensayar juntos = rehearse together. Other supported complements of persuadir are not categorically excluded.

sentence: El salón seguía cerrado; hablé con la encargada y logré que nos abriera la puerta a las seis: Ana y yo entramos a esa hora y pudimos ensayar.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite achievement verb followed by a finite-clause complementizer
grammar: Lograr que introduces an achieved action performed by another actor. The speaker obtains the result; the woman in charge opens the door. Entry at six separately establishes success.
register: Neutral account of arranging rehearsal access.
note: Encargada = woman in charge; nos refers to Ana and the speaker; abriera = she opened within the achieved-result clause; ensayar = rehearse.

sentence: Para terminar hoy la cortina, es imprescindible que mi hermana me preste su máquina de coser: la mía se descompuso y no tenemos tiempo para coserla a mano.
part_of_speech: singular evaluative adjective
grammar: Es imprescindible que evaluates the sister's pending loan as indispensable for today's practical goal. Preste is subjunctive; the broken machine and lack of time make the dependency explicit.
register: Neutral household planning.
note: Cortina = curtain; máquina de coser = sewing machine; la mía refers to the speaker's machine; coserla refers to sewing the curtain; a mano = by hand.

sentence: En la charla del club, el organizador dejó hablar diez minutos a sus amigos y solo uno a los demás; es inadmisible que diera tan poco espacio a quienes también habían preparado su intervención.
part_of_speech: singular normative evaluative adjective
grammar: Inadmisible condemns the established unequal treatment. Diera is factual past subjunctive under a current normative evaluation; the sentence neither doubts the conduct nor makes a legal ruling.
register: Firm criticism of unfair treatment in a club.
note: Los demás = the other participants; dar espacio = allow an opportunity to contribute here; intervención = contribution to the discussion; quienes refers to the other prepared participants.

sentence: Antes de la lectura de ayer, Ana y yo podíamos leer el cuento en voz alta o dejar que Luis lo leyera; era preferible que él lo hiciera, porque las dos teníamos la voz cansada y Luis no.
part_of_speech: singular comparative evaluative adjective
grammar: Era preferible que ranks Luis's reading above the explicitly available alternative. Hiciera names the action favored before yesterday's reading; the comparison does not make it indispensable.
register: Neutral coordination of a reading.
note: Cuento = short story; leer en voz alta = read aloud; las dos identifies Ana and the speaker as women; él and lo hiciera refer to Luis reading the story aloud.

sentence: La maestra del taller nos dijo a los principiantes: «Es aconsejable que prueben el carbón en una hoja aparte para conocer el trazo; ustedes deciden si lo hacen».
part_of_speech: singular advisory evaluative adjective
grammar: Es aconsejable que recommends the beginners' action for a stated learning purpose. Prueben refers to ustedes; the teacher explicitly leaves the decision to the learners.
register: Instructional advice with explicit learner choice.
note: Principiantes = beginners; carbón = drawing charcoal here; hoja aparte = separate sheet; trazo = line or mark made when drawing. Lo hacen refers to trying the charcoal on that sheet.

sentence: Antes de abrir el salón, ya teníamos treinta asistentes confirmados y solo veinte sillas; era previsible que faltaran asientos, y al empezar la charla diez personas se quedaron de pie.
part_of_speech: singular evidential evaluative adjective
grammar: Era previsible que evaluates a shortage as foreseeable from the earlier attendance and chair figures. Faltaran belongs to that expectation; the later standing participants independently establish the outcome.
register: Neutral retrospective assessment of event planning.
note: Asistentes confirmados = confirmed attendees; asientos = seats; quedarse de pie = remain standing. The stated evidence supports a forecast, rather than certainty about every future event.

sentence: Luis esperó dos horas y, al llegar su turno, el empleado cerró la ventanilla sin atenderlo; es comprensible que se enojara, pero los insultos que después dirigió al empleado no fueron aceptables.
part_of_speech: singular evaluative adjective
grammar: Comprensible evaluates Luis's established anger as understandable given the wait and refusal of service. Se enojara is factual subjunctive; understanding the reaction does not endorse the subsequent insults.
register: Measured assessment of a service conflict.
note: Ventanilla = service window; atenderlo = serve Luis; se enojara = Luis became angry within the evaluation; dirigir insultos a alguien = address insults to someone.

sentence: En las cincuenta reuniones anteriores de nuestro club nadie había llevado un instrumento; ayer Ana llegó con un violín y tocó para todos. Me pareció insólito que Ana llevara un instrumento a nuestra reunión.
part_of_speech: masculine singular evaluative adjective
grammar: Insólito marks bringing an instrument as unusual against the club's explicitly bounded prior experience. Llevara is factual imperfect subjunctive; Ana's arrival with a violin independently establishes the evaluated action.
register: Neutral personal assessment of a club gathering.
note: Violín = violin; instrumento = musical instrument; tocó = played music; llevara un instrumento = Ana brought an instrument within the evaluation. The unusualness concerns this club's stated history.

sentence: Mañana mi amiga Ana y yo vamos a llevar una sola mochila a dos calles de casa; sería descabellado que ella propusiera rentar un camión de mudanzas para las dos, aunque tenemos dinero para hacerlo.
part_of_speech: masculine singular evaluative adjective
grammar: Sería descabellado que evaluates a hypothetical proposal as unreasonable because its means greatly exceed the stated task. Propusiera concerns Ana's possible proposal for tomorrow; the available money keeps affordability separate.
register: Conversational assessment between friends.
note: Una sola mochila = just one backpack; a dos calles de casa = two blocks from home; rentar = rent; camión de mudanzas = moving truck; las dos identifies Ana and the speaker as women.

sentence: La única copia del cuento estaba en el cuaderno de Ana; ella lo trajo cinco minutos antes de mi lectura y empecé a la hora anunciada. Fue decisivo que llegara con el cuaderno para empezar sin retraso.
part_of_speech: masculine singular causal evaluative adjective
grammar: Fue decisivo que evaluates Ana's established arrival with the only text copy as decisive for the speaker's timely start. Llegara is factual past subjunctive, with the enabling action and result independently stated.
register: Neutral account of a literary reading.
note: Cuaderno = notebook; la única copia = the only copy; lectura = reading event here; hora anunciada = announced time; sin retraso = without delay.

sentence: Mi vecina Rosa cuidó mis plantas durante un mes sin cobrarme; merece que yo le dé las gracias en persona, pero todavía no lo he hecho.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative evaluative verb
grammar: Merecer que presents a response as deserved because of Rosa's established help. Dé names the speaker's appropriate response in subjunctive; the final clause explicitly establishes that the speaker has not yet thanked Rosa in person.
register: Personal appreciation of a neighbor's help.
note: Vecina = female neighbor; sin cobrarme = without charging me; dar las gracias = thank; en persona = in person; le identifies Rosa as the person to be thanked. No lo he hecho refers to not having thanked her in person.

sentence: Yo esperaba que el cuento de mi hermana terminara con una despedida, pero los personajes acabaron viviendo juntos; me sorprendió que ella eligiera un final tan alegre.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative psychological verb with a clausal subject
grammar: The subject of sorprendió is que ella eligiera un final tan alegre; me identifies the surprised speaker. The actual ending contradicts the stated expectation, so the subjunctive does not express doubt.
register: Personal discussion of a sibling's story.
note: Despedida = farewell; personajes = story characters; acabaron viviendo juntos = ended up living together; eligiera = the sister chose within the factual reaction.

sentence: La encargada devolvió el dinero a sus amigos y se negó a devolverlo a los demás, aunque todos habían pagado por la misma función cancelada; me indignó que hiciera esa distinción.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative psychological verb with a clausal subject
grammar: Que hiciera esa distinción is the factual stimulus causing the speaker's moral anger. The customers refused refunds are the affected party; me identifies the speaker as the experiencer. The sentence does not specify whether the speaker also belongs to that customer group.
register: Moral criticism of unequal treatment.
note: Indignar = cause moral anger; función cancelada = canceled performance; los demás = the other paying attendees; esa distinción refers to refunding friends while refusing everyone else.

sentence: Después de mi primera lectura en público, mi hermano me entregó una nota escrita por él con sus frases favoritas de mi cuento; me conmovió que dedicara tiempo a escribirla.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative affective verb with a clausal subject
grammar: Conmovió expresses an emotional response to the brother's considerate action. Que dedicara tiempo a escribirla is a factual clausal subject; delivery of the note written by him establishes that the writing was completed.
register: Warm personal account of sibling support.
note: Conmover = move emotionally here; frases favoritas = favorite phrases; dedicar tiempo a = devote time to; escribirla refers to writing the note. The sense concerns emotion rather than physical movement.

sentence: Ayer interrumpí a mi hermana tres veces y ella no pudo terminar su explicación; ahora me avergüenza que yo no la dejara hablar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular stem-changing present indicative psychological verb
grammar: Avergüenza expresses current shame about the speaker's acknowledged past conduct. Que yo no la dejara hablar is the factual stimulus clause; la denotes the sister prevented from finishing.
register: Personal acknowledgment of inconsiderate behavior.
note: Interrumpí = I interrupted; no pudo terminar = she was unable to finish; dejar hablar = let someone speak. Avergüenza retains the dieresis in güe; the sentence makes no claim about the sister's feelings.

sentence: Hoy vi a Ana entrelazar tiras de papel hasta formar una canasta; me fascina que pueda crear una figura tan firme sin pegamento, como hizo delante de mí.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative psychological verb with a clausal subject
grammar: Fascina expresses captivated interest in a demonstrated process. Que pueda crear una figura tan firme is a factual stimulus clause; the witnessed basket-making establishes the ability.
register: Enthusiastic discussion of a craft process.
note: Entrelazar = interweave; tiras de papel = paper strips; canasta = basket; firme = sturdy here; pegamento = glue. Pueda concerns Ana's demonstrated ability.

sentence: En las tres reuniones de esta semana, Luis me interrumpió cada vez que intenté explicar una idea; me irrita que lo haga tan seguido, porque no puedo terminar de hablar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative psychological verb with a clausal subject
grammar: Irrita expresses annoyance caused by established repeated behavior. Que lo haga tan seguido is a habitual factual stimulus; me identifies the affected speaker without making the reaction a claim of doubt.
register: Direct complaint about repeated interruptions.
note: Tan seguido = so often; lo haga refers to Luis interrupting the speaker; terminar de hablar = finish speaking. Irritar has an emotional annoyance sense here.

sentence: Mi tía me presentó ayer a tres personas porque, según me dijo, quería ayudarme a encontrar pareja; me incomodó que hiciera esas presentaciones sin consultarme, aunque agradezco su buena intención.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative psychological verb with a clausal subject
grammar: Incomodó expresses social discomfort about an established action. The aunt's stated helpful purpose and the speaker's acknowledged appreciation coexist with discomfort about being excluded from the decision.
register: Measured discussion of a family boundary.
note: Encontrar pareja = find a romantic partner; presentaciones = introductions here; consultarme = ask me before acting; hiciera refers to the aunt's completed introductions.

sentence: Ana siempre me avisa cuando cambia el horario de su librería; hoy la encontré cerrada y ella confirmó por teléfono que no abrirá, aunque no me había avisado. Me extraña que omitiera el aviso previo esta vez.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative psychological verb with a clausal subject
grammar: Extrañar with a finite stimulus clause means finding something strange. Ana's omission of advance notice is established and conflicts with her stated routine; this is distinct from emotionally missing someone.
register: Neutral reaction to an unexpected change in a familiar routine.
note: Librería = bookstore; omitir = omit; aviso previo = advance notice; la encontré cerrada refers to the bookstore. The later telephone confirmation does not supply the omitted advance notice.

sentence: Por las cajas vacías y las paredes sin cuadros, se me antoja que Ana ya está preparando la mudanza, pero todavía no se lo he preguntado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative pronominal judgment verb with visible se and experiencer me
grammar: Se me antoja que presents a proposition as probable in the speaker's judgment. The finite indicative está preparando states the content of that unconfirmed inference; this is not a desire for Ana to act.
register: Reflective personal conjecture.
note: Cajas vacías = empty boxes; cuadros = pictures on the walls; mudanza = household move. Se me antoja que = it seems probable to me that in this sense, distinct from a food craving.

sentence: Mi hermano y yo vivimos en ciudades distintas desde hace tres años; desde entonces anhelamos que nuestros hijos se conozcan en persona, pero la visita de diciembre aún no está confirmada.
part_of_speech: first-person plural present indicative desire verb
grammar: Anhelar que expresses sustained strong longing for a future result. Se conozcan refers to the siblings' children meeting each other; the unconfirmed December visit keeps fulfillment pending.
register: Educated personal expression of strong family longing.
note: Anhelar = long strongly for; desde entonces = since then; se conozcan en persona = meet each other in person; nuestros hijos refers to the children of the speaker and the speaker's brother.

sentence: Ana y yo ya compramos todos los ingredientes, pero eso no garantiza que el pastel salga bien; todavía tenemos que seguir la receta y cuidar el tiempo de horneado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative certainty verb under visible negation
grammar: No garantiza que denies certainty of success from an established favorable condition. Salga is subjunctive in this non-guarantee; following the recipe and attending to baking time remain pending contingencies.
register: Neutral household planning.
note: Ingredientes = ingredients; pastel = cake; salir bien = turn out well; horneado = baking. Garantizar concerns certainty of a result here, rather than a promise to perform an action.

sentence: Antes de salir de casa, me aseguré de que las ventanas estuvieran cerradas: revisé una por una y todas lo estaban.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verification verb with its governed preposition
grammar: Asegurarse de que retains de and expresses making sure through a check. Estuvieran describes the state checked before departure; the subsequent explanation confirms that every window was closed.
register: Neutral household account.
note: Revisé una por una = I checked them one by one; todas refers to the windows; lo estaban = they were closed. The pronominal verification frame differs from assuring a listener that a claim is true.

sentence: Luis practicó aquí con mi guitarra y ahora no la encuentro; no descarto que la haya guardado en su casa, pero todavía no le he preguntado.
part_of_speech: negated first-person singular present indicative possibility-retaining predicate
grammar: No descartar que retains a finite possibility rather than establishing it as true. Haya guardado concerns a possible action after Luis's practice and before the present search; inquiry remains pending.
register: Neutral consideration of an unconfirmed explanation.
note: Practicar = practice; guardar = put away here; la refers to the speaker's guitar; su casa is Luis's home; le identifies Luis as the person not yet asked.

sentence: Ana, cuando tomé ese taller de grabado, el delantal me protegió la ropa de la tinta; como amiga, te recomiendo que lleves uno mañana, aunque puedes decidirlo tú.
part_of_speech: first-person singular stem-changing present indicative advisory verb
grammar: Recomendar que supports a proposed action through the adviser's concrete experience. Lleves refers to Ana's action tomorrow; the friendship and explicit choice make this advice rather than an imposed requirement.
register: Practical recommendation from one friend to another.
note: Grabado = printmaking here; delantal = apron; tinta = ink; proteger la ropa = protect clothing; uno refers to an apron. Recomiendo has the e-to-ie present stem change.

sentence: Ayer mi tía, dueña de la máquina de coser, autorizó a Ana a que la usara mañana por la mañana; Ana todavía no decide si irá a casa de mi tía.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative permission verb
grammar: Autorizar a alguien a que introduces permission with a personal direct object and a finite authorized action. Usara concerns tomorrow's limited morning use, later than yesterday's authorization; Ana has not yet chosen to go.
register: Neutral permission within a family resource arrangement.
note: Dueña = female owner; máquina de coser = sewing machine; la refers to that machine; usara = Ana used it within the permission. Permission does not establish actual use.

sentence: Ana está cosiendo el único mantel para la cena; a mi hermano y a mí nos urge que lo termine antes de las cinco, porque a esa hora vamos a poner la mesa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive urgency verb with a clausal subject and personal indirect object
grammar: Que lo termine is the singular clausal subject of urge. Nos and a mi hermano y a mí identify the people experiencing the urgent need; this is distinct from transitive urgir a alguien a actuar.
register: Time-sensitive household coordination.
note: Mantel = tablecloth; cosiendo = sewing; lo refers to the tablecloth; poner la mesa = set the table. The stated five o'clock deadline explains the urgency.

sentence: A Ana y a mí, que organizamos la próxima reunión del club de lectura, nos interesa que los vecinos compartan recuerdos del barrio; aún no los hemos invitado y queremos reunir varias perspectivas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb with a desired-action clausal subject and dative experiencers
grammar: Que los vecinos compartan recuerdos is the singular clausal subject of interesa; Ana and the speaker are the interested experiencers. The context expresses a desired future contribution, rather than asking whether a fact is true.
register: Neutral collective cultural planning.
note: Club de lectura = reading club; recuerdos del barrio = neighborhood memories; perspectivas = perspectives. Nos interesa que describes what the organizers want to encourage; the neighbors have not yet been invited.

sentence: El encargado empujó a mi hermana para pasar porque el local estaba lleno; esa dificultad no justifica que la tratara así.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative normative verb under visible negation
grammar: No justificar que denies that an acknowledged difficulty makes established conduct acceptable. Tratara is factual subjunctive; the speaker distinguishes a causal explanation from normative justification.
register: Firm criticism of unfair interpersonal treatment.
note: Encargado = man in charge; empujar = push; local lleno = crowded premises; esa dificultad refers to the crowding; la and tratara así refer to the sister and the actual pushing.

sentence: Después de comparar los dos cuentos, Ana y Luis convinieron en que el segundo tenía un final más claro: ambos podían explicar qué pasaba con cada personaje.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative agreement verb with its governed preposition
grammar: Convenir en que expresses agreement on an asserted assessment. Ana and Luis are the agreeing subjects; tenía is indicative within their shared assessment. This intransitive agreement sense retains en.
register: Educated discussion of literary texts.
note: El segundo refers to the second story; final más claro = clearer ending; personaje = story character. Convenir en que differs from suitability and practical advisability; a separate transitive deciding sense can take que without en.

sentence: Ayer la encargada del salón exigió que Ana y yo retiráramos nuestras cajas antes de las seis, porque otro grupo usaría el espacio a esa hora; las sacamos a las cinco y media.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite demand verb followed by a finite-clause complementizer
grammar: Exigir que introduces a required action performed by separately identified actors. Retiráramos concerns the later removal demanded yesterday; the completed five-thirty removal independently establishes compliance.
register: Firm requirement from the person responsible for a shared room.
note: Encargada = woman in charge; retirar las cajas = remove the boxes; usaría places the other group's intended use after the demand; las denotes Ana's and the speaker's boxes.

sentence: Mi compañero de departamento me dice: «Lávame también la ropa». Le contesto: «¡Ni que fuera tu empleado! Compartimos la casa y cada quien lava lo suyo».
part_of_speech: exclamatory locution introducing a dismissed supposition
grammar: Independent ni que introduces imperfect-subjunctive fuera to dismiss the supposed employee relationship as a justification for the request. The actual relationship is between housemates.
register: Colloquial, pointed refusal between housemates.
note: Lávame también la ropa = wash my clothes too; empleado = employee. The male speaker rejects the implied entitlement rather than expressing uncertainty about his actual role.

sentence: ¡Quién pudiera pasar un mes en casa de mis padres! Yo solo tengo dos días de vacaciones y ellos viven a ocho horas de aquí.
part_of_speech: accented pronoun in an independent optative exclamation
grammar: Optative quién with imperfect-subjunctive pudiera expresses the speaker's own unattained wish. It does not request another person's identity.
register: Expressive personal conversation.
note: Pasar un mes = spend a month; a ocho horas de aquí = eight hours away. The speaker's two vacation days make the desired month-long stay unavailable.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo salimos de viaje mañana; guarda nuestros boletos en una bolsa cerrada, no vaya a ser que se pierdan entre las cosas de la maleta.
part_of_speech: precautionary locution introducing an unwanted possible outcome
grammar: No vaya a ser que introduces the possible loss motivating the preventive instruction. Se pierdan has the tickets as its plural subject; the loss is not predicted as certain.
register: Familiar practical travel advice.
note: Guarda = put away safely; nuestros boletos belong to Ana and the speaker; maleta = suitcase. Vaya is part of the precautionary formula here.

sentence: Luis, yo entreno al equipo y decido quién juega el domingo. Como faltes al entrenamiento de mañana sin avisarme, le daré tu lugar a otro jugador.
part_of_speech: conditional subordinating conjunction
grammar: Conditional como with present-subjunctive faltes introduces the warned-against condition. The coach explicitly controls the ordinary consequence of allocating Luis's place to someone else.
register: Firm warning from a coach to a player addressed as tú.
note: Entrenar al equipo = coach the team; faltar al entrenamiento = miss practice; avisarme = notify me; daré tu lugar = I will give your place; jugador = player. This particular como clause is conditional.

sentence: Ana, podríamos presentar mañana nuestros cuentos al club, si es que todavía acepta textos; el aviso que vi era del mes pasado y no he preguntado si sigue abierto el plazo.
part_of_speech: conditional locution adding a reservation about its premise
grammar: Si es que qualifies the proposal by explicitly reserving whether submissions are still accepted. Indicative acepta belongs to this unverified enabling condition.
register: Tentative proposal between familiar peers.
note: Presentar cuentos = submit short stories; textos = written pieces; plazo = submission period here. The older notice supplies limited evidence, not confirmation that submissions remain open.

sentence: Mi hermana propone comprarme otro mantel por la pequeña mancha de tinta que dejó en el mío; el daño no es tan grave como para que lo reemplace.
part_of_speech: degree-consequence linking construction with a finite complement
grammar: No es tan grave como para que evaluates the stated damage as insufficient to warrant the proposed replacement. Reemplace is subjunctive; the sister is the proposed replacing actor.
register: Measured household assessment.
note: Mantel = tablecloth; tinta = ink; daño = damage; reemplazar = replace. El mío and lo identify the speaker's stained tablecloth.

sentence: Luis, como amiga te digo que más vale que recojas tu boleto antes de las seis de hoy; después cierra la taquilla y sin él no podrás entrar a la función de esta noche.
part_of_speech: finite advisory locution
grammar: Más vale que gives preventive practical advice and selects recojas for Luis's pending action. The friendship supplies the advisory relationship; no formal command authority is claimed.
register: Familiar, emphatic advice from a female friend.
note: Recoger el boleto = collect the ticket; taquilla = ticket office; función = performance. Él refers to the ticket, whose absence would prevent entry.

sentence: Mi abuela está renuente a que mi primo incluya en la exposición del barrio las fotos de cuando ella era niña, porque son recuerdos privados; él se lo propuso ayer y ella aún no le da una respuesta definitiva.
part_of_speech: singular adjective governing a
grammar: Renuente a que expresses reluctance to accept another person's proposed action. The governed a remains before que; incluya is subjunctive, and the decision is still pending.
register: Neutral account of a family proposal.
note: Exposición = exhibition; recuerdos privados = private memories; respuesta definitiva = final answer. Ella denotes the grandmother, and él denotes the cousin.

sentence: Como integrante del club de lectura, soy partidario de que cada vecino elija el cuento que va a compartir, porque así tendremos distintas perspectivas; solo pido que la lectura de cada cuento dure como máximo diez minutos.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective governing de
grammar: Ser partidario de que expresses support for a proposal, retaining de before subjunctive elija. The speaker's support is bounded by an explicit maximum duration for reading each story.
register: Educated discussion within a reading club.
note: Integrante = member; elija = choose; perspectivas = perspectives; como máximo = at most. La lectura de cada cuento is the subject of dure; the ten-minute limit applies to each reading.

sentence: Luis, compartimos departamento, pero esta guitarra es mía; propones llevarla al ensayo de mañana para que todos los de tu grupo la usen y no estoy dispuesto a que la prestes sin consultarme.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective with its governed preposition and finite complementizer
grammar: No estar dispuesto a que sets a boundary on another actor's action. Luis would lend the guitar; the speaker is its owner and withholds willingness to allow that loan without consultation.
register: Firm boundary between housemates addressed as tú.
note: Ensayo = rehearsal; prestar = lend; consultarme = consult me. La refers throughout to the speaker's guitar.

sentence: Mi papá no abandona su empeño en que mi hermano participe en la comida familiar del domingo: lo ha invitado tres veces, aunque mi hermano dice que tiene mucho trabajo y todavía no decide si irá.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun governing en
grammar: Empeño en que names persistent insistence on another person's desired action. En remains before subjunctive participe; the repeated invitations do not establish eventual attendance.
register: Neutral family account with an insistent invitation.
note: No abandona = does not give up; lo refers to the brother; participe = take part. The work constraint is the brother's stated obstacle.

sentence: El lunes, mi hermana tenía la esperanza de que su maestra leyera su cuento antes del taller del viernes; hoy sábado sabemos que lo leyó antes del taller, porque el jueves se lo devolvió con comentarios.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun governing de
grammar: Esperanza de que names a hoped-for finite outcome and retains de. Leyera was prospective from Monday's hope. Thursday's return of the commented text establishes reading before Friday's workshop without specifying the exact reading day.
register: Neutral account of a learning activity.
note: Taller = workshop; comentarios = comments. Su maestra is the sister's teacher; su cuento and lo identify the sister's story. Se lo devolvió = the teacher returned the story to the sister.

sentence: La función está programada al aire libre, pero hay posibilidad de que la traslademos al salón si el patio sigue mojado; hoy revisaremos el piso y también podemos mantenerla afuera si ya está seco.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun governing de
grammar: Posibilidad de que packages a bounded possible outcome, retaining de before subjunctive traslademos. Moving indoors and remaining outside are both available; neither is presented as the desired or certain result.
register: Neutral cultural-event planning.
note: Al aire libre = outdoors; trasladar = move to another location; la refers to the performance. The floor inspection remains pending.

sentence: Ayer mi tía, dueña del patio, puso como condición que Ana y yo retiráramos las mesas antes de las ocho para prestárnoslo durante la comida; aceptamos el acuerdo y sacamos todo a las siete y media.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun in poner como condición que
grammar: Poner como condición que states the required term of the aunt's limited loan. Retiráramos identifies Ana and the speaker as the required actors; the seven-thirty removal confirms fulfillment.
register: Explicit family agreement about a shared resource.
note: Dueña = female owner; retirar las mesas = remove the tables; prestárnoslo = lend the patio to Ana and the speaker.

sentence: Como maestra del taller de cuento, aspiro a que mis alumnos publiquen juntos una colección al terminar el año; llevamos meses revisando sus textos, pero todavía no tenemos una versión final.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative verb governing a
grammar: Aspirar a que directs an ambition toward another explicit group's finite result. A remains before subjunctive publiquen; the sustained preparation does not establish publication.
register: Educated statement of a teacher's cultural goal.
note: Taller de cuento = short-story workshop; colección = collection; versión final = final version. Sus textos are the students' pieces.

sentence: Mi tía se empeña en que yo toque el piano en la reunión del sábado: me lo pide cada vez que hablamos, aunque ya le dije que prefiero asistir sin presentarme y todavía no he aceptado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative pronominal verb
grammar: Empeñarse en que identifies the aunt as the persistent actor and retains en before subjunctive toque. The speaker's stated preference and nonacceptance keep insistence separate from compliance.
register: Personal account of an insistent family request.
note: Tocar el piano = play the piano; presentarme = perform here; me lo pide refers to asking the speaker to play.

sentence: La dueña de la librería se resiste a que su socio quite las sillas del rincón de lectura: hoy le entregó una propuesta para conservarlas y pidió discutirla antes de mover nada; aún no hay acuerdo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative pronominal verb
grammar: Resistirse a que expresses active resistance to another person's proposed change. A remains before subjunctive quite; the counterproposal and requested discussion supply actual opposition behavior.
register: Neutral account of a workplace disagreement.
note: Librería = bookstore; socio = business partner; rincón de lectura = reading corner; conservarlas = keep the chairs.

sentence: Ayer la maestra pretendía que todos los alumnos compararan dos finales del cuento durante la clase; repartió ambos textos, pero se fue la luz y solo alcanzaron a leer el primero.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect indicative intention verb
grammar: Pretender que expresses the teacher's intended effect on the students' activity. Compararan is prospective within yesterday's intention; the separately reported interruption establishes nonfulfillment.
register: Neutral account of a literature class.
note: Comparar dos finales = compare two endings; se fue la luz = the power went out; alcanzaron a leer = managed to read. Pretender does not mean feign here.

sentence: Como encargado de la comida del barrio, procuro que cada vecino reciba una porción: preparo una lista y separo los platos, aunque todavía pueden llegar personas que no avisaron.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative intentional verb
grammar: Procurar que expresses practical care directed toward a finite outcome. Reciba is subjunctive; the list and separated plates show effort, while possible unannounced arrivals preserve contingency.
register: Practical community coordination.
note: Encargado = man responsible; porción = portion; separo los platos = set the plates aside. The intended recipients are the neighbors.

sentence: El reparto de tareas que acordamos para la visita infantil a la biblioteca consiste en que yo entregue los libros a los niños y Ana organice los juegos.
meaning: in that (introducing what it consists of)
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a finite complementizer
grammar: Consistir retains en before que when its content is expressed through finite clauses. Yo is the subject of entregue, and Ana is the subject of organice. The subjunctives describe the agreed tasks rather than completed actions.
register: Neutral explanation of agreed responsibilities in a cultural activity.
note: Reparto de tareas = division of tasks; acordamos = we agreed on; entregue = I hand out; organice = Ana organize. The clauses after en que spell out who performs each agreed task.

sentence: Hoy, 14 de mayo, cuento que el 12 Clara me dijo que había terminado de coser el vestido el 11; no he visto el vestido ni comprobado esa fecha.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pluperfect indicative auxiliary
grammar: Había terminado marks completion on May 11 before Clara's May 12 assertion, retold on May 14. Había is an auxiliary before a participle, rather than existential haber.
register: Neutral retelling with an explicit evidence limit.
note: Había terminado de coser = she had finished sewing; vestido = dress. Clara supplies the completion claim; the narrator has not verified the object or date.

sentence: Hoy, 8 de junio, recuerdo que el día 5 Elena prometió que para el 7 a las seis ya habría terminado de pintar el mural; yo estuve allí el 7 a las siete y aún quedaba una sección sin pintar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular conditional perfect auxiliary with temporal future-in-the-past reference
grammar: Habría terminado reports promised completion by a deadline later than the June 5 promise. The June 7 observation independently establishes that the promised deadline was missed.
register: Neutral account separating commitment from fulfillment.
note: Mural = mural painting; sección sin pintar = unpainted section. This conditional perfect expresses completion viewed from an earlier promise.

sentence: Hoy miércoles, Pablo sostiene que la función del lunes empezó a las ocho, aunque Eva le recuerda que ella llegó a las ocho y media y aún estaban acomodando las sillas; yo no asistí y no puedo resolver la diferencia.
part_of_speech: third-person singular stem-changing present indicative reporting verb
grammar: Sostener que means maintaining an assertion across a stated challenge. Indicative empezó gives Pablo's asserted content; firmness does not independently establish its truth.
register: Educated discussion of conflicting event accounts.
note: Acomodar las sillas = arrange the chairs; resolver la diferencia = settle the discrepancy. Eva's recollection challenges Pablo's time claim.

sentence: Hoy lunes, Iván explicó por qué no vino a mi cumpleaños el sábado: alegó que tuvo que cuidar a su sobrino durante la fiesta; esa fue su razón, pero yo no he hablado con su familia para comprobarla.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reporting verb
grammar: Alegar que advances an attributed reason for conduct. The claimed care obligation coincides with Saturday's party; the explanation is given Monday and remains unverified by the narrator.
register: Neutral account of a social explanation.
note: Sobrino = nephew; tuvo que cuidar = had to look after. Comprobarla refers to checking Iván's stated reason.

sentence: En la reunión de ayer, Laura dijo que el precio del taller incluía materiales; luego precisó que cada participante recibiría dos pinceles y una hoja de papel, aunque yo todavía no he visto los paquetes.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reporting verb
grammar: Precisar que adds exact detail to Laura's broader materials statement. Recibiría places distribution after yesterday's statement; the participants and included-materials claim remain the same.
register: Neutral explanation of workshop arrangements.
note: Pinceles = paintbrushes; hoja de papel = sheet of paper; paquetes = packets. The later statement specifies contents rather than correcting an earlier false quantity.

sentence: Ayer la organizadora anunció que la entrada a la convivencia sería gratis; cuando Luis preguntó si eso incluía la comida, ella puntualizó que solo hablaba del acceso y que cada quien pagaría lo que consumiera.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative clarifying reporting verb
grammar: Puntualizar que supplies a limited clarification blocking the proposed inference that free entry includes food. The original free-access claim remains intact.
register: Explicit clarification in an ordinary group event.
note: Convivencia = social gathering here; acceso = admission; consumir = order and consume food or drinks here. Sería and pagaría preserve the future perspective of yesterday's announcement.

sentence: Marta dijo ayer que el cuento era fácil de seguir; después matizó que eso era cierto hasta el último capítulo, donde los cambios de narrador la confundían; yo todavía no he leído el texto.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reporting verb
grammar: Matizar que qualifies the scope of Marta's earlier assessment while retaining its validity for the story before the final chapter. The narrator has not independently read the text.
register: Educated literary discussion.
note: Fácil de seguir = easy to follow; capítulo = chapter; narrador = narrator; la refers to Marta as the person confused.

sentence: Ayer el coordinador dijo que la caminata del domingo era voluntaria; cuando Ana preguntó si faltar tendría alguna consecuencia, él recalcó que nadie estaba obligado a ir, y yo solo transmito su aviso.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reporting verb
grammar: Recalcar que reports renewed emphasis on the previously stated voluntary character. Ana's question motivates the emphasis; repetition is not independent verification.
register: Neutral account of a group organizer's clarification.
note: Caminata = organized walk; voluntaria = voluntary; nadie estaba obligado a ir = nobody was required to go. The narrator identifies the organizer as the source.

sentence: Hoy martes, Inés rectificó lo que anunció ayer: el ensayo será el jueves, no el miércoles; consultó el programa que ya estaba impreso el lunes, y yo también leí allí la fecha del jueves.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reporting predicate
grammar: Rectificar corrects an earlier announced proposition rather than an entry in a written quantity record. The already-printed program supports Thursday as the correction, independently read by the narrator.
register: Neutral correction of an event announcement.
note: Ensayo = rehearsal; programa = event program; impreso = printed. Inés made both the original announcement and the correction.

sentence: Hoy viernes, Rosa contó que el jueves se retractó de haber dicho el miércoles que Leo rompió el florero del salón; reconoció que no tenía pruebas y todavía no sabemos cómo se rompió.
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a perfect-infinitive auxiliary
grammar: Retractarse retains de before perfect-infinitive haber dicho. Rosa's Wednesday statement precedes her Thursday withdrawal, reported Friday; withdrawal does not prove that Leo was uninvolved.
register: Careful report of withdrawing an unsupported assertion.
note: Florero = vase; pruebas = evidence. Rosa is the understood subject of haber dicho as well as the person who withdrew the earlier assertion.

sentence: Luis afirmó el domingo que Ana estuvo en el huerto el sábado; hoy lunes Elena informó que corroboró que Ana estuvo allí al comparar una lista de asistencia con una foto fechada, pero yo solo revisé la lista.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative confirmation verb in an attributed report
grammar: Corroborar que reports confirmation of Luis's earlier assertion about Ana through additional evidence. Elena claims the comparison; the narrator explicitly inspected only the attendance list.
register: Careful community-event reporting.
note: Huerto = vegetable garden; lista de asistencia = attendance list; foto fechada = dated photograph. Ana is the person whose Saturday presence Elena reports corroborating.

sentence: Hoy lunes, Nora refutó la afirmación de Luis de que nadie entró al huerto el sábado: mostró un video grabado ese sábado en el que se ve a Ana entrar al huerto, y yo también vi esa escena.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb with an explicit claim as direct object
grammar: Refutar takes la afirmación as its direct object. The video shows an entry on the Saturday concerned, countering the specific assertion that nobody entered that day. It does not disprove every assertion made by Luis.
register: Evidence-based account of an ordinary disagreement.
note: Grabado ese sábado = recorded that Saturday; se ve a Ana entrar = Ana is shown entering. The narrator independently saw the counterexample scene.

sentence: Ayer miércoles, Beatriz pidió posponer el ensayo y adujo que tres músicos estaban de viaje y regresarían el viernes; hoy jueves repito su explicación, pero no he hablado con ellos para comprobar sus fechas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular preterite indicative reporting verb
grammar: Aducir que puts forward an attributed reason for the postponement request. The musicians' claimed travel was simultaneous with Wednesday's explanation, and their Friday return was still future.
register: Educated report of a rehearsal discussion.
note: Adujo has the irregular preterite stem aduj-; músicos = musicians; regresarían = would return. Ellos identifies the three musicians.

sentence: Con base en las dos sillas que reparó el lunes, Raúl estimó ese día que terminaría las otras cuatro el jueves; hoy martes sigue trabajando y la fecha aún es aproximada.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative approximate-forecast verb
grammar: Estimar que reports an approximate completion forecast based on prior repair experience. Terminaría is future from Monday; Tuesday's update preserves uncertainty about Thursday.
register: Neutral practical work estimate.
note: Con base en = based on; las otras cuatro = the other four chairs; fecha aproximada = approximate date. Estimar does not express personal affection here.

sentence: El lunes, la organizadora pronosticó que unas cincuenta personas asistirían a la función del sábado porque ya había cuarenta reservas; hoy domingo cuento que yo conté treinta y cinco asistentes cuando terminó de entrar el público.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative prediction verb
grammar: Pronosticar que reports Monday's attendance prediction for Saturday. The approximately fifty forecast, reservation basis, and independently counted thirty-five attendees remain distinct.
register: Neutral retrospective cultural-event report.
note: Reservas = reservations; asistentes = attendees; público = audience. Cuando terminó de entrar el público = once the audience had finished coming in. A forecast is not a guarantee.

sentence: En el ensayo de ayer, el director comentó: «Con otra voz, esta canción luciría más». Según entendí yo, insinuó que prefería cambiar de cantante, pero no anunció ningún cambio ni confirmó esa intención.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative indirect-communication verb
grammar: Insinuar que attributes an indirectly communicated preference. The original remark supports the narrator's interpretation, explicitly marked as such; no actual change or confirmed intention is asserted.
register: Careful interpretation of an artistic discussion.
note: Luciría más = would come across better here; cantante = singer; según entendí yo = as I understood it. The statement concerns yesterday's rehearsal.

sentence: El lunes, en la reunión del barrio, mi vecina Eva manifestó que ayudaría a pintar el mural el sábado: «Cuenten conmigo para pintar ese día»; hoy domingo cuento que sí vino y pintó una sección.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative expression-reporting verb
grammar: Manifestar que reports Eva's explicit expression of commitment. Ayudaría preserves Saturday as future from Monday; Sunday's narrator separately confirms her actual help.
register: Educated retelling of an ordinary neighborhood commitment.
note: Cuenten conmigo = count on me, addressed to the group; ese día identifies Saturday; sección = section.

sentence: El lunes, en la reunión del coro, Mario declaró ante los cantantes que no participaría en la función del sábado, aunque seguiría asistiendo a los ensayos; hoy domingo confirmo que faltó a la función, pero lo vi ensayar el viernes.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative position-announcing verb
grammar: Declarar que makes Mario's position explicit to the identified choir audience. His nonparticipation concerns Saturday's performance, while continuing rehearsals remains a separate commitment.
register: Explicit statement to an ordinary cultural group.
note: Coro = choir; ante los cantantes = before the singers; seguiría asistiendo = would continue attending. The narrator separately reports Friday's rehearsal and Saturday's absence.

sentence: Hoy Lucía atestiguó que Tomás devolvió la guitarra al armario durante el ensayo de ayer: dijo que estaba sentada junto a la puerta y que vio cómo Tomás guardó allí la guitarra; yo no estaba en el ensayo y no he revisado ninguna otra evidencia.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative witness-reporting verb
grammar: Here atestiguar que presents Lucía's report as grounded in her claimed observation of Tomás putting the guitar away. The narrator was absent and has no independent verification; Lucía's eyewitness claim is not presented as infallible.
register: Careful, somewhat formal account outside a legal setting.
note: Armario = cupboard; allí = in that cupboard. Lucía is the seated observer, and Tomás puts the guitar away. Vio cómo describes seeing the action.

sentence: Hoy domingo, mi abuelo relató que el sábado leyó con su hermana las cartas que había encontrado el viernes en un cajón; yo no estuve con ellos y todavía no he visto las cartas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative narrative-reporting verb
grammar: Relatar que reports the grandfather's narrated sequence. Había encontrado places Friday's discovery before Saturday's shared reading, both earlier than Sunday's retelling; no additional causal claim is required.
register: Neutral family narrative.
note: Cartas = letters; cajón = drawer; su hermana is the grandfather's sister; ellos identifies those two readers. The narrator has not seen the letters.

sentence: Hoy domingo comparo los relatos de mis amigos Rosa e Iván sobre la fiesta del viernes: a decir de Rosa, que me lo contó ayer sábado, tocaron tres grupos; Iván me habló hoy de dos, y yo no estuve allí.
part_of_speech: prepositional locution attributing a claim to a named source
grammar: A decir de Rosa attributes the three-group count to Rosa. Her Saturday account concerns Friday's party; Sunday's narrator has a different count from Iván and no firsthand observation.
register: Educated conversational source comparison.
note: Tocaron tres grupos = three musical groups performed. Attribution identifies whose claim is being repeated without establishing which count is correct.

sentence: Hoy martes describo el ensayo del lunes en palabras de mi amiga Irene, que al salir ese día dijo: «Fue una buena prueba, aunque faltó tiempo»; reproduzco su frase exacta, pero yo no asistí.
part_of_speech: source-attributing prepositional expression introducing exact wording
grammar: En palabras de introduces Irene's exact quoted assessment. Fue and faltó concern Monday's rehearsal, while the narrator reproduces the wording Tuesday.
register: Careful quotation in a friendly cultural discussion.
note: Prueba = trial or test here; reproduzco su frase exacta = I reproduce her exact phrase. The quotation is Irene's assessment, and the narrator did not attend.

sentence: El lunes, Sofía nos dijo en la comida: «Tal vez vaya al paseo del sábado»; hoy martes, ante nuestros amigos, Bruno lo cuenta como una asistencia segura, pero yo repito su frase textualmente: «Tal vez vaya al paseo del sábado»; Sofía todavía no decide.
part_of_speech: adverb of exact-word reproduction
grammar: Textualmente marks reproduction of the original wording, including tal vez. Bruno's definite-attendance retelling removes that qualification; the exact repetition does not establish attendance.
register: Ordinary correction during a conversation among friends.
note: Asistencia segura = definite attendance; ante nuestros amigos = in front of our friends. Sofía's original uncertainty remains present in the repeated quotation.

sentence: El lunes, mi hermana Nina dijo: «Quizá done cien pesos al coro este viernes»; hoy martes, nuestro amigo Mateo parafraseó su comentario así: «Es posible que Nina aporte cien pesos al coro este viernes»; Nina aún no decide.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reformulation verb
grammar: Parafrasear restates content in different words. Mateo preserves Nina as the possible donor, the choir as beneficiary, one hundred pesos, Friday, and the unresolved decision.
register: Neutral reformulation among relatives and friends.
note: Done = donates within the tentative statement; coro = choir; aporte = contributes. Both quoted formulations retain possibility rather than a commitment.

sentence: El lunes, mi hermana Lucía me dijo: «Puedo cuidar a tu hijo el viernes solo de seis a siete»; hoy martes, mi primo Raúl tergiversó su oferta al decirme que Lucía podía cuidarlo todo el viernes.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb taking an attributed offer as direct object
grammar: Tergiversar identifies a concrete change in the offer's scope: one hour becomes all Friday. The sentence establishes the distortion without specifying whether Raúl intended it.
register: Neutral identification of a misleading family retelling.
note: Oferta = offer; cuidarlo = look after the narrator's son. Solo de seis a siete limits Lucía's offer to one hour.

sentence: El lunes, nuestro maestro de guitarra, Iván, dijo: «Este ejercicio es sencillo si ya conocen los acordes»; hoy martes, Sara descontextualizó la frase al repetir solo «Este ejercicio es sencillo» y decir que no hacía falta conocer los acordes.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb
grammar: Descontextualizar identifies removing the if-clause and using the shortened quotation to support a broader conclusion. Iván's conditional assessment does not establish whether chord knowledge is necessary or how difficult the exercise is without it.
register: Careful correction of a classroom retelling.
note: Acordes = musical chords; sencillo = straightforward. No hacía falta conocer los acordes = knowing the chords was unnecessary, as Sara claimed. The sentence identifies an unsupported extension of the quotation without alleging deliberate deception.

sentence: El lunes, nuestra vecina Noelia dijo: «El sábado prestaré mis herramientas solo a los vecinos de esta calle»; hoy martes, Raúl omitió esa limitación al contarme que Noelia prestaría sus herramientas el sábado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb with a qualification as direct object
grammar: Omitir identifies the missing recipient restriction. Raúl retains Noelia, the tools, and Saturday, but leaves out which neighbors qualify; intention is not specified.
register: Neutral account of an incomplete neighborhood message.
note: Herramientas = tools; limitación = restriction. The omitted information is solo a los vecinos de esta calle.

sentence: El lunes, mi amiga Sara escribió en su cuaderno: «El silencio también acompaña»; hoy martes, con su permiso, Hugo citó esa frase ante nuestro club de lectura: «El silencio también acompaña»; yo no comparto del todo esa idea.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative quotation verb
grammar: Citar means reproducing Sara's wording as a quotation for the reading club. It does not mean arranging an appointment or summoning someone in this context.
register: Ordinary discussion in a reading club.
note: Cuaderno = notebook; ante nuestro club = before our club; no comparto del todo esa idea = I do not entirely share that view. The quoted line is attributed to Sara.

sentence: En nuestra comida familiar del domingo se quemó el pastel y la cocina olía a quemado; hoy lunes mi hermano Leo aludió a ese incidente al proponer cocinar con tiempo: «No quiero otro final con olor a quemado».
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb with its governed preposition a
grammar: Aludir a introduces an indirect reference to the recoverable earlier incident. Leo's later remark recalls the burnt ending without directly naming the cake.
register: Ordinary family reference to a shared mishap.
note: Olía a quemado = smelled burnt; cocinar con tiempo = allow enough time for cooking. The preposition a belongs to the selected aludir frame.

sentence: El lunes, Luis escribió en una nota: «Traje cuatro mesas para el taller»; hoy jueves le digo a mi hermana: «Ana, remítete a esa nota para saber cuántas mesas dijo Luis que llevó; la nota no dice quién las recibió».
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative of pronominal remitirse with attached te and governed a
grammar: Remitirse a directs Ana to the earlier written account as an information source. The imperative remítete carries the pronominal te and an accent; the note reports a quantity but no recipient.
register: Careful practical direction between siblings.
note: Taller = workshop; remítete a esa nota = refer to that note. Las refers to the four tables, and the note does not establish who received them.

sentence: Ayer domingo, mi abuela evocó la comida de su boda de 1970 al oler canela: «Aquel día también olía así la casa»; hoy lunes cuento su recuerdo, sin poder comprobar cómo olía entonces.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative memory-evoking verb
grammar: Evocar brings an earlier occasion into the remembered account. The cinnamon triggers the grandmother's recollection Sunday; Monday's narrator cannot independently verify the remembered smell.
register: Neutral family reminiscence.
note: Boda = wedding; canela = cinnamon; al oler = on smelling. Aquel día refers to the grandmother's wedding day in 1970.

sentence: El lunes, Pilar explicó: «Quizá lleve dos manteles a la comida del viernes; son de algodón y todavía tengo que lavarlos»; hoy martes, esta síntesis conserva su propuesta sin los detalles de la tela y el lavado: «Tal vez Pilar lleve dos manteles a la comida del viernes».
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun naming a compact account
grammar: Síntesis names the compact account. The summary preserves Pilar, two tablecloths, Friday's meal, and uncertainty while omitting fabric and washing details.
register: Careful summarizing of a household proposal.
note: Manteles = tablecloths; algodón = cotton; tela = fabric; lavado = washing. Síntesis is feminine and retains its written accent.

sentence: El domingo, Mar me dijo que el sábado vio dos clientes en la panadería a las nueve; Beto me contó ese domingo que vio cinco allí a las diez de ese sábado. Hoy lunes voy a contrastar sus relatos: ambos describen presencia de clientes, pero las cifras corresponden a horas distintas.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb taking two attributed accounts as its object
grammar: Contrastar compares what the accounts actually cover. Both describe customers, but the counts concern different hours and therefore need not conflict.
register: Neutral comparison of ordinary observations.
note: Panadería = bakery; cifras = numerical figures; relatos = accounts. Allí identifies the bakery, and both observations concern the same Saturday.

sentence: Hoy domingo, mis compañeros del coro Clara y Óscar coinciden en que la letra se entendió en el concierto de ayer; discrepan sobre el ritmo, que Clara consideró lento y Óscar adecuado; yo no asistí.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative agreement verb with governed en and complementizer que
grammar: Coincidir en que introduces the assessment Clara and Óscar share. Indicative se entendió presents their agreed assessment, while their different rhythm judgments and the narrator's absence remain explicit.
register: Neutral discussion among choir members.
note: Letra = song lyrics; ritmo = rhythm or pace; adecuado = appropriate. Agreement between the two participants does not independently verify the assessment.

sentence: Hoy domingo, Luis discrepa de la valoración que Nora hizo esta mañana sobre la función de ayer: ambos vieron que duró dos horas, pero Nora la consideró demasiado larga y Luis cree que esa duración fue adecuada.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative disagreement verb with governed de
grammar: Discrepar de introduces the particular assessment Luis disputes. Both participants accept the two-hour duration, but they evaluate it differently; de precedes the assessment rather than a person.
register: Educated discussion of a performance.
note: Valoración = assessment; función = performance; adecuada = appropriate. Discrepar can take other complements in other constructions; this card selects de with the disputed assessment.

sentence: Hoy martes, Rosa contradijo el relato que Tomás dio ayer sobre la cena del domingo: él dijo que Ana llegó antes de las ocho y ella afirmó que Ana llegó después de las ocho; yo no vi la llegada.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular preterite indicative reporting verb
grammar: Contradecir identifies incompatible claims about Ana's same Sunday arrival relative to eight o'clock. Contradijo has the irregular preterite pattern of decir; the narrator does not establish which claim is true.
register: Neutral account of conflicting personal reports.
note: Él refers to Tomás; ella refers to Rosa. Before eight and after eight cannot both describe the same arrival.

sentence: El lunes, mi hermana Sara confesó que el domingo se comió el último pedazo de pastel, reservado para mamá, y que hasta ese momento nos lo había ocultado; hoy martes repito su admisión, aunque yo no la vi comerlo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb acknowledging concealed personal conduct
grammar: Confesar que acknowledges Sara's own previously concealed action. Sunday's eating precedes Monday's confession and Tuesday's retelling; the narrator reports her admission without claiming to have seen the eating.
register: Ordinary personal admission within a family.
note: Reservado para mamá = set aside for the narrator's mother; hasta ese momento = until the confession; nos lo había ocultado = she had concealed it from us.

sentence: El lunes, mi primo Hugo se jactó de haber arreglado él solo la bicicleta el domingo: «¡Soy un maestro, la dejé como nueva!»; hoy martes cuento su alarde, pero no he probado la bicicleta.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb with governed de
grammar: Jactarse de introduces Hugo's self-praising claim about his own earlier repair. Haber arreglado places the claimed repair Sunday before Monday's boast; the narrator has not tested its success.
register: Neutral reporting of conspicuous self-praise.
note: Él solo = by himself; alarde = boast; la dejé como nueva = I left it like new. The praise and repair claim belong to Hugo.

sentence: El lunes, Óscar dijo: «No saqué la guitarra del salón el domingo»; hoy martes cuento que Óscar negó haber sacado la guitarra ese domingo, pero nadie ha comprobado dónde estuvo el instrumento.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite denial verb followed by the perfect-infinitive auxiliary
grammar: Negar selects haber sacado as the denied prior action, with Óscar understood as both the denier and the person who allegedly took out the guitar. The denial does not establish the action's truth or falsity.
register: Neutral report of an unresolved personal denial.
note: Sacado = taken out; ese domingo identifies the Sunday before Monday's denial; instrumento refers to the guitar. No de is added before haber.

sentence: El lunes, Elena me dijo: «El domingo usé tu mantel sin tu permiso, pero no lo manché»; hoy martes cuento que admitió haber usado mi mantel sin permiso, manteniendo su afirmación de que no lo manchó; yo aún no lo he revisado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite acknowledgment verb followed by the perfect-infinitive auxiliary
grammar: Admitir selects haber usado for Elena's acknowledgment of her own prior action. Elena explicitly addresses the narrator, so quoted tu becomes mi in the retelling. Her acknowledgment of unauthorized use and her unverified no-stain qualification remain distinct.
register: Neutral acknowledgment of an inconvenient household action.
note: Mantel = tablecloth; manchar = stain; manteniendo su afirmación = retaining her assertion. Sin tu permiso explicitly states the absence of authorization; the item's condition has not been checked.

sentence: El domingo el pan de mi tío quedó plano; el lunes él atribuyó ese resultado a que usó muy poca levadura; hoy martes repito su explicación, pero no revisé las cantidades ni sé si hubo otra causa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative causal-attribution verb
grammar: Atribuir un resultado a que assigns the result to an asserted explanation. Indicative usó represents the uncle's causal account; the narrator has neither checked the quantities nor excluded other causes.
register: Neutral household explanation.
note: Quedó plano = turned out flat; levadura = yeast. This use assigns a proposed cause rather than identifying the speaker of some words.

sentence: Ayer lunes, al comentar la propuesta de repetir la comida en el patio, mi vecina Elena señaló que allí solo caben seis sillas; hoy martes repito esa observación, pero todavía no he medido el espacio.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reporting verb with a finite que complement
grammar: Señalar que draws attention to a relevant asserted capacity limit. Elena's observation bears on the patio proposal; the narrator has not independently measured the space.
register: Neutral contribution to a neighborhood proposal.
note: Caben seis sillas = six chairs fit; medir = measure; observación = remark or observation. Señalar does not describe spatial pointing here.

sentence: Ayer lunes, después del primer ensayo de la canción, nuestra compañera Julia apuntó que una pausa antes del final podría ayudar a entender la letra; hoy martes repito esa observación provisional sin haber probado aún el cambio.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb introducing a tentative observation
grammar: Apuntar que introduces Julia's preliminary verbal observation. Podría preserves the suggested benefit as a possibility, and the change remains untested despite the indicative reporting frame.
register: Educated discussion during a shared musical activity.
note: Letra = lyrics; provisional = preliminary; sin haber probado = without having tested. Apuntar does not mean signing up or writing down here.

sentence: El lunes, Paula contó doce sillas y catorce invitados confirmados para la cena del martes; concluyó que harían falta dos sillas más para sentar a todos. Hoy miércoles confirmo que llegaron los catorce y hubo que traer dos sillas más.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative inference verb
grammar: Concluir que introduces Paula's conclusion from the stated chair and guest counts. Monday's inference concerns Tuesday's seating need; Wednesday's narrator separately confirms what happened.
register: Neutral practical reasoning for a shared meal.
note: Invitados confirmados = confirmed guests; sentar a todos = seat everyone; harían falta = would be needed. Concluyó uses y in this third-person preterite.

sentence: El lunes, Iván sabía que su hermana Paula solo podía viajar el martes o el jueves; al recibir de ella el mensaje «El martes trabajo todo el día y no puedo salir», dedujo que viajaría el jueves si mantenía el viaje; hoy miércoles Paula todavía no confirma la fecha.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular preterite indicative inference verb
grammar: Deducir que derives the remaining day from two stated options and Paula's exclusion of Tuesday. Si mantenía el viaje limits the inference: Thursday follows only if the trip remains planned.
register: Neutral reasoning about a family travel plan.
note: Mantenía el viaje = kept the trip planned; dedujo has the irregular preterite stem deduj-. The inference does not establish that Paula will travel.

sentence: El lunes, Leo infirió que Marta estaba en casa porque vio desde la calle la lámpara de la sala de Marta encendida; hoy martes me cuenta esa interpretación y aclara que alguien más pudo encenderla: no vio a Marta.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative inference verb
grammar: Inferir que presents the light in Marta's living room as indirect evidence for her presence. The alternative person who might have switched it on remains explicit, so the sign is not treated as proof.
register: Careful account of an everyday inference.
note: Sala = living room; lámpara encendida = light switched on; interpretación = interpretation; encenderla = switch that lamp on. Infirió has the third-person preterite stem change e to i.

sentence: El lunes, al ver dos tazas usadas, Laura presumió que Lucía, su hermana, había recibido una visita esa mañana; hoy martes me cuenta su suposición y aclara que Lucía pudo usar las dos sin recibir a nadie, así que no lo sabe.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative assumption verb
grammar: Presumir que means suppose on a limited basis here. The used cups support Laura's assumption but also allow the explicitly stated alternative; the verb does not report boasting.
register: Educated everyday account of an unverified assumption.
note: Tazas usadas = used cups; suposición = assumption; había recibido = had received. Lucía is the possible host and the person who might instead have used both cups.

sentence: Por lo que mi amiga Eva me dijo el lunes, hoy jueves tengo entendido que el taller de cerámica del sábado empieza a las diez; aún no he visto el aviso actualizado y no sé si cambiaron la hora.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative construction with invariant predicative participle entendido
grammar: Tener entendido que presents an understanding acquired from an earlier source. The narrator identifies Eva's Monday information and leaves the current Saturday schedule unverified.
register: Neutral qualified statement based on received information.
note: Taller de cerámica = pottery workshop; aviso actualizado = updated notice. Tengo entendido marks the status of the information rather than direct checking.

sentence: El lunes, Inés vio tres macetas nuevas en el patio de su vecino y pensó que él empezaría un huerto; hoy martes me cuenta esa conjetura, pero solo comprobó la presencia de las macetas y aún no le ha preguntado por sus planes.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun naming an unconfirmed inference
grammar: Conjetura names the proposed garden plan inferred from the pots. The observed pots and the neighbor's unconfirmed intention remain separate.
register: Neutral discussion of a neighbor's possible plans.
note: Macetas = plant pots; huerto = vegetable garden; él and le refer to the neighbor. Inés has checked the pots' presence but has not asked about the plan.

sentence: En una nota fechada el lunes 8, Sara dejó constancia de que ayudaría a su vecina Julia a pintar el viernes 12, solo por la mañana; hoy jueves 11 he leído la nota, pero no sé si Sara cumplirá.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite verb-noun recording construction with governed de
grammar: Dejar constancia de que records the statement explicitly. The dated note establishes the recorded morning-only undertaking, while Friday's actual help remains future and unverified Thursday.
register: Careful written record of an ordinary neighborly undertaking.
note: Fechada = bearing a date; cumplir = fulfill the undertaking. Julia is the intended beneficiary, and solo por la mañana limits Sara's stated help.

sentence: El lunes, mi vecino aseguró que ya había devuelto las dos sillas al salón; hoy martes fui allí, comparé las etiquetas con mi lista y pude constatar que las dos sillas estaban en el salón, aunque no vi quién las llevó ni cuándo.
part_of_speech: infinitive verification verb governing a finite que clause
grammar: Constatar que establishes the observable Tuesday location through the narrator's own comparison of labels and list. It does not establish who transported the chairs or when.
register: Neutral practical verification.
note: Etiquetas = labels; comparé = I compared; allí = in the shared room. The narrator directly checks the two chairs' presence after hearing the neighbor's earlier assertion.

sentence: El lunes, mi padre dijo: «El domingo guardé las semillas en el cajón; todavía lo recuerdo»; hoy martes cuento que recordaba haber guardado las semillas allí, aunque yo no lo vi hacerlo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect indicative memory verb followed by the perfect-infinitive auxiliary
grammar: Recordar haber guardado recalls the subject's own completed prior action. The father's Sunday storage precedes Monday's retained memory and Tuesday's retelling; this is neither a pending-task reminder nor narrator verification.
register: Neutral retelling of a family memory report.
note: Semillas = seeds; cajón = drawer; allí refers to that drawer. The father is the understood actor of both remembering and storing.

sentence: El lunes vi a Ana guardar el mantel en el cajón; el martes ella olvidó que ya lo había guardado allí y lo buscó en el tendedero; hoy miércoles lo encontró al abrir el cajón y me dijo: «Ya me acordé de que lo guardé el lunes».
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative forgetting verb with complementizer que
grammar: Olvidar que loses awareness of an established fact rather than omitting the storage action. The narrator witnessed Monday's completed storage, and Ana's Wednesday discovery and statement resolve her Tuesday memory failure.
register: Neutral household narrative.
note: Tendedero = clothesline or drying rack; lo refers to the tablecloth; allí identifies the drawer. Ya lo había guardado places the actual storage before the forgetting.

sentence: El lunes, nuestra vecina Clara devolvió mi olla y yo la recibí; hoy miércoles, mi hermano Diego me cuenta que el martes desconocía que Clara ya la había devuelto y que lo supo anoche, al leer mi mensaje.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect indicative knowledge verb with complementizer que
grammar: Desconocer que reports Diego's earlier lack of knowledge about the independently established return. His own Wednesday account identifies Tuesday's ignorance and Tuesday night's learning source; he is not denying the return.
register: Neutral family explanation of an information gap.
note: Olla = cooking pot; la refers to that pot; lo supo = learned that fact. The narrator personally received the pot Monday.

sentence: El domingo cancelé el paseo y mandé un mensaje al grupo; hoy martes, mi amiga Nora me dice: «El lunes por la mañana ignoraba que lo habías cancelado; me enteré esa noche al leer tu mensaje».
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect indicative knowledge verb with complementizer que inside direct quotation
grammar: Ignorar que means lack knowledge here. Nora explicitly reports Monday morning's nonknowledge and Monday night's discovery; the statement does not attribute deliberate disregard to her.
register: Ordinary explanation between friends.
note: Lo refers to the outing; habías cancelado addresses the narrator as tú; tu mensaje is the narrator's message. Nora is the first-person speaker of ignoraba.

sentence: Al leer el lunes un mensaje del organizador Raúl, Ana se enteró de que él canceló el sábado la función del domingo; hoy martes ella me transmite esa noticia, que yo todavía no he comprobado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb with governed de and complementizer que
