grammar: Enterarse de que marks Ana's acquisition of the information Monday from Raúl's message. Saturday's reported cancellation and Sunday's scheduled performance precede Monday's learning and Tuesday's transmission.
register: Neutral relay of cultural-event information.
note: Él refers to Raúl, and ella to Ana; transmite esa noticia = passes on that news. The narrator has not independently checked the message's claim.

sentence: El domingo le puse una funda nueva a la guitarra de mi hermana Ana; el lunes ella no notó el cambio al entrar, pero se percató de que la funda era nueva cuando vio la etiqueta; hoy martes me cuenta ese momento.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal awareness verb with governed de and complementizer que
grammar: Percatarse de que marks awareness reached through a visible clue after an initial failure to notice. The cover's newness is independently established by the narrator's Sunday action.
register: Neutral personal account of noticing a household detail.
note: Funda = protective cover or case; etiqueta = label; al entrar = on coming in. Ana is the observer who sees the label Monday.

sentence: El lunes, Eva escribió en la invitación «Comida del domingo: a las dos, en el patio»; ayer martes, mi hermano Luis reparó en que el lugar anunciado era el patio, un detalle que había pasado por alto; hoy miércoles aún no sabemos si Eva cambiará el lugar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative attention verb with governed en and complementizer que
grammar: Reparar en que means notice a detail, with en introducing its content. Luis notices what the invitation announces; the written venue is not treated as a guarantee against future changes.
register: Educated but ordinary attention to an invitation.
note: Pasar por alto un detalle = overlook a detail; lugar anunciado = announced location. Reparar does not mean fixing a broken object here.

sentence: El lunes, mi vecina Eva le hizo saber a mi hermano Luis que le prestaría dos sillas el sábado solo hasta las seis: «A esa hora las necesito de vuelta»; hoy martes Luis me cuenta el ofrecimiento, pero Eva todavía no le ha entregado las sillas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite communicative construction with infinitive saber
grammar: Hacer saber que names Eva's intentional communication to Luis. Recipient le and a mi hermano Luis identify the person informed; the limited future loan remains distinct from actual delivery.
register: Neutral communication of a bounded neighborly offer.
note: Ofrecimiento = offer; las necesito de vuelta = I need them back. Eva offers two chairs until six Saturday, and Luis relays the offer Tuesday.

sentence: El lunes, mi amiga Alma me dijo, al hablar de la cena del sábado: «El domingo entro a trabajar a las seis de la mañana»; según lo entendí yo, dio a entender que prefería cenar temprano, pero hoy martes aún no hemos fijado la hora ni ella ha confirmado esa preferencia.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indirect-communication construction
grammar: Dar a entender que communicates an implication rather than stating it directly. The early Sunday shift supports the narrator's interpretation of an early Saturday dinner preference, explicitly left unconfirmed.
register: Careful interpretation of a friend's indirect scheduling remark.
note: Entro a trabajar = I start work; fijar la hora = set the time. Prefería is the narrator's interpretation of Alma's preference at Monday's conversation.

sentence: El músico cuya guitarra quedó en el salón se llama Tomás; él confirmó que la guitarra es suya.
part_of_speech: feminine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: Cuya relates the masculine owner el músico to feminine singular guitarra. The complete phrase cuya guitarra is the subject of quedó; agreement follows the instrument, not its owner.
register: Careful written identification.
note: Quedó en el salón = was left in the room. Tomás explicitly confirms his ownership.

sentence: Raúl, con cuya sierra Lucía cortó ayer las tablas de la mesa, es el dueño de esa herramienta.
part_of_speech: instrument preposition and feminine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: Con marks the saw as Lucía's instrument. Cuya agrees with sierra and identifies Raúl as its owner; Lucía is the separately expressed subject of cortó.
register: Careful written account of practical work.
note: Sierra = saw; tablas = boards; herramienta = tool. Raúl owns the saw, and Lucía uses it.

sentence: La novelista Elena, de cuyo prólogo Marta extrajo una frase sobre el recuerdo para su reseña, escribió tanto la novela como ese texto introductorio.
part_of_speech: source preposition and masculine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: De belongs to extraer una frase de un texto. Cuyo agrees with masculine prólogo, which Elena authored; the complete de phrase marks the source from which Marta extracted the quotation.
register: Educated written account of a review.
note: Prólogo = preface; extrajo = extracted; reseña = review. Marta uses a phrase from Elena's preface.

sentence: Rosa fue ayer a devolver un libro a Julián, a cuya casa llegó a las seis; la vivienda es de él.
part_of_speech: destination preposition and feminine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: A preserves the destination complement of llegar a una casa. Cuya agrees with casa and links that destination to Julián; Rosa performs the movement.
register: Neutral written personal narrative.
note: La vivienda refers to the house, and él refers to Julián. Rosa arrives there to return a book.

sentence: Clara, entre cuyas tres propuestas para la fiesta el comité eligió una comida de ochocientos pesos, también había sugerido un concierto y un baile, ambos de más de mil; el límite de gasto era de mil pesos.
part_of_speech: set-selection preposition and feminine plural possessive relative determiner
grammar: Entre introduces the set containing the selected proposal. Cuyas agrees with propuestas, and el comité is the subject of eligió. The meal alone falls within the stated spending limit.
register: Written report of a group decision.
note: Comité = committee; baile = dance; límite de gasto = spending limit. Clara's three options have explicit costs.

sentence: La artista Elena, uno de cuyos tres cuadros obtuvo el premio del taller por su composición, prestó la obra ganadora para la exposición del sábado; los otros dos cuadros siguen en su casa.
part_of_speech: singular partitive quantifier with de and a masculine plural possessive relative determiner
grammar: Uno selects one painting from Elena's three. Cuyos agrees with cuadros, but singular uno controls obtuvo. The selected painting matters because it won the prize and is being lent for display.
register: Written account of an art workshop.
note: Cuadro = painting; composición = composition; obra ganadora = winning work. The other two paintings remain at Elena's home.

sentence: Andrés es el vecino cuyo jardín fotografió Lucía ayer para un cartel sobre huertos; él autorizó la foto de su terreno, que está detrás de su casa.
part_of_speech: masculine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: Cuyo determines jardín within the complete direct object cuyo jardín. Lucía is the subject of fotografió, while Andrés is the garden's owner. The determiner itself is not the entire direct object.
register: Neutral written neighborhood account.
note: Fotografió = photographed; huerto = vegetable garden; terreno = plot of land. Andrés authorized the photograph.

sentence: El relato cuya última página cuenta la misma despedida desde la voz de la hija, después de diez páginas narradas por el padre, contrapone dos recuerdos; ninguno de los dos se presenta como definitivo.
meaning: whose, linking a work to its component
part_of_speech: feminine singular relative determiner expressing a part–whole relation
grammar: Cuya links relato to its component última página and agrees with página. The relation is between a text and its part; the sentence contrasts the father's and daughter's accounts without choosing a definitive version.
register: Brief written literary discussion.
note: Relato = story; despedida = farewell; contrapone = sets in contrast; definitivo = definitive.

sentence: Mi abuelo Ernesto, cuyo cuaderno de recetas me prestó ayer, es mi única fuente para las cantidades de este pan; el cuaderno es suyo.
part_of_speech: masculine singular possessive relative determiner in an explanatory clause
grammar: The paired commas make the loan added information about the already identified Ernesto. Cuyo agrees with cuaderno; the relative does not identify one grandfather from a subset.
register: Careful written family account.
note: Cuaderno de recetas = recipe notebook; fuente = source of information. Ernesto owns the notebook and lent it to the speaker.

sentence: La comida del domingo podría hacerse en el patio, en cuyo caso cada invitado llevará una silla; si elegimos el comedor, usaremos las sillas de la casa.
part_of_speech: fixed relative connective introducing a consequence of a preceding hypothetical situation
grammar: En cuyo caso refers to the preceding possibility of eating in the patio. It introduces the chair arrangement that applies specifically to that option; the indoor alternative has a different arrangement.
register: Careful practical planning.
note: Invitado = guest; comedor = dining room. The location remains undecided.

sentence: La afirmación «El taller no cobra las clases», a la cual se refirió Elena en su mensaje del lunes, aparece en el aviso del taller; Elena no habló del costo de los materiales.
part_of_speech: governed preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: A is retained from referirse a una afirmación. La cual agrees with afirmación, the explicit noun naming the statement; it does not introduce a movement destination.
register: Careful written report of a message.
note: Afirmación = statement; referirse a = refer to. Elena's reference concerns class fees, not material costs.

sentence: La donación de quinientos pesos, de la cual depende la compra de pintura para el mural, ya está en la caja del grupo; sin ese dinero no tenemos fondos para comprarla.
part_of_speech: governed dependency preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: De comes from depender de. La cual refers to the available donation, while la compra is the subject of depende. The donation's presence is distinct from the hypothetical lack of those funds.
register: Neutral written explanation of shared resources.
note: Mural = wall painting; fondos = funds; comprarla refers to buying the paint.

sentence: Clara considera claro el final de la función de ayer; esa es la valoración con la cual coincide Óscar, aunque ella juzga adecuado el ritmo y él lo considera lento.
part_of_speech: governed agreement preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Con belongs to coincidir con una valoración. Óscar agrees with Clara's assessment of the ending, while their evaluations of the pace differ. The relative introduces an assessment rather than an instrument.
register: Reasoned discussion of a performance.
note: Valoración = assessment; función = performance; ritmo = pace here. Their agreement is limited to the ending's clarity.

sentence: La propuesta de sustituir el huerto del edificio por un estacionamiento, contra la cual protestan los vecinos porque quieren seguir cultivando verduras allí, todavía no está aprobada.
part_of_speech: opposition preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Contra marks the proposal opposed through protestar contra algo. La cual agrees with propuesta; los vecinos perform the protest, and their stated reason is preserving their vegetable-growing activity.
register: Neutral written account of a neighborhood proposal.
note: Huerto = vegetable garden; estacionamiento = parking lot; protestar contra = protest against. The proposal remains unapproved.

sentence: Ana ya tiene la llave de la bodega, sin la cual no podría sacar las sillas para la comida de hoy; la puerta solo se abre con esa llave.
part_of_speech: absent-resource preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Sin la cual imagines the absence of the identified key and states the resulting inability. Ana actually has the key; the relative does not assert that the resource is missing.
register: Neutral household preparation.
note: Bodega = storeroom here; sacar las sillas = take the chairs out. Only the identified key opens the door.

sentence: La falta de sombra en el patio, sobre la cual debaten Clara y Luis, es un problema que ambos reconocen; Clara propone poner una lona y Luis prefiere plantar un árbol.
part_of_speech: topic preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Sobre introduces the topic of debatir sobre algo. La cual refers to the acknowledged lack of shade; the topic is a prepositional complement, not the direct object of debaten.
register: Neutral report of a practical discussion.
note: Lona = tarpaulin or shade sheet; plantar = plant. Clara and Luis recognize the same problem but propose different responses.

sentence: El coro se comprometió por escrito con Julia, dueña del salón, a usarlo este mes solo los sábados de cuatro a seis; esa es la condición bajo la cual ella autorizó los ensayos, que todavía no han empezado.
part_of_speech: condition preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Bajo la cual links authorization to the stated condition limiting use to Saturdays from four to six this month. La cual agrees with condición. Authorization and the choir's written commitment do not imply that rehearsals have begun.
register: Careful written account of an agreed arrangement.
note: Coro = choir; ensayos = rehearsals; usarlo refers to the room owned by Julia.

sentence: Nora adopta la perspectiva de la igualdad de participación, desde la cual valora el reparto de turnos de ayer: cada integrante tuvo cinco minutos; por eso juzga equitativo el tiempo, sin evaluar la calidad de las intervenciones.
part_of_speech: interpretive-viewpoint preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Desde la cual introduces Nora's stated criterion for interpreting the allocation of speaking time. It refers to perspectiva and limits the favorable judgment to equal time rather than contribution quality.
register: Educated written assessment of a discussion.
note: Equitativo = equitable; integrante = member; intervenciones = contributions to the discussion.

sentence: El equipo del comedor ajusta las porciones para tirar como máximo un kilo de comida al día; esa es la meta hacia la cual dirige sus esfuerzos, pero esta semana aún tira dos kilos diarios.
part_of_speech: abstract-direction preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Hacia la cual refers to the target maximum waste amount. Dirigir esfuerzos hacia una meta expresses the direction of ongoing work; the current two-kilo figure shows that the goal remains unmet.
register: Neutral explanation of practical group efforts.
note: Ajustar las porciones = adjust serving sizes; meta = goal; tirar = throw away here.

sentence: El aviso fija el 30 de junio como la fecha hasta la cual seguirá abierta la exposición, incluido ese día; el 1 de julio la sala cerrará para cambiar las obras.
part_of_speech: temporal-endpoint preposition and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Hasta la cual refers to fecha and marks the endpoint of continued exhibition access. Incluido ese día explicitly includes June 30; closure begins July 1.
register: Written explanation of an exhibition notice.
note: Fija = specifies here; exposición = exhibition; obras = artworks. The notice supplies both the endpoint and the following closure.

sentence: La carta escrita por Lucía, por medio de la cual Marta recibió el lunes el aviso «Se canceló el ensayo del martes», no explicaba el motivo; Marta aún no ha confirmado la cancelación con el coro.
part_of_speech: communication-channel prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Por medio de la cual identifies Lucía's letter as the channel through which Marta receives the cancellation notice. Receiving that notice does not independently confirm the cancellation or establish its reason.
register: Careful written account of communicated information.
note: Motivo = reason; coro = choir. The cancellation notice concerns a rehearsal scheduled for Tuesday.

sentence: Elena, a través de la cual recibí el lunes el mensaje de Raúl «La reunión será el martes a las seis», me aclaró hoy miércoles que solo lo transmitió y que no asistió a esa reunión.
part_of_speech: intermediary prepositional locution and feminine singular personal relative sequence
grammar: A través de la cual identifies Elena as the intermediary between Raúl and the narrator. Her Wednesday clarification distinguishes transmitting Monday's scheduling message from attending Tuesday's meeting.
register: Careful written account of a relayed message.
note: Transmitió = passed on; lo refers to Raúl's message. Elena explicitly reports that she did not attend.

sentence: La pregunta «¿Debe el club comprar libros o pedir prestados los de la biblioteca?», en torno a la cual giró la charla del sábado, dividió a Inés y Pablo: ella defendió la compra y él el préstamo; solo acordaron comparar costos.
meaning: around which, as the central topic
part_of_speech: central-topic prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: En torno a la cual identifies the question organizing the discussion. Girar en torno a a topic is figurative here; Inés and Pablo agree only to compare costs, not on buying versus borrowing.
register: Written report of a club discussion.
note: Defendió la compra = argued for buying; préstamo = borrowing arrangement here. The decision remains open.

sentence: Luis apoyó en un dibujo sin medidas su afirmación «Las seis mesas caben en el patio», respecto de la cual Ana expresó dudas ayer; ella no opinó sobre el precio de las mesas.
part_of_speech: assessment-topic prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Respecto de la cual bounds Ana's doubts to Luis's space claim. It refers to afirmación rather than the drawing or Luis himself; the sentence separately excludes a judgment about price.
register: Educated written report of a qualified assessment.
note: Medidas = measurements; caben = fit; expresó dudas = voiced doubts. The drawing contains no measurements.

sentence: El acuerdo escrito del grupo contiene esta cláusula: «Quien aporte una mesa podrá usar gratis el salón el sábado de dos a seis»; es la cláusula en virtud de la cual Ana, que aportó una mesa, tiene ese derecho, aunque todavía no ha usado el salón.
part_of_speech: formal basis prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: En virtud de la cual identifies the agreement clause establishing Ana's bounded entitlement. She meets its contribution requirement; the Saturday time limit remains part of the permission, whose exercise is still pending.
register: Formal written explanation of a group's arrangement.
note: Cláusula = provision of an agreement; derecho = entitlement here. Gratis means without a usage charge.

sentence: Nora vio ayer tierra húmeda en la maceta del patio; esa fue la observación a partir de la cual supuso que alguien había regado la planta, aunque también consideró posible que hubiera llovido.
part_of_speech: inferential-basis prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: A partir de la cual introduces the observation used to develop an inference. The wet soil is observed; watering is supposed, with prior rain retained as an alternative explanation.
register: Neutral account of a limited inference.
note: Tierra húmeda = damp soil; maceta = plant pot; regar = water a plant. Nora does not establish who caused the wetness.

sentence: La elección del repertorio, al margen de la cual se desarrolló la charla del sábado por acuerdo de Ana y Luis, sigue pendiente; ese día solo fijaron la fecha del concierto y dejaron las canciones para todo el coro.
part_of_speech: scope-exclusion prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Al margen de la cual identifies repertoire selection as deliberately outside Saturday's agreed discussion. The issue remains for the whole choir; exclusion from that conversation does not declare it unimportant.
register: Careful written account of cultural planning.
note: Repertorio = repertoire or set of pieces; fijar la fecha = set the date. Ana and Luis settled only the concert date.

sentence: La escasez de agua del huerto, frente a la cual Marta propone reducir a la mitad el riego esta semana, podría atenderse también comprando agua, según Luis; todavía no han elegido ninguna medida.
part_of_speech: abstract-response prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: Frente a la cual presents the water shortage as the problem motivating Marta's proposed response. Luis offers a different possible measure; neither proposal is represented as approved or sufficient.
register: Neutral written account of practical alternatives.
note: Escasez = shortage; riego = watering; medida = measure or action here. Marta's proposed reduction is limited to this week.

sentence: La propuesta de cerrar la biblioteca a las seis en vez de a las cinco los sábados, a favor de la cual se pronunció Elena ayer porque sale del trabajo a las cinco, no incluye abrir los domingos, cuestión sobre la que Elena no opinó.
part_of_speech: support prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: A favor de la cual identifies the exact proposal Elena supports. Her five-o'clock work finish supplies her reason; her position does not extend to Sunday opening, about which she gave no opinion.
register: Written report of a service-hours proposal.
note: Pronunciarse a favor de = state support for; en vez de = instead of. No approval or voting result is stated.

sentence: El coro propuso ayer eliminar la pausa del ensayo para ganar diez minutos de práctica; esa es la modificación en contra de la cual se pronunció Julia, que comparte la meta de practicar más pero propone empezar diez minutos antes y conservar el descanso.
part_of_speech: opposition prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: En contra de la cual identifies removing the break as the opposed change. Julia shares the practice goal and offers an earlier start as an alternative; the opposition is directed at the modification.
register: Reasoned report of a choir disagreement.
note: Eliminar = remove; modificación = change; conservar el descanso = keep the break.

sentence: Inés, a cargo de la cual está hoy el reparto de materiales del taller, supervisa la lista mientras Pablo entrega un cuaderno a cada participante.
part_of_speech: responsibility prepositional locution and feminine singular personal relative sequence
grammar: A cargo de la cual identifies Inés as responsible for the distribution. El reparto is the subject of está; Pablo performs the physical notebook delivery while Inés supervises.
register: Neutral report of assigned workshop responsibilities.
note: Reparto = distribution; cuaderno = notebook. Responsibility and personal execution are assigned to distinct people.

sentence: Ayer a las cinco se produjo la caída de un árbol, a causa de la cual los músicos trasladaron el ensayo al patio de Clara a las seis; el árbol bloqueó la única entrada del salón.
part_of_speech: causal prepositional locution and feminine singular relative sequence
grammar: A causa de la cual refers to the tree's fall and introduces its later consequence. The blocked sole entrance explains the musicians' relocation; the five-o'clock cause precedes the six-o'clock move.
register: Neutral written account of an interrupted rehearsal.
note: Se produjo = occurred; caída = fall; trasladaron = moved or relocated; bloqueó = blocked.

sentence: El taller del sábado aceptará a cuantos entreguen una muestra antes del jueves; hoy miércoles, Ana, Luis y Nora ya cumplieron ese requisito, pero los tres aún no confirman su asistencia.
part_of_speech: masculine plural quantitative personal relative pronoun
grammar: Cuantos introduces all qualifying people without a following people noun. A marks the personal object of aceptará; entreguen states the open eligibility criterion. Meeting it does not establish attendance.
register: Careful written participation notice and update.
note: Muestra = sample; requisito = requirement; asistencia = attendance. Three named people have met the requirement.

sentence: Durante los veinte minutos que tenía libres antes de entrar a trabajar, Lucía ayudó cuanto pudo a limpiar el patio; al terminar ese tiempo tuvo que irse y quedó la mitad sin barrer.
part_of_speech: invariant relative adverb expressing extent of action
grammar: Cuanto pudo expresses the extent of Lucía's helping under her time limit. Cuanto modifies the action rather than naming its direct object; the remaining unswept half limits the achieved result.
register: Neutral account of practical assistance.
note: Tenía libres = had available; barrer = sweep. Lucía leaves when her twenty available minutes end.

sentence: Luis dijo que Pablo colocó ayer el cartel, pero yo vi a Ana fijarlo en la pared: fue Ana la que lo colocó.
part_of_speech: feminine singular relative sequence in a focus cleft
grammar: Fue Ana la que lo colocó focuses the actor and corrects Luis's attribution to Pablo. La agrees with Ana; the narrator's stated observation supplies evidence for the correction.
register: Neutral correction of an event attribution.
note: Colocó = put up here; fijarlo en la pared = attach it to the wall. Lo refers to the poster.

sentence: Ana, lo que te pido hoy es reservar una mesa para cuatro personas el viernes a las dos; no te pido organizar toda la comida.
meaning: what, introducing the precise requested action
part_of_speech: neuter free-relative sequence in an identifying pseudocleft
grammar: Lo que te pido hoy is identified by es reservar una mesa. The pseudocleft specifies the requested action, party size, and reservation time while rejecting the broader task of organizing the meal.
register: Direct clarification using familiar singular address.
note: Reservar una mesa = book a table. Ana is asked today to reserve for four on Friday at two.

sentence: El miércoles, Ana pagó quinientos pesos por la reparación de la mesa, doscientos más de lo que había calculado el lunes, cuando la estimó en trescientos.
part_of_speech: comparative preposition and neuter relative sequence introducing a finite comparison standard
grammar: De lo que introduces Ana's earlier calculated amount as the comparison standard. Monday's three-hundred-peso estimate precedes Wednesday's five-hundred-peso payment, leaving an explicit two-hundred-peso difference.
register: Neutral account of an expense exceeding an estimate.
note: La estimó refers to estimating the repair's cost. Había calculado locates the estimate before payment.

sentence: Elena, de quien depende que el coro pueda abrir el salón mañana sábado, tiene la única llave y se comprometió a entregársela al grupo a las nueve; todavía no lo ha hecho.
part_of_speech: governed dependency preposition and singular personal relative pronoun
grammar: De belongs to depender de una persona. Elena's possession of the only key and her delivery commitment make the dependency concrete. The relative does not mark her as a conversation topic or item source.
register: Neutral planning report about a shared room.
note: Entregársela means hand the key over to the group. The promised Saturday delivery remains unperformed.

sentence: Clara, con quien discrepo hoy sobre el horario del ensayo del sábado, coincide conmigo en que faltan dos canciones por practicar; ella propone ensayar de cinco a ocho y yo de seis a nueve.
part_of_speech: governed disagreement preposition and singular personal relative pronoun
grammar: Con quien introduces Clara as the person with whom the narrator disagrees. The matter is the rehearsal schedule, stated separately; both accept the unfinished two-song task but propose different time slots.
register: Reasoned first-person account of a scheduling disagreement.
note: Discrepo = I disagree; conmigo = with me. Both proposed rehearsal slots last three hours.

sentence: Hoy jueves cuento que el lunes dejamos unos frijoles en remojo a las ocho de la noche durante doce horas, al cabo de las cuales los escurrimos el martes a las ocho de la mañana.
part_of_speech: temporal prepositional locution and feminine plural interval-relative sequence
grammar: Las cuales agrees with doce horas. The complete twelve-hour interval runs from Monday at eight at night to Tuesday at eight in the morning; Thursday is only the retelling day.
register: Neutral household recollection.
note: En remojo = soaking; escurrimos = drained; los refers to the beans.

sentence: Elena considera fiel la traducción dentro de lo que pudo cotejar ayer: comparó las dos primeras páginas con el original, pero no revisó las demás.
part_of_speech: bounding prepositional locution and neuter free-relative sequence
grammar: Dentro de lo que limits Elena's assessment to the content she could compare. The finite relative supplies that content without a named noun antecedent.
register: Careful assessment of a translation.
note: Fiel = faithful to the original; cotejar = compare closely. Only the first two pages were checked.

sentence: Rosa considera útil un resumen en la medida en que conserva las razones de los personajes: el de Ana recoge las tres y le sirve más que el de Luis, que solo recoge una; no está juzgando el estilo.
part_of_speech: locution introducing a degree-dependent assessment
grammar: The usefulness Rosa assigns varies with the number of characters' reasons retained. Three retained reasons support a higher assessment than one; style is excluded.
register: Reasoned comparison of two summaries.
note: Recoge = includes or captures here; juzgar = assess. The comparison concerns preservation of reasons.

sentence: Según Raúl, el piano quedó afinado el lunes, de lo cual Marta duda hoy martes porque aún no ha recibido la confirmación del afinador ni ha probado el instrumento.
part_of_speech: governed preposition and clause-anaphoric neuter relative sequence
grammar: De is retained from dudar de algo. Lo cual represents the preceding attributed claim about Monday's tuning, rather than a possessed or received noun.
register: Neutral report distinguishing a claim from confirmation.
note: Afinado = tuned; afinador = piano tuner. Marta's missing confirmation does not establish that the claim is false.

sentence: Ayer, la dueña nos permitió usar también el patio para la comida, con lo cual pudimos separar las mesas y dejar libre el pasillo; el comedor solo no tenía espacio suficiente.
part_of_speech: preposition and clause-anaphoric neuter relative sequence expressing consequence
grammar: Con lo cual refers to the owner's permission to use the patio and introduces the resulting arrangement. It does not introduce unnamed materials available for use.
register: Neutral account of meal arrangements.
note: Dueña = female owner; comedor = dining room. The extra space allowed the group to leave the passage clear.

sentence: Nora anunció el lunes que el taller del sábado sería gratuito, sobre lo cual Pedro comentó el martes: «Eso aclara el precio de las clases, pero no el de los materiales».
part_of_speech: topic preposition and clause-anaphoric neuter relative sequence
grammar: Sobre lo cual makes Nora's complete attributed claim the topic of Pedro's comment. Pedro limits what that claim clarifies rather than supplying a cause.
register: Careful report with a quoted qualification.
note: Gratuito = free of charge. El de los materiales means the price of the materials.

sentence: Hoy lunes me arrepiento de lo que hice ayer con mi hermano: le grité porque perdió mi libro; ya le pedí disculpas por los gritos.
part_of_speech: governed preposition and neuter free-relative sequence
grammar: De belongs to arrepentirse de. Lo que hice identifies the speaker's acknowledged shouting as the content of regret, without a named action antecedent.
register: Personal acknowledgment of regretted conduct.
note: Le grité = I shouted at him; gritos = shouting. The brother lost the book, and the speaker regrets the response.

sentence: Luis cree que critiqué la acústica del salón, pero me refiero a lo que dije ayer: «Aquí no podemos ensayar a las diez de la noche porque los vecinos ya están dormidos».
part_of_speech: governed preposition and neuter free-relative sequence
grammar: A is retained from referirse a. The free relative supplies yesterday's remark as the intended content; the quotation identifies a time restriction, correcting Luis's acoustic interpretation.
register: Direct correction of a misunderstood remark.
note: Acústica = acoustic qualities; ensayar = rehearse. The stated objection concerns late-night noise affecting sleeping neighbors.

sentence: Ana se preocupa por lo que pueda pasarle a su gato durante la mudanza de mañana: teme que se escape al abrir las puertas, pero por ahora el gato está en casa y nada de eso ha ocurrido.
part_of_speech: governed concern preposition and neuter free-relative sequence
grammar: Por belongs to preocuparse por. Lo que pueda pasarle supplies possible future events as the content of concern; it does not connect a preceding cause to a consequence.
register: Neutral description of a specific personal concern.
note: Pueda pasarle = might happen to the cat; se escape = gets out. The feared escape has not occurred.

sentence: Julia dice que estas tijeras sirven para lo que necesita hacer hoy: recortar las invitaciones de papel delgado; probó una hoja y la cortó bien, aunque no logró cortar cartón grueso.
part_of_speech: purpose preposition and neuter free-relative sequence
grammar: Para lo que introduces the finite task against which Julia judges the scissors suitable. The successful thin-paper test and failed cardboard test limit that assessment.
register: Practical assessment of a household tool.
note: Tijeras = scissors; recortar = cut out; cartón grueso = thick cardboard.

sentence: Ana me contó ayer la fecha de cada visita que hicimos ella y yo durante el viaje; sin lo que me contó, no podría ordenar hoy las fotos por fecha, porque yo no recordaba cuándo habíamos estado en cada pueblo.
part_of_speech: hypothetical absence preposition and neuter free-relative sequence
grammar: Sin lo que imagines the absence of Ana's supplied information. The speaker actually received it; the relative introduces that content without a named noun antecedent.
register: Everyday explanation of organizing travel photographs.
note: Ordenar por fecha = arrange by date; pueblo = town. Habíamos estado places the visits before Ana's account.

sentence: Según el acuerdo de ayer, preparar la merienda para los niños les corresponde a quienes se ofrecieron a organizarla: Ana y Luis; los niños solo van a recibir la comida.
part_of_speech: responsibility-holder preposition and plural personal free-relative pronoun
grammar: A quienes identifies the people to whom the preparation responsibility falls. Preparar la merienda is the subject of corresponde; les marks the same responsibility holders.
register: Neutral explanation of an agreed division of work.
note: Merienda = snack or light meal. Ana and Luis organize it; the children are its beneficiaries.

sentence: Marta desconfía de quienes afirman hoy que el coro ya ensayó las seis canciones: Raúl y Pedro dijeron ayer cantidades distintas; ella aún no ha revisado la lista del ensayo.
meaning: those who, as the people mistrusted
part_of_speech: governed preposition and plural personal free-relative pronoun
grammar: De belongs to desconfiar de alguien. The relative identifies Raúl and Pedro as the people Marta mistrusts, while their current claim remains unverified.
register: Bounded report of reservations about a claim.
note: Desconfiar de = mistrust; cantidades distintas = different numbers here. Their earlier disagreement is not proof that today's claim is false.

sentence: Ana y Luis propusieron ensayar el sábado de seis a ocho y me autorizaron a comunicar solo ese horario; hoy hablo por quienes hicieron esa propuesta, no por todo el coro ni sobre otros asuntos.
part_of_speech: representation preposition and plural personal free-relative pronoun
grammar: Por quienes identifies Ana and Luis as the people whose authorized position the speaker represents. They explicitly proposed the rehearsal hours and authorized only their communication.
register: Explicitly limited group representation.
note: Hablar por alguien = speak on someone's behalf. The speaker's authorization concerns Saturday's proposed six-to-eight rehearsal.

sentence: Rosa repartió hoy ocho cuadernos entre quienes se inscribieron ayer: Ana, Luis, Nora y Pedro; cada uno recibió dos, y las dos personas inscritas hoy quedaron fuera de ese reparto.
part_of_speech: distribution preposition and plural personal free-relative pronoun
grammar: Entre quienes defines the distribution group by yesterday's registration. Eight notebooks are divided among its four members, two each; today's registrants are outside this distribution.
register: Neutral account of a materials distribution.
note: Inscribirse = sign up; reparto = distribution; quedaron fuera = were excluded from this distribution.

sentence: Ana y Luis acordaron ayudarme solo una hora a empacar; al terminar ese tiempo les exigí otras tres, y ahora reconozco que abusé de quienes se ofrecieron a ayudarme.
part_of_speech: governed exploitation preposition and plural personal free-relative pronoun
grammar: De is selected by abusar de. The speaker acknowledges taking unfair advantage of the helpers' willingness by demanding three additional hours beyond their agreed limit.
register: Personal acknowledgment of excessive demands.
note: Empacar = pack; exigí = I demanded. Abusar de here means unfairly exploit someone's willingness to help.

sentence: Ana y Luis recogieron ayer las sillas del patio mientras yo guardaba las mesas; hoy expreso mi gratitud hacia quienes me ayudaron, porque sin ellos no habría terminado antes de la lluvia.
part_of_speech: attitude-direction preposition and plural personal free-relative pronoun
grammar: Hacia directs the speaker's stated gratitude toward Ana and Luis. The relative identifies the helpers, rather than a destination of physical movement.
register: Personal expression of appreciation.
note: Gratitud = gratitude; expresar = express. Ana and Luis collected chairs while the speaker put away tables.

sentence: Ayer jueves Clara leyó a Ana y Luis, que no forman parte del grupo musical, el mensaje de Pedro para los músicos: «Los vecinos prestarán diez sillas el sábado»; fueron las únicas personas ante quienes lo presentó.
part_of_speech: audience preposition and plural personal relative pronoun
grammar: Ante quienes identifies Ana and Luis as the actual audience. Clara presents Pedro's message, which concerns the neighbors and is intended for the musicians.
register: Neutral account of presenting a message.
note: Lo refers to Pedro's message. Ana and Luis heard its presentation on Thursday; the promised loan concerns Saturday.

sentence: Ana y Luis perdieron el uso del salón de ensayo esta semana; me solidarizo con quienes se quedaron sin espacio para practicar y les ofrezco mi patio solo este sábado de cuatro a seis.
part_of_speech: governed solidarity preposition and plural personal free-relative pronoun
grammar: Con is retained from solidarizarse con. The speaker expresses support for the affected people and offers a precisely bounded use of the patio.
register: Supportive personal offer.
note: Solidarizarse con = express solidarity with. The offered help covers Saturday from four to six.

sentence: El ejercicio de nombrar diez notas en una partitura es fácil para quienes ya saben leerla: Ana y Luis lo terminaron en un minuto, mientras que Nora, que nunca ha leído música, necesita primero aprender los signos.
part_of_speech: perspective preposition and plural personal free-relative pronoun
grammar: Para quienes gives the experience-based perspective under which this particular exercise is easy. The group is defined by prior score-reading knowledge, not by intended benefit.
register: Bounded comparison of experience with a music exercise.
note: Partitura = musical score; nombrar = name. Leerla refers to reading the score; lo refers to the exercise.

sentence: Rosa explicó a Ana y Luis cómo separar el diálogo de las indicaciones en un guion; ellos dijeron después que la explicación influyó en quienes estaban escribiendo su primera escena, es decir, en ellos dos, y que por eso cambiaron el formato.
part_of_speech: governed influence preposition and plural personal free-relative pronoun
grammar: En belongs to influir en alguien and introduces the people affected. Ana and Luis themselves attribute their format change to Rosa's explanation.
register: Attributed account of a specific learning influence.
note: Guion = script; indicaciones = stage directions here; formato = format. The reported effect concerns these two writers.

sentence: Ana eligió el turno de las nueve para acompañar a su hijo a la escuela y dejó el de las ocho, que ofrecía dos beneficios a los cuales renunció: elegir primero el material y tener una mesa individual.
part_of_speech: governed preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: A is retained from renunciar a algo. Los cuales refers to the two benefits Ana voluntarily gives up when choosing the later session.
register: Neutral account of a practical tradeoff.
note: Beneficios = advantages here; mesa individual = a table for one person. The later session lets Ana accompany her son.

sentence: El tablero, las cuatro fichas y los dos dados son los siete elementos de los cuales se compone este juego; la caja es solo el envase y no cuenta como parte del juego.
part_of_speech: composition preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: De belongs to componerse de. Este juego is the subject of se compone; the seven elements are its components, not a quantified subset of seven games.
register: Practical description of a game's contents.
note: Tablero = game board; fichas = playing pieces; dados = dice; envase = packaging.

sentence: Ana y Luis son los músicos con los cuales Clara se comprometió ayer jueves a llevar dos atriles para el ensayo del sábado; hoy viernes aún no los entrega y aclaró que no llevará los instrumentos.
meaning: to whom, as the people receiving her commitment
part_of_speech: governed personal-commitment preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Con identifies the people to whom Clara undertakes the commitment. A llevar introduces its action; los later refers to the two music stands.
register: Neutral report of a bounded undertaking.
note: Atriles = music stands. Thursday's commitment concerns Saturday; Friday's update says delivery is still pending.

sentence: Para encuadernar el cuaderno, Ana podía elegir cartón, tela o cuero; prefirió cartón y tela, los dos materiales por los cuales optó porque juntos costaban cincuenta pesos, frente a los ciento veinte del cuero.
meaning: for which, as the chosen options
part_of_speech: governed selection preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Por is selected by optar por and introduces the chosen materials. The following porque clause separately states Ana's reason for that choice.
register: Practical explanation of a craft-material choice.
note: Encuadernar = bind pages; cartón = cardboard; tela = fabric; cuero = leather.

sentence: El humor y la fama del autor eran dos criterios sobre los cuales debía prevalecer la duración, según el acuerdo de ayer del club; hoy el grupo eligió un cuento de cinco minutos frente a otro más cómico y de autor famoso que duraba veinte.
part_of_speech: governed priority preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Sobre belongs to prevalecer sobre and introduces the competing criteria. La duración is the subject and takes priority under this club's stated rule.
register: Reasoned account of a cultural selection.
note: Prevalecer sobre = take priority over; fama = fame. The rule concerns this selection of a story.

sentence: Los roces y los dobleces eran los dos riesgos contra los cuales Rosa protegió las fotos con fundas y cartón rígido durante el traslado; aun así, una copia llegó con una esquina marcada.
part_of_speech: protective preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Contra introduces the risks in proteger algo contra algo. The photographs are protected with sleeves and stiff cardboard, but the final damage limits the achieved protection.
register: Neutral account of packing photographs.
note: Roces = rubbing or scuffing; dobleces = bends or creases; fundas = protective sleeves; rígido = stiff.

sentence: Conservo dos mensajes del coro, del lunes y del martes, según los cuales el ensayo del sábado empezará a las cinco y a las seis, respectivamente; hoy miércoles solo verifiqué su contenido y no sé qué horario sigue vigente.
part_of_speech: source-attribution preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Según los cuales attributes different start times to the two written messages in their stated order. Verification of their wording does not establish which schedule remains valid.
register: Careful comparison of written notices.
note: Respectivamente pairs Monday with five and Tuesday with six. Vigente = still valid.

sentence: Luis repite dos juicios a los que se aferra: «Todo cuento corto es fácil y todo cuento largo es difícil»; hoy dijo que no piensa revisarlos, aunque admitió que un relato de una página le costó mucho entenderlo.
part_of_speech: governed figurative-attachment preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: A belongs to figurative aferrarse a. Los que refers to Luis's two stated judgments; his explicit refusal to reconsider supports the tenacious-attachment reading.
register: Critical but evidence-based report of a stated position.
note: Juicios = judgments; aferrarse a una idea = cling to an idea; revisarlos = reconsider the judgments here.

sentence: Para bordar las hojas del mantel, Rosa necesita hilos verdes y azules, de los que hoy carece: solo tiene hilo rojo y por eso aplazó esa parte del trabajo.
part_of_speech: governed lack preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: De is retained from carecer de. Los que refers to the required green and blue threads, which are unavailable; it does not select a quantified subset.
register: Neutral account of a craft-material shortage.
note: Bordar = embroider; mantel = tablecloth; hilos = threads. Rosa postpones only the part requiring the missing colors.

sentence: Ana dijo al empezar el ensayo: «Hoy revisaré solo el ritmo y las entradas de las voces»; esos son los aspectos en los que se concentra ahora, mientras deja la pronunciación para mañana.
part_of_speech: governed attention preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: En belongs to concentrarse en and introduces the selected aspects. Ana's stated plan identifies her current scope, while pronunciation is explicitly deferred.
register: Neutral rehearsal report with quoted intentions.
note: Entradas de las voces = points when the singers begin. Concentrarse en = focus on.

sentence: En el taller, Pablo aprendió a cortar tablas rectas y a unirlas con pegamento; esos son los trabajos para los que dice estar capacitado, y aclara que no sabe construir una silla completa.
part_of_speech: governed task-preparation preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Para introduces the tasks in estar capacitado para. Pablo reports preparation for two learned tasks and explicitly excludes constructing a complete chair.
register: Bounded self-assessment of workshop preparation.
note: Tablas = boards; pegamento = glue; estar capacitado para = have the preparation for a task.

sentence: Clara usó dos bocetos de ayer, mediante los cuales reconstruyó hoy la posición de las mesas del ensayo; comparó ambos dibujos, pero no pudo recuperar la ubicación de las sillas, que ninguno mostraba.
part_of_speech: means preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Mediante introduces the means Clara used to reconstruct the table positions. The drawings support that result but contain no chair-location information.
register: Practical account of reconstructing an arrangement.
note: Bocetos = sketches; reconstruir = reconstruct; ubicación = location. Mediante means by means of.

sentence: El límite de diez minutos de lectura y la presencia de un solo narrador fueron los criterios conforme a los cuales el club eligió hoy el cuento de Ana: dura ocho minutos y tiene un narrador, mientras que el de Luis dura quince y tiene dos.
part_of_speech: conformity prepositional sequence and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Conforme a los cuales relates the club's choice to its two stated criteria. Ana's story meets both, while Luis's exceeds the time limit and has two narrators.
register: Reasoned explanation of a club selection.
note: Criterios = criteria; narrador = narrator. Conforme a expresses compliance with criteria here.

sentence: Raúl puso dos reparos al paseo, el precio del boleto y el costo del transporte, detrás de los cuales estaba, según él mismo explicó, el temor de superar sus doscientos pesos disponibles; aclaró que sí quería ir.
meaning: behind which, as an underlying motive
part_of_speech: figurative underlying-motive prepositional locution and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Detrás de los cuales presents the acknowledged concern underlying Raúl's two objections. Raúl himself supplies the motive; the narrator does not infer a concealed intention.
register: Reported explanation of practical reservations.
note: Reparos = objections or reservations; superar = exceed. Raúl still wanted to join the outing.

sentence: Rosa vio ayer la puerta del salón abierta a las nueve y cerrada a las diez; hoy dice que esos son los datos más allá de los cuales no quiere sacar conclusiones: no vio quién entró ni quién cerró.
part_of_speech: evidential-boundary prepositional locution and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: Más allá de los cuales marks the boundary Rosa places on inference from her two observations. The opening and closing agents remain outside what she witnessed.
register: Careful statement of evidential limits.
note: Datos = observed facts here; sacar conclusiones = draw conclusions. The observations were yesterday; Rosa states her limit today.

sentence: Nora tenía cuatro cuentos para la lectura, uno de Ana, otro de Luis, otro de Rosa y otro de Pedro, de entre los cuales eligió hoy los dos de menos de cinco minutos: los de Ana y Luis; los otros duraban diez.
part_of_speech: selection compound preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: De entre los cuales identifies the candidate set from which Nora actively selects. Two of four stories meet the under-five-minute criterion and are explicitly identified.
register: Neutral account of selecting reading material.
note: Los de Ana y Luis refers to their two stories. The other two stories each lasted ten minutes.

sentence: Ayer estaban en marcha los ensayos de música y danza, en medio de los cuales se fue la luz a las seis; habían empezado a las cinco, se detuvieron y se reanudaron a las seis y cuarto.
part_of_speech: temporal-overlap prepositional locution and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: En medio de los cuales locates the outage within both ongoing rehearsals. Their five-o'clock start precedes the six-o'clock interruption; resumption occurs at six fifteen.
register: Neutral account of interrupted rehearsals.
note: En marcha = underway; se fue la luz = the power went out; se reanudaron = resumed.

sentence: El poco espacio y el ruido de la calle fueron dos inconvenientes del patio, a pesar de los cuales el club logró hacer ahí la lectura de ayer: movió las macetas y esperó hasta que disminuyó el tráfico.
part_of_speech: concessive prepositional locution and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: A pesar de los cuales refers to the two established obstacles and introduces the reading that nevertheless occurred. Both the obstacles and the successful result are factual.
register: Neutral account of overcoming practical obstacles.
note: Macetas = flowerpots; disminuyó = decreased. Moving the pots and waiting reduced the stated difficulties.

sentence: Hoy viernes, Elena cuenta que pasó dos días completos en casa, del lunes a las ocho al miércoles a las ocho, a lo largo de los cuales no salió ni una vez; recibió ahí todas sus visitas.
cloze: a lo largo de los cuales
answer: a lo largo de los cuales
part_of_speech: interval-spanning prepositional locution and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: A lo largo de los cuales links Elena's continuous presence to the full two-day interval. No salió ni una vez explicitly excludes intermittent absence; Friday is the reporting day.
register: Neutral report of a bounded period at home.
note: Dos días completos establishes a full forty-eight-hour interval. Todas sus visitas refers to the visitors she received at home.

sentence: Hoy lunes, Ana cuenta que pasó dos días en Puebla, del viernes a las seis de la tarde al domingo a la misma hora, durante los cuales visitó un museo el sábado a las once de la mañana y cenó con Luis esa noche a las ocho.
part_of_speech: temporal preposition and masculine plural interval-relative sequence
grammar: Durante los cuales places two discrete events within the forty-eight-hour stay. It does not say that visiting the museum or dining occupied the whole interval.
register: Neutral account of a completed visit.
note: A la misma hora means Sunday at six in the afternoon. Esa noche refers to Saturday night; Monday is the reporting day.

sentence: Busco a alguien que haya encuadernado un libro completo para dirigir nuestro taller; no basta con saber pegar hojas y todavía no sé si algún participante tiene esa experiencia.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present perfect subjunctive auxiliary in a qualifying relative clause
grammar: Haya encuadernado requires completed bookbinding experience before the current search. The relative describes an unidentified qualifying person whose existence remains unconfirmed.
register: Neutral recruitment for a practical workshop.
note: Encuadernar = bind a book; pegar hojas = glue sheets together. Prior completion, rather than current skill alone, is required.

sentence: El lunes busqué a alguien que para el viernes a las seis ya hubiera leído las tres obras, requisito para dirigir la charla de esa noche; elegí a Nora el martes y terminó de leerlas el jueves.
meaning: had, marking required completion by then
part_of_speech: third-person singular pluperfect subjunctive auxiliary in a prospective relative criterion
grammar: The Monday search requires completion before Friday at six, a checkpoint later than the search. Nora's Thursday completion independently establishes fulfillment. Hubiese is also valid in this induced subjunctive clause.
register: Neutral planning of a literary discussion.
note: Obras = literary works here; charla = discussion. Las in leerlas refers to the three works.

sentence: El martes entrevisté a Clara, la autora que había terminado el cuento el domingo; lo leí completo ese martes y comprobé la fecha de terminación en su cuaderno.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pluperfect indicative auxiliary in an asserted relative clause
grammar: Había terminado asserts Sunday's completion before Tuesday's interview. Clara is identified, and the narrator separately reports checking the completion date; this is an asserted event rather than an open search requirement.
register: Neutral account of an interview and documentary check.
note: Autora = female author; fecha de terminación = completion date. Lo refers to the story.

sentence: En mi reseña escribo: «He leído los seis cuentos del cuaderno; de esos seis, el de Nora es el mejor que haya leído, por la coherencia de su final».
meaning: I have, within the superlative assessment
part_of_speech: first-person singular present perfect subjunctive auxiliary in a superlative relative
grammar: Haya leído is a written superlative-relative option. He leído is also valid in this exact sentence. Both retain the reviewer's completed reading and the comparison limited to six stories.
register: Written literary review; the subjunctive adds a more literary tone.
note: Reseña = review; coherencia = coherence. El de Nora refers to Nora's story among the six assessed.

sentence: Según lo que respondieron los veinte vecinos del paseo, hay pocos que conozcan toda la ruta: solo dos afirmaron conocerla y los demás dijeron que no; no he comprobado sus respuestas.
part_of_speech: masculine plural nominal quantifier functioning as an internal modal inductor
grammar: Pocos bounds the scarcity to qualifying people within the twenty respondents. In hay pocos que, it licenses the visible subjunctive conozcan; an indicative descriptive framing is also possible.
register: Careful report of a group's self-reported route knowledge.
note: Conocer toda la ruta = know the whole route. The speaker reports answers and explicitly leaves them unverified.

sentence: Según las respuestas de los ocho integrantes del grupo, Luis es el único que ha leído los tres poemas; los otros siete solo leyeron uno y él mostró sus notas sobre los tres.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective expressing exclusive qualification
grammar: El único restricts qualification to Luis within the eight-member group. The indicative relative reports the attributed reading history; exclusive-property relatives can also admit subjunctive under a different framing.
register: Neutral report of a reading group's responses.
note: Integrantes = members. The stated qualification is reading all three poems, rather than reading any poem.

sentence: Tengo con quien ensayar el diálogo mañana: mi hermana Ana aceptó practicar conmigo; yo diré las preguntas y ella las respuestas.
part_of_speech: companion preposition and personal relative pronoun in a free indefinite infinitive relative
grammar: Con quien ensayar supplies an available partner for the speaker's pending rehearsal. Con quién is also valid here with a tonic reading and need not introduce a question.
register: Neutral family coordination for practice.
note: Ensayar el diálogo = rehearse the dialogue. The speaker rehearses with Ana, with their parts explicitly divided.

sentence: Tengo un cuento que leer esta tarde por gusto; nadie me ha impuesto esa lectura y yo decidiré si la hago.
part_of_speech: relative pronoun functioning as the direct object of an infinitive
grammar: Que represents un cuento as the object of leer; the speaker is the understood reader. Tengo takes the noun phrase un cuento, so this is distinct from auxiliary tener que expressing obligation.
register: Everyday statement of optional leisure reading.
note: Por gusto = for pleasure. The speaker has reading material available and expressly denies an imposed reading duty.

sentence: Tengo dos pinceles limpios con los que pintar mañana el marco de mi espejo; todavía no he empezado y los usaré yo.
part_of_speech: instrument preposition and masculine plural relative sequence introducing an infinitive relative
grammar: Con los que relates the available brushes to a prospective use. The speaker is the understood painter; possession supplies availability without asserting completed painting.
register: Everyday home-repair planning.
note: Pinceles = paintbrushes; marco de mi espejo = frame of my mirror. Los usaré yo makes the intended user explicit.

sentence: Para mis tardes de lectura, busco el patio ideal en el que leer sin ruido; cualquiera de varios patios con sombra podría servirme y todavía no he elegido uno.
part_of_speech: locative preposition and masculine singular relative sequence introducing an infinitive relative
grammar: El patio ideal describes a desired type that several places could instantiate. En el que leer gives the speaker's prospective reading location, rather than a fact about one identified patio.
register: Neutral description of a desired reading setting.
note: Sombra = shade; podría servirme = could suit my purpose. No particular patio has been selected.

sentence: Hoy jueves, lo poco que sé del paseo proviene de la nota que Rosa dejó ayer: saldremos el sábado a las ocho; aún faltan el destino y la hora de regreso.
part_of_speech: neuter quantificational relative sequence introducing limited content
grammar: Lo poco que sé del paseo is the nominal subject of proviene. It packages a small amount of known content, explicitly limited to the departure information in Rosa's note.
register: Careful practical statement of limited information.
note: Proviene de = comes from; destino = destination. The missing information concerns the destination and return time.

sentence: Con diez minutos y una aguja prestada, cosí el dobladillo lo mejor que pude; quedó sujeto, aunque varias puntadas salieron desiguales.
part_of_speech: superlative degree-relative sequence used adverbially
grammar: Lo mejor que pude modifies the quality of cosí under the stated time and tool constraints. It identifies the speaker's best attainable performance, not a best object or a perfect result.
register: Everyday account of a constrained clothing repair.
note: Aguja = needle; dobladillo = hem; puntadas = stitches; desiguales = uneven. The hem held despite the uneven stitches.

sentence: El acuerdo del intercambio de libros de nuestro grupo establece que todo aquel que entregue un libro en buen estado podrá elegir otro; este acuerdo solo se aplica a las doce personas inscritas.
part_of_speech: universal quantifier with a personal demonstrative antecedent and relative pronoun
grammar: Todo aquel que includes every person satisfying the stated contribution condition within the twelve-person arrangement. Aquel has generalized personal reference here rather than pointing to a distant person.
register: Formal wording of a small group's arrangement.
note: Intercambio = exchange; personas inscritas = registered participants. Eligibility is limited to this group's exchange.

sentence: El lunes, Ana me dijo: «No muevas las macetas del patio»; hoy respeté aquello que me pidió entonces: dejarlas en su sitio, aunque limpié el piso a su alrededor.
part_of_speech: neuter demonstrative antecedent and relative pronoun referring to earlier discourse content
grammar: Aquello que recovers Ana's specified earlier request. The following explanation identifies the recovered content as leaving the pots in place, rather than referring to an unidentified distant object.
register: Neutral account of following an earlier household request.
note: Macetas = flowerpots; dejarlas en su sitio = leave them in place. Las refers to the pots.

sentence: Los vecinos ayudaron a la biblioteca del barrio, para cuya sala de lectura donaron dos lámparas; Ana y Luis las instalaron allí ayer para mejorar la iluminación.
part_of_speech: beneficiary-purpose preposition and feminine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: Cuya links sala de lectura to biblioteca and agrees with sala. Para identifies that room as the intended beneficiary of the donated lamps; Ana and Luis perform the installation.
register: Careful written account of neighborhood support.
note: Sala de lectura = reading room; iluminación = lighting. Las refers to the two lamps.

sentence: Rosa, dueña del patio, es la persona sin cuyo permiso no podemos ensayar allí, según nuestro acuerdo con ella; ya nos autorizó a usarlo este sábado.
part_of_speech: exclusion preposition and masculine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: Cuyo links permiso to Rosa and agrees with masculine permiso. Sin describes the hypothetical absence that would block authorized use under their agreement; her actual permission has already been granted.
register: Careful explanation of a private rehearsal arrangement.
note: Dueña = female owner; autorizó = authorized. Usarlo refers to using the patio.

sentence: Según la nota firmada por los ocho integrantes del coro, Ana fue la vecina por cuya intervención ensayaron el sábado en el patio de Rosa: Ana habló con Rosa y obtuvo su permiso.
part_of_speech: causal preposition and feminine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: Por gives the causal relation, while cuya links intervención to Ana and agrees with intervención. The signed note attributes the rehearsal to her obtaining Rosa's permission.
register: Written attribution of a bounded helpful intervention.
note: Intervención = intervention or helpful involvement; obtuvo = obtained. The eight choir members are the rehearsal participants.

sentence: Según el reparto escrito de hoy, Elena es la coordinadora bajo cuya supervisión Ana y Luis montarán la exposición del sábado; ellos colgarán los dibujos y ella revisará su distribución.
part_of_speech: supervisory-authority preposition and feminine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: Bajo cuya supervisión identifies Elena's supervisory role. Cuya agrees with supervisión; Ana and Luis are assigned the physical hanging, while Elena checks the arrangement.
register: Written explanation of cultural-event task allocation.
note: Montar una exposición = set up an exhibition; colgar = hang; distribución = arrangement here.

sentence: Rosa leyó la propuesta de Ana, sobre cuya claridad escribió: «El orden de los turnos se entiende, pero falta explicar cómo se elegirán los textos».
part_of_speech: topic preposition and feminine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: Sobre introduces claridad as the assessment topic. Cuya links that property to Ana's proposal and agrees with claridad; Rosa's judgment distinguishes clear turn order from an unexplained text-selection method.
register: Written feedback on a reading proposal.
note: Claridad = clarity; orden de los turnos = order of turns. Rosa's assessment is qualified rather than wholly favorable or unfavorable.

sentence: Rosa llevó un cuaderno de riego; Ana consultó ese cuaderno, a partir de cuyo registro calculó un intervalo de tres días entre los riegos anotados el lunes y el jueves, sin saber si hubo otros.
part_of_speech: evidential-basis prepositional locution and masculine singular possessive relative determiner
grammar: A partir de marks the evidence basis, and cuyo links registro to the notebook. Ana calculates the interval between two recorded waterings without concluding that no other watering occurred.
register: Careful written account of reasoning from a household record.
note: Riego = watering; registro = record. The three-day interval concerns the Monday and Thursday entries.

sentence: La comida del domingo será a las cuatro; hoy sábado llamé a mi hermana Ana para anticipárselo, antes de que ella comprara los ingredientes, y ella anotó la hora.
meaning: tell her about it in advance
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached recipient replacement se and propositional direct-object lo
grammar: Anticipar means communicating information before the relevant event. Se identifies Ana as the listener, and lo represents the stated Sunday meal time.
register: Neutral family coordination.
note: Ingredientes = ingredients. The Saturday call precedes both Ana's shopping and Sunday's meal.

sentence: Rosa escribió el resumen del paseo y me dio una copia para Luis; él me la pidió hoy y voy a remitírsela esta tarde, sin cambiar el texto.
part_of_speech: nonpronominal infinitive verb with attached recipient replacement se and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Remitir means forwarding a document here. Rosa wrote the summary, the speaker forwards its copy, se identifies Luis as recipient, and la represents copia.
register: Neutral to somewhat formal document forwarding.
note: Resumen = summary; copia = copy. Remitir a document differs from remitirse a a document to consult it.

sentence: La directora del coro expresó su confianza en Luis y me pidió transmitírsela antes del concierto; yo hablé con él y aclaré que esas palabras de apoyo eran de ella.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached recipient replacement se and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Transmitir conveys expressed confidence rather than a physical object. La represents the director's confianza, se identifies Luis, and the speaker serves as intermediary.
register: Neutral supportive communication in a choir.
note: Directora del coro = choir director; palabras de apoyo = words of support. The director originates the reassurance.

sentence: El reloj era de Ana; Pedro lo había guardado sin su permiso y ella no pudo usarlo durante una semana; ayer Pedro decidió restituírselo y se lo entregó esa tarde.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached return-recipient replacement se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Restituir restores a withheld possession to its owner. Se identifies Ana as the rightful return recipient and lo represents her watch; Pedro's subsequent delivery establishes the return.
register: Somewhat formal account of restoring a private possession.
note: Ana owned the watch throughout. Pedro's keeping it without permission prevented her use for a week.

sentence: Clara perteneció al coro durante tres años, dejó de asistir seis meses para cuidar a su mamá y decidió reintegrarse al grupo; ayer volvió al ensayo y cantó con sus compañeros.
part_of_speech: pronominal infinitive with attached lexical se and governed a complement
grammar: Reintegrarse a means returning to a group or activity after an absence. Se belongs to the pronominal lexical construction; it is neither a replacement recipient nor literal self-directed bodily action.
register: Neutral account of returning to a cultural group.
note: Perteneció al coro = belonged to the choir. Clara's return is confirmed by attending and singing at yesterday's rehearsal.

sentence: El premio del concurso de dibujo de nuestro club era un juego de acuarelas; el jurado decidió adjudicárselo a Ana por el uso del color, el criterio anunciado, y la entrega será mañana.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached award-recipient replacement se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Adjudicar makes the award decision. Se identifies Ana, and lo represents the prize; tomorrow's delivery remains distinct from the jury's completed decision.
register: Neutral to formal account of a club prize decision.
note: Juego de acuarelas = watercolor set; jurado = judging panel. Color use was the announced criterion.

sentence: Marta coordina la cena del grupo y debe repartir las tareas; la preparación del arroz decidió asignársela a Luis, quien aceptó encargarse de ella y ya puso el agua a calentar.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached assignee replacement se and feminine singular task direct-object la
grammar: Asignar allocates a responsibility rather than handing over an object. Se identifies Luis as assignee, and la represents la preparación del arroz; his acceptance and initial action are separately stated.
register: Neutral coordination of a shared meal.
note: Encargarse de una tarea = take responsibility for a task. Marta allocates the work, and Luis performs the rice preparation.

sentence: La elección de la ruta me correspondía como coordinadora del paseo; decidí delegársela a Nora, que aceptó elegir entre las dos opciones aprobadas, mientras yo conservo la responsabilidad general y el control del presupuesto.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached delegate replacement se and feminine singular decision direct-object la
grammar: Delegar entrusts the route decision to another performer. La represents elección and se identifies Nora; the speaker retains overall responsibility and budget control, and Nora's choice is limited to two approved options.
register: Neutral explanation of bounded group coordination.
note: Presupuesto = budget. Nora receives a defined decision task rather than unlimited authority over the outing.

sentence: Mi mamá viajará del lunes al viernes y dejará sus plantas en casa; su cuidado diario quedará a cargo de mi hermano Luis: ella decidió encomendárselo y él aceptó regarlas según sus indicaciones.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached entrusted-person replacement se and masculine singular responsibility direct-object lo
grammar: Encomendar entrusts an ongoing responsibility. Lo represents cuidado diario and se identifies Luis; the plants stay at home rather than being transferred as his possessions.
register: Neutral family arrangement.
note: Regarlas = water the plants; indicaciones = instructions. The stated care period runs from Monday through Friday.

sentence: Mi papá valora el respeto a los turnos y procura inculcárselo a mi hermano pequeño con su propio ejemplo: siempre espera para hablar; mi hermano todavía interrumpe a veces.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached learner replacement se and masculine singular principle direct-object lo
grammar: Inculcar develops a principle through teaching and example. Lo represents respeto a los turnos and se identifies the younger brother; the father's example is actual, while complete uptake is explicitly absent.
register: Neutral family account of teaching a social habit.
note: Respeto a los turnos = respect for taking turns. Procura marks an effort rather than a guarantee of learning.

sentence: Nora le pidió a Luis dos horas de ayuda para mover sus muebles; él tenía toda la tarde libre, pero decidió escatimársela: solo la ayudó cinco minutos y dejó casi todo sin mover.
meaning: give her too little of it
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached affected-beneficiary replacement se and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Escatimar reduces help below what should be given in the stated situation. La represents ayuda and se identifies Nora; Luis's available afternoon distinguishes withholding from inability.
register: Neutral criticism of inadequate practical help.
note: Muebles = furniture. Nora requested two hours; five minutes left almost all the moving unfinished.

sentence: Luis y Pedro habían acordado compartir la limpieza de la cocina; Luis decidió endilgársela completa a Pedro sin consultarlo y se fue a pasear, mientras Pedro acabó lavando todo solo.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached burdened-person replacement se and feminine singular task direct-object la
grammar: Endilgar presents an unwelcome burden imposed on another person. La represents limpieza and se identifies Pedro; the unilateral full assignment violates their stated agreement to share.
register: Colloquial critical account of household work.
note: Sin consultarlo = without consulting Pedro. Luis goes out while Pedro performs all the cleanup.

sentence: El error del cartel era la fecha: decía viernes en vez de sábado; Rosa decidió imputárselo a Luis porque lo vio escribirla, aunque no sabe si alguien la cambió después.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached attributed-responsibility replacement se and masculine singular error direct-object lo
grammar: Imputar attributes responsibility for a mistake. Lo represents error and se identifies Luis; Rosa's observation supports her attribution but the possible later alteration remains unresolved.
register: Somewhat formal attribution in an everyday disagreement.
note: Cartel = poster; escribirla refers to writing the date. Attribution does not itself prove who caused the wrong date.

sentence: En nuestro club, Marta decide quién usa el salón fuera del horario habitual; Luis pidió permiso para ensayar el domingo, pero ella resolvió denegárselo porque el grupo ya había reservado ese día para limpiar.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached requester replacement se and masculine singular permission direct-object lo
grammar: Denegar refuses a requested permission. Se identifies Luis as the affected requester and lo represents permiso; Marta's stated club role gives her authority over this request.
register: Formal refusal within an ordinary club arrangement.
note: Fuera del horario habitual = outside normal hours. The refusal concerns Sunday's rehearsal request.

sentence: El dibujo era de Ana y ella lo llevaba en su carpeta; vi a Luis sustraérselo sin que ella se diera cuenta, y después él me mostró el dibujo que había escondido en su mochila.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached affected-holder replacement se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Sustraer describes covert taking from a holder. Se identifies Ana as the affected holder and lo represents her drawing; Luis completes the taking and conceals the drawing.
register: Somewhat formal firsthand account of a concealed taking.
note: Carpeta = folder; mochila = backpack. Ana remains unaware during the taking, which the narrator witnesses.

sentence: Esa noche, Rosa estudiaba con la única lámpara de su cuarto; su hermano se la llevó para leer y acabó por privarla de luz para estudiar, así que ella dejó la tarea hasta el día siguiente.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached feminine singular personal direct-object la and governed de complement
grammar: Privar a alguien de algo makes Rosa the direct object, represented by la. De luz identifies the resource removed from her; her brother is the depriving actor.
register: Neutral account of a household consequence.
note: Rosa was using the room's only lamp at night. Losing its light prevents her from continuing the stated study task.

sentence: Rosa es dueña de este marco de madera y me pidió quitarle la pintura vieja; empecé por despojarlo de esa capa y ahora la madera está descubierta.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached masculine singular inanimate direct-object lo and governed de complement
grammar: Despojar strips a thing of its covering here. Lo represents marco as the affected direct object, and de esa capa names the removed layer of old paint.
register: Careful account of a home craft task.
note: Marco = frame; capa = layer; madera descubierta = exposed wood. Rosa owns the frame, and the speaker removes its covering at her request.

sentence: Ana tenía asignada la limpieza del salón de hoy; como coordinadora del taller, decidí eximirla de esa tarea porque ya había limpiado ayer, pero ella sigue encargada de guardar los materiales.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached feminine singular personal direct-object la and governed de complement
grammar: Eximir releases a person from an obligation. La represents Ana as direct object, and de esa tarea identifies today's cleaning duty; her materials-storage duty remains.
register: Neutral to formal explanation of a workshop duty adjustment.
note: The speaker coordinates the workshop and releases Ana only from today's cleaning. The participle of eximir is eximido.

sentence: En nuestro círculo de lectura, cada participante debe presentar un comentario escrito en cada reunión; hoy Rosa, la coordinadora, decidió dispensarme de ese requisito solo en esta reunión porque ayer presenté el mío en una sesión adicional, pero sigo participando en la conversación.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person singular personal direct-object me and governed de complement
grammar: Dispensar releases someone from a requirement in this use. Me represents the speaker as direct object; de ese requisito identifies the written-comment obligation.
