The requirement normally applies at every meeting, and Rosa grants an exception for today's meeting while conversation participation continues.
register: Careful explanation of an exception within a reading group.
note: Círculo de lectura = reading group; requisito = requirement; sesión adicional = extra session. El mío refers to the speaker's written comment submitted at yesterday's extra session.

sentence: El lunes, el viento tiró y rompió dos macetas de mi vecina Clara; decidí resarcirla por esa pérdida y el martes le entregué dos iguales, que ella aceptó.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached feminine singular personal direct-object la and a por loss complement
grammar: In this frame, resarcir takes the compensated person as direct object: la represents Clara. Por esa pérdida identifies the damage, and Tuesday's accepted replacement establishes compensation beyond the initial decision.
register: Somewhat formal account of voluntary neighborly compensation.
note: Macetas = flowerpots; pérdida = loss. Wind causes the damage, and the speaker supplies the replacement pots.

sentence: Como el tendedero del patio estaba roto y llovía, Nora tuvo que ingeniárselas para secar la ropa dentro de casa: tendió un cordón entre dos muebles y al día siguiente la ropa ya estaba seca.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached lexical se and fixed idiomatic las
grammar: Ingeniárselas means devising practical means to achieve something. Se belongs to the idiom; las does not replace named feminine plural objects.
register: Everyday practical account.
note: Tendedero = clothesline or drying rack; cordón = cord. Nora finds a way to dry the clothes despite the broken drying arrangement and rain.

sentence: Para la comida compartida solo teníamos arroz, frijoles y cien pesos; Elena se las arregló con eso y preparó un plato abundante para cada uno de los cuatro invitados.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative idiomatic verb phrase
grammar: Arreglárselas con expresses managing with available resources. Fixed las does not represent the ingredients, and the expression does not describe repairing them.
register: Colloquial account of practical resourcefulness.
note: Comida compartida = shared meal; abundante = generous in quantity. Four guests each receive a substantial serving.

sentence: Luis había aceptado regar el huerto durante las vacaciones de Ana, pero se desentendió de esa responsabilidad: dijo «Ya no me toca» y dejó de ir, aunque Ana seguía de viaje.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Desentenderse de means withdrawing involvement in a matter or responsibility. Here Luis's prior commitment, explicit disclaimer, and discontinued visits establish that withdrawal.
register: Critical account of an abandoned responsibility.
note: Regar = water plants; huerto = vegetable garden. Ana is still away when Luis stops carrying out the agreed task.

sentence: Desde que su hermana empezó a buscar trabajo, Rosa se desvive por ella: revisa sus solicitudes cada noche y la acompaña a las entrevistas, aunque todavía no le han ofrecido un puesto.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Desvivirse por someone expresses devoted effort for that person. The nightly reviews and accompanying visits demonstrate effort without guaranteeing the desired result.
register: Warm description of sustained family support.
note: Solicitudes = applications; entrevistas = interviews; puesto = job position. Rosa's sister is the job seeker.

sentence: En la reunión familiar me ofrecieron el micrófono para contar la discusión de mi hermana, pero decidí abstenerme de hablar de ese asunto: les dije que era privado y devolví el micrófono.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached first-person singular me
grammar: Abstenerse de takes an action that the actor deliberately refrains from performing. The offer establishes an opportunity; decidí establishes a choice.
register: Deliberate restraint in a family interaction.
note: Micrófono = microphone; asunto privado = private matter. The speaker declines to discuss the sister's argument.

sentence: Marta se cercioró de que su nombre figuraba en la lista del taller: leyó la lista completa y encontró su inscripción; todavía no sabe quién impartirá el curso.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Cerciorarse de que verifies a proposition through a check. De remains before que; checking the enrollment does not establish who will teach.
register: Neutral account of deliberate verification.
note: Figurar en una lista = appear on a list; inscripción = enrollment; impartir un curso = teach a course.

sentence: En la reunión del coro, Pablo se vanaglorió de haber organizado solo el concierto, aunque Ana reservó el salón y Julia coordinó los ensayos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal reporting verb phrase
grammar: Vanagloriarse de presents boastful self-praise. Pablo claims sole organization; the independently stated contributions limit that claim.
register: Somewhat formal, critical account of self-praise.
note: Coro = choir; ensayos = rehearsals. Pablo's boast concerns organizing this concert, not every activity of the choir.

sentence: Cuando llegamos, el museo ya había cerrado y el guardia confirmó que no volvería a abrir ese día; tras pedir entrar sin éxito, Luis se resignó a regresar el domingo, aunque quería visitarlo esa tarde.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Resignarse a expresses accepting an unwanted outcome that cannot be changed in the stated circumstances. A introduces the action Luis accepts.
register: Everyday account of reluctant acceptance.
note: Guardia = guard. Luis wanted a visit that afternoon, unsuccessfully requested entry, and accepts returning another day.

sentence: Rosa midió dos veces el ancho de la mesa delante de Pedro y mostró metro y medio en la cinta; él se obcecó en afirmar que medía solo un metro y se negó a revisar la medida.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Obcecarse en expresses obstinate persistence that prevents reconsideration. Pedro maintains a specified incorrect measurement despite the displayed contrary measurement.
register: Critical description of stubborn reasoning.
note: Ancho = width; cinta = measuring tape here; metro y medio = one and a half meters.

sentence: En la tienda, Paula se encaprichó con un florero azul; «Es puro capricho», reconoció, porque el que tiene sirve igual y había otros más baratos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Encapricharse con identifies a particular object of a whim. Paula explicitly calls her desire a capricho; the account does not infer that from a purchase.
register: Everyday discussion of a nonessential preference.
note: Florero = vase; capricho = whim. Paula already owns a vase that serves the same purpose; no purchase is reported.

sentence: En el taller, solo autorizamos a Tomás a comparar los precios de pintura, pero se extralimitó en su encargo: usó el dinero común para comprar veinte litros y tuvimos que pedir la devolución.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Extralimitarse en means going beyond the limits of one's task or authority. Comparing prices was permitted; spending the group's money was beyond that assignment.
register: Critical explanation within a shared workshop.
note: Encargo = assigned task; dinero común = shared money. The group requests a refund; receipt of that refund is not asserted.

sentence: Ana y Rosa iban a decidir solas si seguirían compartiendo casa y le pidieron a su vecino Luis que no interviniera; aun así, él decidió inmiscuirse en esa decisión y les dijo cuál de las dos debía mudarse.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached third-person se
grammar: Inmiscuirse en describes intervening in another person's matter. Ana and Rosa own this decision and explicitly exclude Luis's intervention.
register: Critical account of unsolicited involvement.
note: Intervenir = intervene; mudarse = move home. Luis is their neighbor, and his opinion crosses an explicitly stated boundary.

sentence: Mientras Ana y su hermano Luis hablaban de un problema familiar, le pidieron a su vecino Pedro que les diera privacidad; él empezó a entrometerse en la conversación, interrumpiéndolos para opinar sobre lo que debían hacer.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached third-person se
grammar: Entrometerse en describes unwelcome participation in others' affairs or conversation. Pedro's conversational intervention follows an explicit request for privacy.
register: Critical account of a conversational boundary violation.
note: Privacidad = privacy; interrumpiéndolos = interrupting Ana and Luis. The intrusion concerns speaking in their conversation, not physically entering a room.

sentence: Julia decidió preparar hoy toda la comida de mañana y se abocó a cocinar: durante tres horas lavó y picó verduras y coció frijoles; todavía falta hacer el postre.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Abocarse a expresses applying focused effort to a task. Julia's decision and three hours of work establish dedication; the dessert remains unfinished.
register: Neutral to careful description of focused practical work.
note: Picar verduras = chop vegetables; coció = cooked by boiling, from cocer; postre = dessert.

sentence: Llegué frustrado a casa por el retraso del camión y me desquité con mi hermano al contestarle de mala manera; después reconocí que había sido injusto, porque él solo me preguntó por mi día y no causó el retraso.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Desquitarse con identifies the person who receives a displaced reaction. The bus delay causes the frustration; the brother receives the unfair reply.
register: Self-critical account of a family interaction.
note: De mala manera = rudely; injusto = unfair. Frustrado identifies a male speaker.

sentence: En el ensayo del coro, Leo se ensañó con Ana por una sola entrada a destiempo: la llamó «incapaz» tres veces, aun después de que ella corrigió ese pequeño error.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Ensañarse con identifies the target of excessive harshness. Repeated personal disparagement over one corrected minor error supports that evaluation here.
register: Critical description of disproportionate verbal treatment.
note: Entrada = musical entrance here; incapaz = incapable. The excessive treatment consists of repeated spoken criticism.

sentence: Pablo dijo que quería ganarse el favor de la directora del coro y trató de congraciarse con ella: alabó exageradamente cada una de sus decisiones, pero ella no le concedió el solo que pidió.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached third-person se
grammar: Congraciarse con means gaining another person's goodwill or favor. Trató de marks Pablo's attempt; he states his intention, performs flattering acts, and does not obtain the requested solo.
register: Critical account of deliberate ingratiation.
note: Alabar = praise; solo = solo singing part. Ella and sus refer to the choir director.

sentence: Al leer la novela, me identifiqué con la protagonista: ella extraña a su familia en su primer mes fuera de casa, y yo sentí lo mismo cuando me mudé para estudiar.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Identificarse con expresses seeing one's own experience reflected in someone else. The character's homesickness parallels the speaker's explicitly described experience.
register: Personal literary discussion.
note: Novela = novel; protagonista = main character. The speaker relates to one experience rather than claiming an identical life.

sentence: Ayer, con un límite de trescientos pesos para el postre, nos ajustamos al presupuesto: en vez de pedir dos pasteles de doscientos cada uno, decidimos pedir uno; todavía podemos elegir el sabor.
part_of_speech: first-person plural preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Ajustarse a expresses conforming to a constraint. Ayer places the completed plan adjustment in the past: four hundred pesos for two cakes becomes two hundred for one, within the three-hundred-peso limit.
register: Everyday shared budgeting.
note: Presupuesto = budget; sabor = flavor. Yesterday's decision specifies one cake; its flavor remains undecided now.

sentence: En casa acordamos cenar a las ocho para comer juntos; yo solía cenar a las diez, pero me amoldé a esa rutina y esta semana cené con mi familia tres noches, aunque a veces me da hambre más tarde.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Amoldarse a expresses adapting one's behavior to an arrangement. The speaker changes the habitual dinner time to participate in the agreed family routine.
register: Everyday account of household adaptation.
note: Cenar = eat dinner. Three shared dinners demonstrate a concrete adjustment without implying that every difficulty has disappeared.

sentence: Antes del taller no conocía el bordado tradicional de la familia de la maestra; empecé a familiarizarme con él al ver una demostración y probar dos puntadas, que ahora reconozco aunque todavía no puedo hacer el diseño completo.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached first-person singular me
grammar: Familiarizarse con expresses acquiring familiarity through exposure. Él represents bordado; recognizing two stitches is narrower than making the complete design.
register: Account of an introductory cultural craft workshop.
note: Bordado = embroidery; puntada = stitch; demostración = demonstration. The practice is identified as a tradition in the teacher's family.

sentence: Después de leer una introducción a la filosofía de la ciencia, Elena empezó a adentrarse en el problema de qué cuenta como evidencia: comparó dos ensayos y anotó preguntas sobre sus argumentos, sin llegar aún a una conclusión.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached third-person se
grammar: Adentrarse en has a figurative exploration sense here. Elena moves beyond an introductory overview into a specific question, without reaching a conclusion.
register: Educated intellectual discussion.
note: Filosofía de la ciencia = philosophy of science; evidencia = evidence; ensayos = essays here; argumentos = arguments or reasons.

sentence: Mi hermano y yo aceptamos dedicar los próximos seis meses a preparar un recetario familiar y decidimos embarcarnos en ese proyecto; esta semana entrevistamos a nuestra abuela y escribimos las primeras tres recetas.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached first-person plural nos
grammar: Embarcarse en expresses undertaking a substantial project. Nos includes the speaker and the explicitly identified brother; the first interviews and recipes establish a start.
register: Everyday description of a substantial shared undertaking.
note: Recetario = recipe collection; entrevistar = interview. The agreed six months concern preparing the family collection.

sentence: El grupo del huerto propuso cerrar el acceso a todos los vecinos que no pagan cuota; en la asamblea, Ana decidió desmarcarse de esa propuesta y pidió mantener el acceso gratuito, aunque sigue apoyando el objetivo común de cuidar el huerto.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached third-person se
grammar: Desmarcarse de expresses publicly distancing oneself from a position. Ana rejects the access restriction while retaining the group's stated garden-care goal.
register: Public qualification of a group position.
note: Cuota = membership fee or contribution; asamblea = assembly. Ana's disagreement concerns access, not the shared goal of caring for the garden.

sentence: Era la primera vez que Julia asistía sola a una comida con sus nuevos vecinos; se desenvolvió bien en esa reunión: se presentó, preguntó dónde podía sentarse y participó en la conversación sin necesitar ayuda.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Desenvolverse en describes managing oneself in a situation. The evaluation is limited to this first meal and supported by Julia's observable actions.
register: Neutral description of bounded social success.
note: Se presentó = introduced herself. The sentence describes handling one social gathering, without a claim about every unfamiliar situation.

sentence: En las últimas tres semanas, Teresa se volcó en la colecta de libros del barrio: visitó a los donantes cada tarde y clasificó lo recibido los sábados; todavía no sabemos cuántos libros reuniremos al cierre.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Volcarse en expresses concentrated dedication. The repeated visits and sorting demonstrate Teresa's effort; the collection's final total remains unknown.
register: Positive account of sustained community work.
note: Colecta = collection drive; donantes = donors; al cierre = when the drive closes.

sentence: Mientras cosía el borde de un mantel, Rosa se esmeró en mantener rectas las puntadas: «Quiero cuidar cada detalle», dijo, y revisó cada tramo dos veces; aún no termina la pieza.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Esmerarse en expresses taking particular care over a task. Rosa states that intention and checks the work repeatedly; completion and perfection are not asserted.
register: Careful description of craft work.
note: Mantel = tablecloth; puntadas = stitches; rectas = straight. Cada tramo refers to each section of the sewn edge.

sentence: Al empezar sus vacaciones, Lucía dijo que quería dedicarse por completo a pintar y se entregó a la acuarela: pasó cada mañana probando mezclas de color, aunque todavía no ha terminado ningún cuadro.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Entregarse a describes wholehearted dedication to an activity. Se belongs to the dedication sense; it does not represent a person receiving an object.
register: Personal account of artistic dedication.
note: Acuarela = watercolor painting; mezclas de color = color mixtures; cuadro = painting. Dedication does not entail a completed painting.

sentence: En el ensayo del grupo, Diego tocaba el tambor más rápido que los demás; redujo la velocidad para seguir las palmas de sus compañeros y logró acoplarse al ritmo común durante la última canción.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached third-person se
grammar: Acoplarse a describes coordinating one's performance with an existing group pattern. Diego changes his speed and matches the common rhythm for one song.
register: Everyday account of group music practice.
note: Tambor = drum; palmas = rhythmic handclaps. The successful coordination is limited to the final song.

sentence: La bicicleta era mía y aún funcionaba; decidí desprenderme de ella para ayudar a mi vecina a ir al trabajo y ayer se la regalé, aunque yo también la usaba a diario.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached first-person singular me
grammar: Desprenderse de means voluntarily parting with a possession here. The speaker owns and uses the bicycle, chooses to give it up, and completes the gift to the neighbor.
register: Personal account of a voluntary useful gift.
note: A diario = daily. Ella refers to the bicycle after de; se identifies the neighbor in se la regalé.

sentence: Elena dice que el taller abrirá el domingo; yo me lo creo y reservé esa mañana para ir, aunque todavía no he comprobado el horario con quien lo coordina.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase with propositional direct-object lo
grammar: Lo resumes Elena's proposition that the workshop will open Sunday. Me belongs to the pronominal acceptance use; it is not an indirect recipient.
register: Everyday statement of personal belief.
note: Reservé esa mañana = I kept that morning available. The speaker accepts Elena's information, but independent confirmation remains pending.

sentence: Luis explicó su ausencia diciendo que el camión no había pasado; yo me lo tragué, pero después él admitió que el camión sí pasó y que él se quedó dormido.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase with propositional direct-object lo
grammar: Tragarse something figuratively means accepting it uncritically here. Lo resumes the excuse about the bus; Luis's later admission explicitly disproves that excuse.
register: Colloquial self-critical account.
note: Ausencia = absence; se quedó dormido = fell asleep. Lo refers to the excuse about the bus, rather than to food.

sentence: El texto de bienvenida del club tiene cuatro líneas; Julia se lo sabe y acaba de recitarlo completo sin mirar la hoja.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase with masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Saberse a text expresses having it memorized. Lo represents the four-line welcome text, and reciting without looking supplies concrete evidence.
register: Everyday account of memorized wording.
note: Texto de bienvenida = welcome text; recitar = recite. The claim concerns this short text, not Julia's general knowledge.

sentence: Sé que mi reputación como organizadora puede quedar dañada si el grupo falla, pero voy a jugármela por mis compañeros: los recomendaré para preparar la feria.
part_of_speech: infinitive pronominal verb with attached first-person me and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Jugarse something means putting it at risk here. La explicitly resumes reputación; por mis compañeros identifies those for whose sake the speaker accepts that risk.
register: Personal commitment involving an ordinary social risk.
note: Organizadora identifies a female organizer. The planned recommendation risks her reputation without guaranteeing that the group will succeed.

sentence: Desde que empezó sus vacaciones el lunes, mi hermano se la pasa dibujando en el patio: dedica varias horas a eso cada día, aunque también sale a caminar por la tarde.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative idiomatic verb phrase governing a gerund
grammar: Pasársela plus a gerund presents sustained or frequent activity over a period. Fixed la does not refer to a transferred object, and the expression need not exclude other activities.
register: Colloquial Mexican-compatible conversation.
note: Dibujar = draw. Several hours of daily drawing support the expression; afternoon walks remain compatible with it.

sentence: Restaurar este marco parecía fácil, pero se las trae: la pintura cubre unos relieves diminutos y llevo dos horas limpiando solo una esquina.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative idiomatic verb phrase
grammar: Traérselas describes greater difficulty than was initially apparent here. Las is fixed and does not represent objects being brought.
register: Colloquial evaluation of unexpected difficulty.
note: Restaurar = restore; relieves diminutos = tiny raised details. The speaker has cleaned only one corner in two hours.

sentence: Mañana tendré que habérmelas con el encargado del salón: insiste en cobrarnos dos horas que no usamos y no acepta revisar juntos el registro de entrada.
part_of_speech: infinitive idiomatic verb with attached first-person me and fixed las
grammar: Habérselas con means facing or dealing with someone or something difficult. Me identifies the speaker as the actor; las has no transferred-item antecedent.
register: Colloquial anticipation of a difficult exchange.
note: Encargado del salón = person responsible for the room; registro de entrada = entry record. The confrontation is pending tomorrow.

sentence: Para sacar el sofá por la puerta estrecha, me las vi y me las deseé: durante una hora tuve que girarlo una y otra vez y quitarle las patas antes de lograrlo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal component of a fixed verbal idiom
grammar: The visible me las vi y combines with me las deseé to express substantial effort. The fixed clitics do not identify things being transferred or literally wished for.
register: Colloquial account of a difficult practical task.
note: Sofá = sofa; estrecha = narrow; patas = furniture legs. The complete idiom means having a very hard time accomplishing something.

sentence: Marta afirma: «Me tengo por paciente»; sin embargo, ayer interrumpió tres veces a su sobrino mientras él intentaba explicar un juego.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal self-assessment verb phrase
grammar: Tenerse por introduces a quality one attributes to oneself. Marta supplies the self-assessment; one contrary episode limits its support without establishing a universal judgment.
register: Attributed personal assessment with a qualification.
note: Paciente = patient; sobrino = nephew. Marta is the speaker inside the quotation and the person who interrupts in the later account.

sentence: En el club, Raúl se las da de experto en ajedrez: presume que puede enseñar cualquier jugada, pero hoy no supo explicar cómo se mueve el caballo y pidió ayuda para colocar las piezas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative idiomatic verb phrase
grammar: Dárselas de presents a claimed quality with a critical tone. Fixed las does not represent gifts, and se is not replacement for a recipient le.
register: Colloquial criticism of pretended expertise.
note: Jugada = move in a game; caballo = knight in chess; piezas = chess pieces. Raúl's boast and today's specified knowledge gaps support the evaluation.

sentence: El grupo de lectura detectó doce libros dañados y cinco sin etiqueta; con el consentimiento expreso de todos sus integrantes, esos dos hallazgos se divulgan en una hoja abierta a todo el barrio, mientras los comentarios personales quedan dentro del grupo.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Divulgar makes information known to a broad audience. Esos dos hallazgos is the plural patient subject; the people communicating them remain unnamed.
register: Neutral explanation of a community information decision.
note: Hallazgos = findings; consentimiento expreso = explicit consent. The public sheet reports the two findings, while personal comments remain within the reading group.

sentence: Las dos propuestas para la convivencia, abrir el patio el sábado y prestar las sillas el domingo, se someten a revisión: tres integrantes examinarán sus horarios y costos, y la asamblea decidirá después si las aprueba.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Someter algo a revisión means submitting it for examination. Las dos propuestas is the patient subject and controls plural someten; a revisión introduces the examination process.
register: Neutral group-planning explanation.
note: Asamblea = assembly; examinar = examine. Examination by three members precedes the assembly's still-pending approval decision.

sentence: Las copias del programa fechadas el 2 y el 5 de mayo se cotejan línea por línea; en el horario, la primera dice «Salida a las nueve» y la segunda, «Salida a las diez», pero esa diferencia no aclara cuál hora quedó acordada.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Cotejar compares documents closely to identify agreements or differences. Las copias is the plural patient subject; the documents do not compare themselves.
register: Neutral explanation of a document comparison.
note: Fechadas = dated; línea por línea = line by line. The comparison establishes a difference between the copies, while the agreed departure time remains unresolved.

sentence: En casa se anotó un gasto semanal único de novecientos pesos; ahora esos novecientos pesos se desglosan en seiscientos de comida y trescientos de productos de limpieza, que juntos dan el total anotado.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Desglosar una cantidad en componentes means breaking a total into its component amounts. Esos novecientos pesos controls plural desglosan; the person calculating remains unnamed.
register: Everyday household expense explanation.
note: Seiscientos plus trescientos equals novecientos. Productos de limpieza = cleaning supplies.

sentence: En la charla, Ana propuso abrir el patio los domingos para leer juntos y Luis objetó que faltaban sillas; los puntos principales se sintetizan así: «Ana propuso lectura dominical en el patio; Luis objetó que faltaban sillas».
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Sintetizar condenses the essential points. Los puntos principales is the plural patient subject; the summary retains both the proposal and Luis's objection in their original past time frame.
register: Concise written summary of an ordinary discussion.
note: Dominical = Sunday-related; objetó = raised an objection. Faltaban sillas reports the shortage Luis identified during the discussion.

sentence: El relato dice: «Marta llegó el lunes. Pedro llegó el lunes. Los dos quizá vuelvan el viernes»; esas tres frases se condensan en «Marta y Pedro llegaron el lunes y quizá vuelvan el viernes».
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Condensar wording makes it more compact. Esas tres frases is the plural patient subject; en introduces the resulting formulation.
register: Written editing explanation.
note: Both versions retain Marta and Pedro, Monday's arrival, Friday's possible return, and quizá. This use concerns wording rather than vapor.

sentence: Las afirmaciones «Nadie vino el martes» y «La sala cerró el martes a las cuatro» se rebaten con el registro de ese día, que anota la visita de Ana a las tres y el cierre a las seis; aún falta explicar por qué la sala estaba vacía a las cinco.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Rebatir challenges an argument or claim through opposing reasons or evidence. Las afirmaciones is the plural patient subject; both claims and the cited record concern the same Tuesday.
register: Reasoned discussion of two bounded claims.
note: Registro = written record. The evidence addresses Tuesday's visit and closing time; the empty room at five still needs an explanation.

sentence: El comité del club decidió retirar del aviso interno de Julia las frases «El cierre fue injusto» y «Pido cambiar al comité»; esos pasajes se censuran antes de repartir el texto, aunque Julia pide que permanezcan.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Censurar means suppressing passages here. Esos pasajes is the plural patient subject; the committee's decision and the author's objection are explicit.
register: Neutral account of an internal club dispute.
note: Aviso interno = internal notice; pasajes = passages. The two quoted phrases are removed rather than merely criticized.

sentence: Por acuerdo de la familia, las cartas de la abuela se preservan en una caja dentro de un cajón, separadas de los objetos pesados para evitar nuevos dobleces; sus bordes ya están frágiles.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Preservar emphasizes keeping something from damage. Las cartas is the plural patient subject; unnamed people carry out the storage decision.
register: Neutral family explanation.
note: Cajón = drawer; dobleces = folds; bordes = edges. The storage choice aims to avoid further folds in fragile family letters.

sentence: La escuela prestó al grupo del taller dos tambores y tres flautas de su propiedad; como la lluvia alcanza la mesa del patio, los instrumentos se resguardan dentro del salón hasta devolverlos mañana.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Resguardar protects or shelters something from exposure. Los instrumentos is the plural patient subject; the school explicitly owns and lends them, while the workshop group has temporary custody.
register: Ordinary workshop coordination.
note: Tambores = drums; flautas = flutes; de su propiedad = owned by the school. Indoor storage responds to rain reaching the patio table; the instruments are due back tomorrow.

sentence: De los treinta pliegos de cartón de la familia, hoy se usaron diez para hacer máscaras; los otros veinte se almacenan en el armario del comedor para construir títeres el próximo domingo y siguen perteneciendo a la familia.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Almacenar keeps materials in a place for later use. Los otros veinte resumes pliegos de cartón and controls plural almacenan.
register: Everyday family craft planning.
note: Pliegos de cartón = sheets of cardboard; máscaras = masks; títeres = puppets. Twenty sheets remain for Sunday's activity.

sentence: En el taller se confeccionan dos blusas para Ana y Julia a partir de tela de algodón, siguiendo el dibujo de ambas, con cuello redondo y mangas cortas; las piezas ya están cosidas, pero faltan los botones.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Confeccionar garments means making them from material according to a design. Dos blusas is the plural patient subject; para identifies the intended wearers.
register: Neutral description of clothing production.
note: Tela de algodón = cotton fabric; cuello redondo = round neckline; cosidas = sewn. The blouses still need their buttons.

sentence: Las cuatro patas y el tablero, comprados ya hechos, se ensamblan con tornillos para formar la mesa de la cocina; la unión de las piezas está en marcha y todavía falta pintar la mesa.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Ensamblar joins separate parts into a whole. Las cuatro patas y el tablero is the coordinated patient subject and takes plural ensamblan.
register: Ordinary household craft explanation.
note: Tablero = tabletop panel; tornillos = screws; unión = joining. The parts were purchased already made, and painting remains pending.

sentence: Para la salsa de la comida familiar, las nueces enteras se trituran en un mortero hasta quedar en fragmentos pequeños y desiguales; se busca una textura gruesa, con trocitos visibles y sin convertirlas en polvo.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Triturar breaks food into small fragments by crushing. Las nueces enteras is the plural patient subject; the resulting texture remains coarse.
register: Ordinary cooking description.
note: Nueces = walnuts; mortero = mortar; trocitos = small pieces; polvo = powder. The walnuts start whole and end as visible coarse fragments.

sentence: Antes de preparar el pastel, la harina y la cocoa se tamizan con una malla fina: los grumos visibles quedan en la malla y debajo caen los ingredientes sueltos, sin esos pequeños bloques.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Tamizar passes dry ingredients through a fine mesh. La harina y la cocoa forms a coordinated plural patient subject.
register: Ordinary baking explanation.
note: Malla fina = fine mesh; grumos = lumps; cocoa = cocoa powder. The visible lumps remain above while the loose ingredients pass through.

sentence: La mezcla de harina y agua se amasa a mano sobre la mesa, presionándola y doblándola hasta obtener una masa uniforme para el pan; el horno sigue apagado y el pan todavía no está hecho.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Amasar works a mixture by pressing and folding it into dough. La mezcla is the singular patient subject and controls amasa.
register: Ordinary home-baking description.
note: Masa = dough; presionar = press; doblar = fold here. Kneading is underway, while baking has not begun.

sentence: Las superficies ásperas de la mesa y del banco, ambos de madera y ya armados, se pulen con lija para que resulten suaves al tacto; todavía falta aplicarles una capa de barniz.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Pulir makes a rough surface smooth. Las superficies ásperas is the plural patient subject; ambos de madera y ya armados describes the wooden table and bench after assembly.
register: Ordinary craft-work explanation.
note: Lija = sandpaper; suave al tacto = smooth to the touch; barniz = varnish. Surface smoothing precedes the still-pending coat.

sentence: En el taller se barnizaron hoy con una capa transparente los dos marcos de madera de mi familia para proteger su superficie; el trabajo ya terminó y ambos conservan su color natural.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Barnizar coats something with varnish. Los dos marcos de madera is the plural patient subject; barnizaron presents today's coating as completed.
register: Neutral account of completed craft work.
note: Marco = frame; capa transparente = transparent coat. Both family frames have received their coat and retain their natural color.

sentence: En el taller familiar se restauran una caja y un marco de la abuela: se reparan las esquinas rotas y se recupera el acabado que aparece en una foto antigua, pero la caja conserva una mancha de los años de uso.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Restaurar repairs objects to recover an earlier appearance. Una caja y un marco is a coordinated plural patient subject; retaining the box's stain limits the restoration.
register: Neutral family craft description.
note: Esquinas = corners; acabado = finish. An old photograph supplies the earlier appearance, and the box retains a visible trace of use.

sentence: Las dos fundas de tela para las sillas del patio se impermeabilizan ahora con un recubrimiento; según quien las hizo, el tratamiento busca reducir el paso del agua, pero todavía no se han probado bajo la lluvia.
meaning: are treated to resist water penetration
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Impermeabilizar applies a treatment intended to prevent water penetration. Las dos fundas is the plural patient subject; the maker's stated purpose remains distinct from tested effectiveness.
register: Ordinary description of household craft work.
note: Fundas = covers; recubrimiento = coating. Treatment is underway, and performance under rain remains untested.

sentence: En la tienda de telas se asesora a Ana y a Luis sobre qué tela elegir para sus cortinas; ambos comparan dos muestras, pero la decisión de compra sigue siendo de ellos y hoy aún no han comprado nada.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Asesorar a alguien sobre algo means giving someone informed advice about a matter. Ana and Luis are personal direct objects; impersonal asesora remains singular.
register: Neutral customer-service description.
note: Cortinas = curtains; muestras = samples. Ana and Luis retain the purchasing decision and have not bought anything yet.

sentence: En el teatro del barrio se capacita a los voluntarios Ana y Luis para doblar los programas mediante una práctica con un modelo; cada uno ya dobló un programa siguiendo ese modelo y el reparto al público será mañana.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Capacitar a alguien para una tarea means preparing someone through training. Ana and Luis are personal direct objects, so impersonal capacita remains singular.
register: Neutral description of ordinary volunteer preparation.
note: Doblar = fold here; programa = printed theater program; reparto = distribution. Each volunteer has folded one program using the model.

sentence: En el taller de pintura se instruye a Rosa y a Iván en el uso de esponjas para extender pintura sobre cartón; ambos observan una demostración y todavía no han trabajado sin ayuda.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Instruir a alguien en el uso de algo gives instruction in using something. Rosa and Iván are personal direct objects; en introduces the content of instruction.
register: Neutral description of an ordinary art lesson.
note: Esponjas = sponges; extender pintura = spread paint. Observing the demonstration does not establish independent performance.

sentence: Según el acuerdo aprobado por todos los integrantes del huerto compartido, se faculta a los integrantes Inés y Pablo para elegir la fecha de la jornada de limpieza, pero no para cambiar las cuotas; todavía no han elegido el día.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Facultar a alguien para hacer algo grants authority for that action. Inés and Pablo are personal direct objects; their authority covers the cleanup date and excludes changing contributions.
register: Formal wording within a private shared arrangement.
note: Huerto compartido = shared garden; cuotas = agreed contributions; jornada de limpieza = cleanup day. Authority has been granted, while choosing the date remains pending.

sentence: Después de seis meses de ausencia, Ana y Luis solicitaron volver al coro; con el acuerdo del grupo, hoy se reincorpora a ambos al coro, aunque su primer ensayo de regreso será mañana.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative transitive lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Reincorporar a alguien a un grupo restores that person's membership or participation. A ambos is the personal direct object; al coro introduces the destination group.
register: Neutral cultural-group update.
note: Ambos refers to Ana and Luis. Their return to the group is agreed today, and their first returning rehearsal is tomorrow.

sentence: Los organizadores de la feria acordaron previamente pagar doscientos pesos a cada colaborador por montar los puestos; hoy se remunera a Julia y a Raúl por ese trabajo ya terminado, y cada uno recibe la cantidad pactada.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Remunerar a alguien por un trabajo pays that person for work. Julia and Raúl are personal direct objects; por introduces the completed task that earns the agreed payment.
register: Neutral description of an agreed work-payment arrangement.
note: Montar los puestos = set up the stalls; pactada = agreed. Each collaborator receives two hundred pesos for the completed setup.

sentence: Por decisión de los organizadores del festival, se recompensa a Elena y a Mario con dos entradas para cada uno por quedarse una hora extra a recoger las sillas; esa ayuda fue voluntaria y no tenía un pago pactado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Recompensar a alguien con algo por una acción rewards someone with a benefit for that action. Elena and Mario are personal direct objects; con introduces the tickets.
register: Neutral account of a volunteer reward.
note: Entradas = admission tickets. Each helper receives two tickets for an extra hour collecting chairs.

sentence: En el club se acordó guardar silencio durante la lectura; hoy se amonesta a Ana y a Luis con una advertencia por interrumpir en voz alta tres veces, pero ambos pueden quedarse y participar en la charla posterior.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Amonestar warns or reprimands someone for conduct. Ana and Luis are personal direct objects, so impersonal amonesta remains singular.
register: Moderately formal wording for a club warning.
note: Advertencia = warning; charla posterior = discussion afterward. The repeated interruptions trigger a warning while permission to remain is retained.

sentence: El grupo de teatro acordó que para actuar el domingo había que asistir a dos ensayos; Ana y Luis, que solicitaron participar, solo asistieron a uno, así que se excluye a ambos de esa función, aunque pueden acudir como público.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Excluir a alguien de una actividad keeps that person out of it. A ambos is the personal direct object; de esa función identifies the activity excluded.
register: Neutral explanation of a private group's participation arrangement.
note: Actuar = perform on stage; público = audience. The agreed threshold is two rehearsals, while Ana and Luis attended one.

sentence: En la casa compartida del grupo de teatro se acoge a las visitantes Rosa e Inés: reciben una bienvenida y un cuarto prestado del viernes al domingo, durante las dos noches de su visita, sin que el cuarto pase a ser suyo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Acoger receives people hospitably and offers them a place here. Rosa and Inés are personal direct objects; impersonal acoge remains singular.
register: Neutral social hospitality description.
note: Bienvenida = welcome; cuarto prestado = room lent temporarily. The visit lasts two nights, and ownership is not transferred.

sentence: En el taller de poesía se alienta a Ana y a Luis, que dudan en participar, a leer cuatro versos propios con la opción de detenerse; Ana acepta, Luis prefiere observar y se respeta su decisión.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Alentar a alguien a hacer algo encourages that person to act. Ana and Luis are personal direct objects; the second a introduces the encouraged action.
register: Supportive cultural-workshop interaction.
note: Versos propios = lines of their own poetry. Participation is optional: Ana accepts, and Luis's choice to observe is respected.

sentence: Mediante un mensaje de la coordinación del coro, se convoca a las integrantes Ana y Julia a una charla el viernes a las seis en el salón para elegir las canciones de junio; todavía ninguna ha confirmado su asistencia.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Convocar a alguien a una reunión calls that person to a gathering. Ana and Julia are personal direct objects; a una charla introduces the event.
register: Neutral group-coordination message.
note: Coordinación del coro = choir coordination; asistencia = attendance. The invitation specifies time, place, and purpose, while attendance remains unconfirmed.

sentence: Al terminar la primera charla del círculo de escritura, se emplaza a Elena y a Raúl a una nueva reunión el sábado a las diez en la biblioteca para revisar sus cambios; ambos aceptan la cita voluntariamente y ese día todavía no llega.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Emplazar a alguien a una reunión sets a further meeting for that person here. Elena and Raúl are personal direct objects; the event complement gives the agreed checkpoint.
register: Formal wording in a voluntary cultural arrangement.
note: Círculo de escritura = writing group; cambios = revisions here. Both accept the specified appointment, whose date remains future.

sentence: La asamblea había permitido a Ana anunciar las fechas en nombre del club; por un nuevo acuerdo de esa misma asamblea, ahora se desautoriza a Ana como portavoz sobre ese asunto y se retira ese permiso, aunque puede expresar su opinión personal.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Desautorizar removes previously held authority here. Ana is the personal direct object; the withdrawal concerns speaking for the club about dates.
register: Formal description of a private group's representation decision.
note: Portavoz = spokesperson; en nombre del club = on behalf of the club. Ana's permission to announce dates is withdrawn, while personal expression remains allowed.

sentence: En la explicación «Hoy llegaron tarde dos camiones; por eso todos los camiones llegan tarde y mañana ninguno será puntual» se incurre en dos generalizaciones sin apoyo: observar dos llegadas de hoy no basta para afirmar que todos los camiones llegan tarde ni para asegurar lo que pasará mañana.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive lexical verb with governed en in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Incurrir en un error means committing an error. Dos generalizaciones follows governed en and does not control agreement; impersonal incurre has no grammatical subject.
register: Reasoned critique of a short explanation.
note: Generalizaciones sin apoyo = unsupported generalizations. Two observed arrivals establish neither every bus's usual punctuality nor tomorrow's outcomes.

sentence: En el barrio se pugna por conservar el acceso gratuito al huerto mediante turnos de trabajo voluntario y donaciones para las herramientas; otra propuesta es cobrar entrada para cubrir esos gastos, y la decisión sigue pendiente.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive lexical verb with governed por in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Pugnar por hacer algo expresses sustained effort toward a goal. Por conservar introduces the pursued outcome; impersonal pugna has no grammatical subject.
register: Educated description of a community disagreement.
note: Huerto = garden for growing plants; herramientas = tools. Volunteer shifts and donations support free access, while charging admission remains a competing proposal.

sentence: En la reunión del club de ajedrez se aboga por abrir el salón el domingo, porque tres integrantes trabajan los sábados; otros prefieren mantener el sábado y todavía no se ha votado el cambio.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive lexical verb with governed por in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Abogar por una opción advocates that option. Por abrir introduces the supported action; the unnamed advocates are not grammatical subjects.
register: Educated wording in an ordinary club discussion.
note: The Sunday proposal has an explicit scheduling reason. Support for it is distinct from the still-pending vote.

sentence: En el taller se acordó dejar media mesa libre para quien llegue después; se vela por el cumplimiento de ese acuerdo revisando el espacio al inicio de cada sesión, aunque aún pueden surgir desacuerdos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive lexical verb with governed por in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Velar por algo attends to its protection or fulfillment. El cumplimiento de ese acuerdo follows por and is not a passive subject; impersonal vela remains singular.
register: Neutral explanation of care for a shared arrangement.
note: Media mesa = half the table; para quien llegue después = for whoever arrives later; cumplimiento = fulfillment; surgir = arise. Checking supports the agreement without guaranteeing that disagreements never occur.

sentence: En el grupo de teatro se apuesta por ensayar las escenas en grupos pequeños, porque en la prueba de ayer así hubo tiempo para cada participante; la elección ya está hecha, pero aún no sabemos si mejorará la función completa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive lexical verb with governed por in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Apostar por figuratively backs an approach because it seems promising. Por ensayar introduces the selected method; no money wager is described.
register: Educated figurative wording in practical artistic planning.
note: Escenas = scenes. Yesterday's small-group trial allowed time for each person; improvement of the whole performance remains uncertain.

sentence: En la cocina del centro vecinal, se perdió la página con las cantidades de la receta del pastel; se recurre al cuaderno de Rosa y ya se usan sus medidas para preparar la mezcla, aunque ese cuaderno no indica el tiempo de horneado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive lexical verb with governed a in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Recurrir a algo turns to it as a resource. Al cuaderno is a governed resource complement, not a personal indirect object or passive subject; impersonal recurre is singular.
register: Ordinary explanation of a practical cooking workaround.
note: Centro vecinal = neighborhood center; horneado = baking. The recipe's quantities page was lost; Rosa's notebook supplies quantities already in use but leaves baking time unspecified.

sentence: Mis zapatos tenían las suelas gruesas cuando los compré; después de dos años de caminar a diario, se me desgastaron y ahora están lisas y mucho más delgadas.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner change construction
grammar: Las suelas is the changing subject and controls plural desgastaron. Me identifies their affected owner; repeated walking supplies the stated cause.
register: Everyday account of wear through use.
note: Suelas = shoe soles; gruesas = thick; lisas = smooth; delgadas = thin. Desgastarse describes gradual deterioration through use.

sentence: Mi blusa era azul intenso; se me destiñó durante el lavado de ayer y salió azul pálido, algo que no esperaba.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner color-loss construction
grammar: Mi blusa is the subject of destiñó; me marks its affected owner. Desteñirse has the third-person preterite stem destiñ-.
register: Ordinary account of an unexpected laundry result.
note: Azul intenso = deep blue; azul pálido = pale blue; lavado = wash. The color loss happened during yesterday's wash.

sentence: Al revisar hoy mi mantel, noté que el borde se me había deshilachado durante los últimos meses: antes estaba parejo y ahora le cuelgan varios hilos sueltos.
part_of_speech: past participle in a third-person singular pluperfect indicative pronominal construction
grammar: El borde is the subject of se me había deshilachado; me identifies the affected owner. The compound participle remains invariant after había.
register: Everyday observation of household fabric.
note: Mantel = tablecloth; borde = edge; parejo = even; hilos sueltos = loose threads. The speaker notices today a change that developed over several months.

sentence: Mi maqueta de una casa cayó de la mesa y se deshizo en sus piezas de cartón; recogí del piso las cuatro paredes y el techo, todos enteros.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an inanimate disintegration construction
grammar: Mi maqueta is the subject of se deshizo. Deshacerse here means coming apart into components; it does not use the disposal frame deshacerse de algo.
register: Ordinary account of a craft mishap.
note: Maqueta = scale model; piezas de cartón = cardboard pieces; paredes = walls; techo = roof. The recovered components remained whole.

sentence: La repisa larga de mi librero estaba recta; después de varios meses con todos mis diccionarios encima, se combó y ahora veo una curva hacia abajo en el centro, aunque sigue entera.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an inanimate shape-change construction
grammar: La repisa is the subject undergoing the change. Combarse describes bending into a curve; the sentence separately states that the shelf remains whole.
register: Neutral household observation.
note: Repisa = shelf; librero = bookcase; recta = straight; curva hacia abajo = downward curve. The dictionaries supply the stated load.

sentence: Hoy revisé mi cómoda antigua: la pintura, antes lisa, se ha cuarteado con los años y ahora forma una red de grietas finas, aunque sigue pegada a la madera.
part_of_speech: past participle in a third-person singular present perfect indicative pronominal construction
grammar: La pintura is the changing subject. Se ha cuarteado describes deterioration over the years reaching its observed present condition; the participle is invariant after ha.
register: Neutral description of an old household object.
note: Cómoda = chest of drawers; red de grietas finas = network of fine cracks; pegada = attached. The paint remains attached to the wood.

sentence: Mi bote de metal chocó contra la pata de la mesa mientras lo llevaba al patio; se me abolló de un lado, pero todavía cierra bien y lo sigo usando para guardar semillas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner deformation construction
grammar: Mi bote is the subject of abolló; me identifies its affected owner and carrier. The collision is stated separately from the resulting dent.
register: Everyday description of minor household damage.
note: Bote de metal = metal container; pata de la mesa = table leg; semillas = seeds. The container still closes and remains in use.

sentence: Mi espejo estaba liso y sin marcas; al rozar con la hebilla de mi cinturón mientras lo cargaba, se me rayó y quedó una línea visible en la superficie, sin ninguna grieta.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner surface-damage construction
grammar: Mi espejo is the subject undergoing scratching. Me marks the affected owner; contact with the buckle supplies the stated circumstance.
register: Ordinary account of limited surface damage.
note: Espejo = mirror; rozar con = brush against; hebilla = buckle; cinturón = belt; grieta = crack. The damage is a visible surface line.

sentence: Vi que mi caja de madera golpeó el escalón al caer; se me astilló una esquina y quedaron pequeñas puntas de madera y varios fragmentos junto a ella.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner material-change construction
grammar: Una esquina is the subject of astilló; me identifies the affected owner of the box. The corner develops small pointed fragments after the impact.
register: Neutral account of a household mishap.
note: Escalón = step; esquina = corner; puntas de madera = pointed pieces of wood; fragmentos = fragments.

sentence: Mi taza de cerámica resbaló de mis manos y golpeó el fregadero; se me despostilló del borde y perdió un pedacito, pero no se hizo añicos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner chipping construction
grammar: Mi taza is the understood subject of despostilló; me marks its affected owner. The stated result is the loss of a small piece from the rim.
register: Ordinary Mexican-compatible household vocabulary.
note: Cerámica = ceramic; borde = rim here; pedacito = small piece; hacerse añicos = shatter into pieces. The cup is chipped rather than shattered.

sentence: La costura de mi pantalón estaba cerrada esta mañana; mientras lo llevaba puesto, se me descosió y ahora hay una abertura con el hilo suelto a un lado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-wearer seam-opening construction
grammar: La costura is the subject of descosió. Me identifies the affected owner and wearer; it does not mark a recipient or a person taking clothing off.
register: Everyday clothing problem.
note: Costura = seam; abertura = opening; hilo suelto = loose thread; lo llevaba puesto = I was wearing it.

sentence: Jalé la manija para abrir el cajón de mi escritorio, pero se me atascó a la mitad; intenté jalarlo otra vez y ya no se deslizó ni un centímetro.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-user jamming construction
grammar: El cajón is the subject of atascó; me identifies its affected owner and user. The speaker's attempts to pull it are separate from the drawer's jamming.
register: Everyday Mexican household description.
note: Jalar = pull; manija = handle; cajón = drawer; deslizarse = slide. The drawer stops halfway through opening.

sentence: En mi patio se obstruyó la coladera con las hojas que se juntaron durante la semana; veo el montón sobre los agujeros y el agua de la lluvia queda encharcada alrededor.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an inanimate obstruction construction
grammar: La coladera is the subject becoming blocked. The visible leaves obstruct the water's passage; this is different from a movable component jamming.
register: Neutral Mexican household observation.
note: Coladera = drain; montón = pile; agujeros = holes; encharcada = pooled. The speaker observes both the leaves and the pooled rainwater.

sentence: Guardé separados mis dos cables de sonido en una bolsa, pero durante el traslado se me enredaron entre sí; ahora forman varios nudos y no puedo conectarlos sin separarlos primero.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner entanglement construction
grammar: Mis dos cables is the subject of enredaron; me marks their affected owner. Entre sí describes the cables' entanglement, without assigning them intentional reciprocal actions.
register: Ordinary preparation for using sound equipment.
note: Cables de sonido = audio cables; traslado = transport; nudos = knots; conectar = connect. The cables were separate before transport.

sentence: Antes de empezar mi bordado, tenía seis hilos separados; al sacar la tela de la bolsa, se me enmarañaron y quedaron hechos un nudo tan apretado que ya no distinguía sus extremos.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner entanglement construction
grammar: Seis hilos is the plural changing subject; me identifies their affected owner. Enmarañarse emphasizes a dense, disordered tangle.
register: Everyday account of a craft difficulty.
note: Bordado = embroidery; tela = cloth; apretado = tight; extremos = ends. Six separate threads become one dense knot.

sentence: La cerradura de mi alacena cerraba bien antes de la mudanza; después del traslado se me desajustó y ahora el pestillo queda un poco más abajo del hueco, así que la puerta no cierra.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner loss-of-adjustment construction
grammar: La cerradura is the subject losing its adjustment; me identifies its affected owner. The bolt's mismatch with the opening makes the particular defect explicit.
register: Neutral description of a household mechanism.
note: Cerradura = lock; alacena = cupboard; pestillo = bolt or latch; hueco = opening. The account states the mismatch without identifying who caused it.

sentence: Mi mesa estaba nivelada sobre el piso de la cocina; cuando la pasé al patio, una pata quedó sobre una loseta más alta y la mesa se me desniveló: la superficie quedó inclinada y una canica rodó del centro hacia la orilla.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner loss-of-level construction
grammar: La mesa is the subject of desniveló; me identifies its affected owner. The speaker moves the table, and one higher support leaves its surface tilted.
register: Everyday household observation.
note: Nivelada = level; loseta = floor tile; inclinada = tilted; canica = marble; orilla = edge. The marble rolls across the tilted tabletop.

sentence: Yo llevaba mi charola horizontal e intentaba mantenerla así, pero una naranja rodó de pronto hacia una orilla; se me desequilibró la charola y se inclinó, aunque alcancé a sujetarla y nada cayó.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-carrier balance-change construction
grammar: La charola is the subject of desequilibró; me marks its affected owner and carrier. The orange's movement, the tilt, and the successful catch are separate events.
register: Everyday Mexican account of carrying food.
note: Horizontal = level or horizontal; rodar = roll; orilla = edge; sujetar = hold securely. Nothing falls from the tray.

sentence: Mi sombrero flexible era redondo antes del viaje; dentro de la maleta quedó aplastado bajo un libro y se me deformó: ahora tiene un lado hundido, aunque todavía me lo puedo poner.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner shape-change construction
grammar: Mi sombrero is the subject changing shape; me identifies the affected owner. The visible result is one sunken side, while continued wearability is stated separately.
register: Ordinary description of travel-related damage.
note: Sombrero = hat; flexible = bendable; redondo = round; aplastado = flattened; hundido = sunken.

sentence: Preparé un pastel para mi cumpleaños; cuando intenté cortar la primera rebanada, el pastel entero se me desmoronó, pero recogí sus trozos y migas en un tazón y pude servirlos ahí.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-person crumbling construction
grammar: El pastel entero is the explicit subject of desmoronó; me identifies its affected maker and server. Cutting the first slice is the attempted action, and crumbling is the resulting change.
register: Everyday account of serving homemade cake.
note: Pastel entero = whole cake; trozos = pieces; migas = crumbs; tazón = bowl. The cake could still be served in fragments.

sentence: Al oler el pan que horneaba mi abuela, lo conté así: «Se me agolparon los recuerdos de su cocina: la mesa de madera, las tardes de lluvia y nuestras conversaciones llegaron juntos a mi memoria».
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb in a figurative pronominal gathering construction
grammar: Los recuerdos is the subject of agolparon; me identifies the experiencer. Agolparse figuratively presents several memories arriving together rather than being received as transferred objects.
register: Personal reminiscence with figurative vocabulary.
note: Hornear = bake; agolparse = crowd together or crowd in. The narrator explicitly describes memories prompted by the smell of the grandmother's baking.

sentence: Durante los cuatro días que estuve fuera de casa no hice mis tareas domésticas y se me amontonaron: al volver tenía pendientes lavar los platos, barrer, sacar la basura y lavar la ropa.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb in a figurative affected-person accumulation construction
grammar: Mis tareas domésticas is the plural subject; me identifies the person responsible for the unfinished tasks. Amontonarse figuratively presents a backlog rather than intentional stacking.
register: Everyday account of household responsibilities.
note: Tareas domésticas = household chores; barrer = sweep; pendientes = still to be done. Four specific tasks remain after a four-day absence.

sentence: En mis cinco clases de esta semana, que debían durar una hora, se me acumularon cinco retrasos de seis minutos al llegar; como todas terminaron a la hora prevista, perdí treinta minutos de clase.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb in an affected-person cumulative-growth construction
grammar: Cinco retrasos is the subject of acumularon; me marks the person affected by the repeated lateness. Five delays of six minutes total thirty minutes.
register: Neutral reflection on a weekly study schedule.
note: Hora prevista = planned finishing time here. Each late arrival shortened attendance because the classes finished on schedule.

sentence: Yo contaba con tocar el piano en el recital del viernes, pero hoy avisaron que el único piano del salón ya no está disponible; se me esfumó esa oportunidad justo cuando ya tenía preparada mi pieza.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in a figurative affected-person disappearance construction
grammar: Esa oportunidad is the subject of esfumó; me identifies the affected prospective performer. Esfumarse figuratively expresses the opportunity's disappearance.
register: Personal account of an unexpected cultural disappointment.
note: Recital = recital; pieza = musical piece here. The expected performance depended on the only piano at the venue.

sentence: Tenía la esperanza de ver a mi hermana el domingo; tras sus dos mensajes sobre nuevos retrasos en el viaje, esa esperanza se me fue desvaneciendo, aunque todavía no sé si alcanzará a llegar.
part_of_speech: gerund in a figurative pronominal gradual-change construction
grammar: Esa esperanza is the subject of se me fue desvaneciendo. Ir plus gerund presents gradual fading; me identifies the person holding the hope.
register: Personal account of a weakening hope.
note: Tras = after; alcanzará a llegar = will manage to arrive in time. The fading hope does not settle whether the sister will arrive.

sentence: Para nuestro pícnic, Ana y yo preparamos la comida y acordamos la hora, pero una tormenta que no esperábamos cerró el parque y se nos malogró el plan; pudimos reunirnos a comer en mi casa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-planner frustrated-result construction
grammar: El plan is the subject of malogró; nos identifies Ana and the speaker as affected planners. The storm frustrates the picnic plan while the meal at home remains possible.
register: Ordinary account of an unforeseen social setback.
note: Pícnic = picnic; tormenta = storm. Preparing the food and agreeing on a time precede the park closure.

sentence: Nuestro ensayo de teatro iba a durar dos horas y recorrer las cuatro escenas, pero se truncó a los cuarenta minutos cuando una gotera inundó el escenario; salimos del salón sin ensayar las dos últimas escenas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an interrupted-activity construction
grammar: Nuestro ensayo is the subject of truncó. The activity had begun and was interrupted before its intended duration and remaining scenes were completed.
register: Neutral account of an interrupted artistic activity.
note: Escenario = stage; inundar = flood; recorrer las escenas = work through the scenes here. Two final scenes remain unrehearsed.

sentence: Al inicio del mes, los seis integrantes del círculo de lectura prometimos asistir cada sábado; nuestro compromiso se fue diluyendo: el segundo sábado asistimos cuatro y el último solo dos, aunque los seis seguimos inscritos.
part_of_speech: gerund in a figurative pronominal gradual-change construction
grammar: Nuestro compromiso is the subject of se fue diluyendo. Diluirse figuratively describes a loss of strength, supported here by declining fulfillment of a shared promise.
register: Reflective account of group participation.
note: Círculo de lectura = reading group; inscritos = registered members. Attendance falls from the initial six-person promise to four and then two.

sentence: Sobre mi visita al museo de hace veinte años, digo esto: «Antes recordaba con claridad el orden de las salas, pero esos detalles se me han ido desdibujando con el tiempo; todavía recuerdo el vestido rojo del retrato de la entrada».
part_of_speech: gerund in a figurative pronominal gradual-change construction with a present perfect auxiliary
grammar: Esos detalles is the subject of se me han ido desdibujando; me identifies the remembering narrator. The room sequence was formerly clear, while the retained portrait detail limits the stated loss of clarity.
register: Personal reminiscence with figurative vocabulary.
note: Con claridad = clearly; sala = gallery room here; retrato = portrait; orden = sequence. The narrator contrasts a formerly clear room sequence with a visual detail still remembered.

sentence: Durante la reunión del coro, Raúl dijo: «Solo Ana debería elegir las canciones»; entre Julia y Raúl se desató una discusión, porque Julia defendió una votación de todos, y la elección quedó pendiente.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in a figurative outbreak construction
grammar: Una discusión is the subject of desató. Entre Julia y Raúl identifies the participants; desatarse describes the disagreement's outbreak rather than untying something.
register: Neutral account of a group disagreement.
note: Coro = choir; votación = vote. Raúl's proposal and Julia's competing position are explicit; no song selection is settled.

sentence: Al preparar juntos una exposición, Ana aprendió a dejarle a Luis tiempo para revisar cada dibujo y él aprendió a avisarle antes de cambiar el orden; con esos ajustes se compenetraron y ahora entienden cómo trabaja el otro.
meaning: came to understand each other closely
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative pronominal verb with reciprocal meaning
grammar: Ana and Luis are the joint subjects of se compenetraron. Each adjusts to the other's working style, making the mutual understanding explicit.
register: Neutral account of artistic collaboration.
note: Exposición = exhibition; ajustes = adjustments. Ana allows review time, and Luis gives notice before changing the display order.

sentence: En su taller de encuadernación, Marta sabe coser los cuadernillos pero no diseñar las portadas, y Diego sabe diseñarlas pero no coser; se complementan: ella hace la costura de los libros de Diego y él diseña las portadas de los de ella.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative verb with a reciprocal direct-object clitic
grammar: Reciprocal se makes Marta and Diego the people complementing one another. Each supplies a skill the other lacks; neither replaces the other's contribution.
register: Neutral description of craft collaboration.
note: Encuadernación = bookbinding; cuadernillos = folded page sections; portadas = covers. Marta sews Diego's books, and Diego designs Marta's covers.

sentence: Clara y Pablo son adultos y declaran estar enamorados el uno del otro; se corresponden con cartas cariñosas que cada uno escribe para el otro.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative verb with a reciprocal personal direct-object clitic
grammar: Se is reciprocal in the selected personal transitive use: each returns the other's affection. It is not replacement se before a separate object clitic.
register: Neutral description of explicitly mutual romantic affection.
note: Estar enamorado = be in love; cartas cariñosas = affectionate letters. Both adults explicitly declare their feelings and write to one another.

sentence: Para sacar adelante la exposición, Ana propuso pedir prestadas dos mesas y Luis apoyó esa petición; después él propuso ampliar el horario y ella defendió su propuesta: se secundaron en esas dos iniciativas, aunque discrepan sobre el cartel.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb with a reciprocal direct-object clitic
grammar: Se is reciprocal: Luis backs Ana's initiative, and Ana backs Luis's. En esas dos iniciativas limits the mutual support to the stated actions.
register: Educated description of practical collaboration.
note: Iniciativas = proposed actions; ampliar el horario = extend opening hours; cartel = poster. Their support does not extend to agreement about the poster.

sentence: Ana y Julia son amigas y este mes se arroparon mutuamente: cuando Ana perdió su empleo, Julia la escuchó cada tarde, y cuando Julia recibió una crítica dura sobre su pintura, Ana la acompañó y la animó a seguir pintando.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb with a figurative reciprocal direct-object clitic
grammar: Se and mutuamente mark support in both directions. Arroparse figuratively means providing emotional shelter or support here, without any literal covering with clothing.
register: Warm account of support within an explicit friendship.
note: Crítica dura = harsh criticism; acompañar = keep someone company here. The sentence reports supportive acts without claiming complete recovery from either difficulty.

sentence: Después de que rechazaron su propuesta de exposición, Elena y Raúl se reconfortaron: ella le dijo «Tu trabajo merece otra oportunidad» y él le respondió «El tuyo también; podemos buscar otra sala», aunque ambos seguían decepcionados.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb with a reciprocal direct-object clitic
grammar: Reciprocal se links the reassurance Elena gives Raúl with the reassurance he gives her. Their continuing disappointment limits the emotional outcome.
register: Supportive exchange after an artistic setback.
note: Decepcionados = disappointed; sala = exhibition space here; el tuyo = your work. Both collaborators receive explicit reassurance.

sentence: Elena y Hugo comparten un departamento solo hasta diciembre; ella dice que le molesta el ruido de él y él dice que le incomoda la rigidez de ella, pero se toleran y cumplen los turnos de limpieza acordados.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative verb with a reciprocal personal direct-object clitic
grammar: Se represents the two people as each other's direct objects. Tolerarse here concerns enduring one another in a bounded living arrangement, rather than permitting a finite action.
register: Neutral account of strained shared living.
note: Departamento = apartment; rigidez = inflexibility; turnos de limpieza = cleaning turns. Their mutual complaints coexist with compliance with an agreed household routine.

sentence: En las cenas del club, Elena y Hugo se repelen: ella dice que siente rechazo hacia él y busca sentarse lejos, y él declara sentir el mismo rechazo y también evita su compañía; ambos mantienen un trato cortés.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative verb with a reciprocal personal direct-object clitic
grammar: Se gives repeler a reciprocal personal reading. Each person's explicit statement and avoidance support mutual aversion; no physical pushing or force is described.
register: Careful, neutral description of mutual social aversion.
note: Rechazo = aversion here; evitar su compañía = avoid the other's company; trato cortés = courteous interaction. The setting is limited to club dinners.

sentence: Lidia, de treinta años, y Omar, de treinta y dos, se cortejan: ella lo invita a cenar y él le lleva flores; ambos han dicho que quieren explorar una relación romántica, aunque todavía no se consideran pareja.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative verb with a reciprocal personal direct-object clitic
grammar: Se marks reciprocal courting. Both adults explicitly acknowledge romantic interest, so the invitations and flowers are interpreted within that stated intention.
register: Neutral description of mutually acknowledged romantic interest.
note: Explorar una relación romántica = explore a romantic relationship; considerarse pareja = regard themselves as a couple. Interest is mutual, while couple status remains unclaimed.

sentence: Al revisar el montaje de la exposición, Ana le echó en cara a Luis haber llegado tarde y él le reprochó a ella haber olvidado las etiquetas; se recriminaron esas dos fallas, pero después ambos reconocieron su error y retomaron el trabajo.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb with a reciprocal indirect-object clitic and an explicit direct object
